206.summary: Some finite lattices are not congruence lattices of any finite algebra, answering the finite lattice representation problem negatively. Moreover, no algorithm decides whether a finite lattice has such a representation, or whether it is a full subgroup interval of a finite group.

papers.title: Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability
A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem

207.explainer: The Bass conjecture says the trace of an idempotent matrix over a group ring only sees elements of finite order; for torsion-free groups it forces idempotents to be trivial (Kaplansky). For torsion-free groups this forces the trace of an idempotent to equal the rank of its augmentation, which yields the idempotent conjecture; the algebraic statement is checked in Lean (I did not examine the proof technique in detail).
207.caveats: Lean formalizes (b) (the algebraic companion): BassTrace.lean — OAI.BassTrace.RightProjective.bassTraceModules_vanishing_and_support at OAI/RingTheory/BassTrace/Main.lean:23 — and BassTorsionFree.lean (trace rank and char-0 Kaplansky idempotents). The family headline (ℓ¹-Bass, 207_0, Oct 5, analytic) is NOT formalized.
207.summary: Proves the ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for every discrete group: Hattori–Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over ℓ¹(G) are supported on finitely many finite-order conjugacy classes. The algebraic companion proves the integral Bass trace conjecture and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups over every commutative unital characteristic-zero domain.

papers.title: The ℓ¹-Bass Conjecture for Discrete Groups
The Bass trace conjecture and the characteristic-zero Kaplansky idempotent conjecture

208.explainer: Deligne's theorem says symmetric tensor categories in characteristic 0 are representations of supergroups; in characteristic p new 'incompressible' categories Ver_{p^n} appear, and BEO conjectured they are the only new targets. The proof builds a higher Frobenius functor from restricted tilting modules and selects an embedding by rank support.
208.caveats: Finite case only (moderate-growth general case not claimed). 26 pp. The Lean challenge DeligneDrinfeld.lean (OAI/Algebra/Drinfeld) is not listed for this family in lean/docs; I did not establish a link — treat as unformalized.
208.summary: Proves that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0 admits a k-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal fiber functor to a higher Verlinde category Ver_(pⁿ). The level may depend on the category, and the theorem includes characteristic two, resolving the finite case of the Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture.

papers.title: Fiber functors for finite symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic

209.explainer: Gersten's conjecture says K-theory of a regular local ring injects into K-theory of its fraction field (the start of the Gersten resolution). It is known whenever the ring contains a field. The counterexamples exploit ramification: a class that dies over the fraction field survives mod 5 on A[1/π].
209.caveats: Ramified only (π ∈ m²) and integral coefficients; the unramified mixed-characteristic case and finite-coefficient forms are untouched. The class is detected mod 5 after inverting π; its order is not determined. 35 pp. No Lean.
209.summary: Disproves unrestricted integral Gersten injectivity in degrees 3 and 5. Two explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic (0,5) have nonzero integral K-theory classes that vanish over their fraction fields.

papers.title: An integral counterexample to Gersten's conjecture
An integral degree-three Gersten counterexample

210.explainer: Foulkes conjectured a plethysm inequality: for a ≤ b, Sym^a(Sym^b V) embeds in Sym^b(Sym^a V). The natural Foulkes–Howe 'transpose the array' map is shown surjective once b ≥ a(a−1), which settles a = 6 for b ≥ 30 and with extra work for 6 ≤ b < 30.
210.caveats: Only a = 6 for Foulkes (not the full conjecture). Lean: FoulkesHowe.lean — OAI.Problem346.canonical_foulkes_howe_surjective at OAI/RepresentationTheory/FoulkesHowe/Stabilization.lean:15 — formalizes the quadratic stabilization (b ≥ a(a−1)) and the sixth-power case only for b ≥ 30; the full range b ≥ 6 is not formalized (lean/docs/210.md).
210.summary: Proves the sixth case of Foulkes’ conjecture: Sym ⁶(Sym ^bV) embeds equivariantly in Sym ^b(Sym ⁶V) for every b ≥ 6 and finite-dimensional complex V. More generally, the canonical multiplication map Sym ^b(Sym ^aV) → Sym ^a(Sym ^bV) is surjective for a ≥ 2 and b ≥ a(a-1), giving dimension-independent quadratic stabilization.

papers.title: Foulkes' conjecture for the sixth symmetric power
Quadratic stabilization of the canonical Foulkes--Howe map

211.explainer: Random planar maps are discrete random surfaces; physics predicts they converge to Liouville quantum gravity when decorated by critical FK clusters with q≤4, and collapse to trees when q>4. The family proves the whole picture for spherical FK maps, including the hardest piece (graph distances), and then shows random walk on them becomes Liouville Brownian motion.
211.caveats: 762 pages across 7 papers that cite each other, including a metric-measure companion revised 2026-10-03 that the spectral paper uses as an input; the spectral results are explicitly conditional on 'stated Brownian/LQG inputs'. Lean (docs/211.md, FKCRT) covers only the q>4 CRT limit — the least novel regime. Random-walk/spectral results only for q=2 and spanning-tree maps. No public expert reaction found.
211.summary: Critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres for 0 < q ≤ 4 and to the Brownian continuum random tree for q > 4, establishing the surface-to-tree geometric transition. For FK–Ising and spanning-tree-weighted maps, stationary random walks converge to Liouville Brownian motion on the limiting sphere. The FK–Ising spectral result also gives convergence of eigenvalues and heat traces, using the stated Brownian/LQG inputs.

papers.title: Random Walks on Critical FK–Ising Maps and Liouville Brownian Motion
Spectral convergence for critical FK–Ising planar maps
A Linear Clock for Random Walk on Tree-Weighted Planar Maps
Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps
The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4
Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps
Brownian continuum random tree limits of finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn maps above four

212.explainer: First-passage percolation puts random travel times on lattice edges; a bigeodesic would be a doubly infinite fastest route, and their absence is the FPP analogue of 'no bi-infinite ground states' in disordered systems. The proof uses Busemann functions along rays, confines rays in sectors, and shows via a label budget on horizontal lines and finite perturbations that any bigeodesic would yield a contradiction.
212.caveats: Moment condition E[min of 4]^2<∞ (the standard Cox–Durrett type condition). Lean (PlanarFirstPassage in yaml main_results; GammaPassage) formalizes the differentiability of the time constant for Gamma weights only; strict convexity and no-bigeodesics are not formalized. No public expert reaction found.
212.summary: Proves that planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite geodesic for iid nonnegative nonatomic edge weights when the minimum of four weights has finite second moment. For exponential weights, the limit shape is strictly convex with C¹ boundary. Differentiability also holds for every Gamma law with positive shape and rate.

papers.title: No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation
Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape

213.explainer: θ(p_c)=0 asks whether, exactly at the percolation threshold, an infinite cluster can exist; it is the central open problem of percolation theory in d=3. The finite mechanism is a 'gluing' inequality P(o↔A, o↔T) ≥ P(o↔A)·min_{a∈A} P(a↔T): reaching a relay set whose points all connect onward well gives a good chance to continue. If an infinite cluster existed at p_c, finitely many crossing estimates would persist slightly below p_c, and an adaptive exploration would build an infinite cluster below p_c — a contradiction.
213.caveats: Priority: the famous Z^3 case is not first here (Leder/Claude, Bou-Rabee); the OpenAI Z^3 paper is explicitly a 'self-contained cubic argument' with antecedent credit. What is new is the general quasi-transitive theorem (subexponential growth cases via relative-entropy search and a Tessera–Tointon structure theorem), which uses Hutchcroft's exponential-growth theorem as an input. Lean: CriticalZ3 (in yaml main_results) and CriticalPercolation challenges, standard axioms; statements look faithful. Bond only for the general graphs.
213.summary: Resolves the Benjamini–Schramm criticality conjecture for bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1: at the critical probability, there is almost surely no infinite cluster. The family also establishes this conclusion for both nearest-neighbor bond and site percolation on ℤ³.

papers.title: Critical bond and site percolation on the cubic lattice
No percolation at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs

214.explainer: On a tree-like (nonamenable) graph, percolation is expected to have an intermediate phase with infinitely many infinite clusters before they merge into one. The proof bounds the critical two-point operator on ℓ^2 directly (a weighted finite trace averaging the root), then shows the ℓ^2 threshold is strictly above p_c, which by known arguments gives non-uniqueness.
214.caveats: Lean challenge BenjaminiSchramm/CayleyPercolation with docs/214.md (standard axioms) but not in yaml main_results. 53 pages for a 30-year-old conjecture whose special cases each required substantial work. No public expert reaction found.
214.summary: Proves p_c < p_u for Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, resolving the Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture. Thus there is a nonempty range of probabilities with infinitely many infinite clusters. A stronger operator bound also establishes the critical triangle condition.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs

215.explainer: In 2D, spins on a sphere with n≥3 components were predicted (Polyakov) to have exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature — the lattice cousin of the mass gap in 4D Yang–Mills. The proof uses exact rotation (Ward) identities: a fourth derivative along two non-commuting rotation axes, summed over test functions, produces a nonnegative square that controls a boundary twist on an annulus; the remaining small quantity is a sign-cluster crossing probability, and n>3 reduces to n=3 by spherical disintegration.
215.caveats: The 20-page exponential-decay theorem is formalized (ClassicalON, in yaml main_results, standard axioms; the challenge statement looks faithful: finite subgraphs, free boundary, uniform A,m). The O(3) continuum limit (122+26 pp.) and the O(4) asymptotics (109+102 pp.) are not formalized; the O(4) 'sharp bounds' paper notes a continuum spectral interpretation needs separate convergence hypotheses. The family title leads with the continuum limit, but the formally checked landmark is the decay theorem. No public expert reaction found.
215.summary: Constructs the canonical continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor O(3) model: a non-Gaussian local relativistic theory with a unique vacuum and a positive mass gap. For the square-lattice O(4) model, determines the exact leading asymptotic of the full transfer gap, m_(lat)(β) ∼ 32e^(π/4-1/2)√β e^(-πβ). The family also proves exponential spin-correlation decay for two-dimensional nearest-neighbor O(n) models with n ≥ 3 at every positive temperature.

papers.title: The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model
An Isolated Particle Pole for the Two-Dimensional O(3) Spin Field
Exact mass asymptotics for the two-dimensional O(4) lattice model
Sharp mass bounds for the two-dimensional O(4) model
Exponential decay in two-dimensional classical O(n) models

216.explainer: The XY model (planar spins) has a topological phase transition driven by vortex unbinding, predicted with very specific fine structure: a logarithmic correction at criticality and a correlation length diverging like exp(c/√(β_c-β)). The family proves these fine details via the dual integer-height model and its Gaussian scaling limit.
216.caveats: 461 pages, 6 papers; the center-magnetization and spin-field papers are explicitly conditional on 'critical-height, local-renormalization and spin-field inputs from the companion papers'. Results are for the specific cosine nearest-neighbor model and free-box limits taken in a specified order. No Lean docs for 216. No public expert reaction found.
216.summary: For the square-lattice nearest-neighbor cosine XY model, proves critical axis correlations C_(β_c)(r) ∼ Ar^(-1/4)(log r)^(1/8) and the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity √(β_c-β)logξ(β) → B, with A,B > 0 after the free-box thermodynamic limit. For finite square-symmetric interactions containing nearest neighbors, discrete Gaussian heights converge to Gaussian fields throughout the rough phase, including its threshold, along geometric torus sizes. Critical center-magnetization and spin-field conclusions retain their stated height, renormalization, and field-input assumptions.

papers.title: The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model
Critical Center Magnetization in the Planar XY Model
The Critical Spin Field of the Planar XY Model
Essential Singularity of the Correlation Length in the Planar XY Model
The critical correlation exponent of the planar XY model
BKT universality for height and planar spin fields

217.explainer: The SK model is the canonical mean-field spin glass; its free energy is known (Parisi formula, Talagrand), but sample-to-sample fluctuations at low temperature were only predicted by physicists to scale as n^{1/6}. The papers prove the exponent and a limit law via comparisons on a hierarchy of cavity/projection estimates (one-site comparison, profile rigidity).
217.caveats: No formalization; limiting law 'uniquely characterized' but not explicit (not identified with a known distribution). Zero-field Gaussian couplings only. 126+80 pages. No public expert reaction found.
217.summary: For every fixed inverse temperature β > 1, determines the fluctuation scale and limiting law of the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick log partition function. Its variance is asymptotic to c_β n^(1/3), with c_β > 0, confirming the predicted n^(1/6) standard-deviation scale. Exact centering and standardization give full-sequence convergence to a uniquely characterized nondegenerate law.

papers.title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free-energy limiting law
The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale

218.explainer: Universality says microscopic details should not change critical behaviour; for Ising this was known only for exactly solvable (nearest-neighbor, isoradial) cases or for energy correlations. The family pushes conformal invariance of spins and interfaces to weakly interacting and weakly disordered models using comparison of conditional laws across bands.
218.caveats: Perturbative (sufficiently weak) only. The log-fluctuation paper is conditional on 'stated deterministic critical-reference estimates'. Lean (BufferedIsing, docs/218.md) covers only a finite-graph comparison lemma. No public expert reaction found.
218.summary: Weak finite-range square-symmetric even multispin perturbations of the square-lattice Ising model preserve critical bulk spin and energy limits; weak square-symmetric contour interactions also yield chordal SLE₃ interface limits. With sufficiently weak iid bond disorder of any fixed bounded nondegenerate mean-zero law, critical spin interfaces converge to the same law in probability over environments.

papers.title: Quenched SLE₃ limits for general weak random-bond Ising models
Quenched SLE₃ Universality for the Weak Random-Bond Ising Model
Logarithmic Relative Fluctuations in the Weakly Disordered Planar Ising Model
Conformal universality of bulk Ising correlations under weak interactions
SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions
Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising

219.explainer: Even though a random 3-regular graph looks locally like a tree, its eigenvalue spacings were conjectured to follow the same GOE statistics as a dense Gaussian matrix. The result proves this for every fixed degree, the long-missing sparse end of random-matrix universality.
219.caveats: Laplace-functional (fixed-energy) formulation; disorder part needs disorder strength small depending on d and distance from edges. No Lean docs. No public expert reaction found.
219.summary: For every fixed degree d ≥ 3, the bulk adjacency-eigenvalue point process of a uniform simple random d-regular graph converges to the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble law, including for cubic graphs. The same fixed-energy universality persists under sufficiently weak fixed iid uniform diagonal disorder, throughout compact bands strictly inside the clean spectral edges.

papers.title: Fixed-energy universality for weak Anderson disorder on random regular graphs
GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs

220.explainer: A random walk whose transition probabilities are random but fixed (a 'random environment') can escape in a direction yet move sublinearly, as in 1D. The conjecture said that in d≥2 escape forces positive speed; the proof controls regeneration times (moments where the walk never returns below a height record) so their durations have finite mean.
220.caveats: Ballisticity is in formalization.yaml main_results (DirectionalBallisticity, standard axioms); DirectionalWalk and VelocityHemisphere challenges also exist. Strong verification signal. Strict ellipticity 0–1 law requires d≥3. No public expert reaction found.
220.summary: On ℤᵈ, d ≥ 3, directional escape has probability zero or one for iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environments, and for stationary ergodic finite-range-dependent environments under uniform ellipticity. In iid uniformly elliptic environments with d ≥ 2, almost-sure directional transience implies a deterministic limiting velocity with positive projection in that direction, resolving the ballisticity conjecture.

papers.title: A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments
A directional zero–one law under strict ellipticity
Directional transience implies ballisticity

221.explainer: In a sparse random spin glass each spin sees finitely many neighbours, and physicists describe its free energy via a hierarchy of laws of 'cavity messages' (Parisi's replica symmetry breaking for sparse graphs). The upper bound by interpolation was known; the proof gets the lower bound by adding small marked Poisson perturbations that force identities among multi-replica spin patterns, shifting every branching depth of a target replica tree by one level so errors average out, and then comparing a cavity insertion with independent hierarchical messages.
221.caveats: Restricted to the PT class: even arity, Poisson (not fixed-degree/random regular) graphs, positivity condition E[(-b)^n]≥0 — excludes odd-K SAT, hard constraints, Bethe lattice proper. OpenAI's own prompt (reasoning trace) posed exactly this class. Lean challenge DilutedSpin.lean (theorem mezard_parisi, standard axioms) with docs/221.md; not in yaml main_results. One of 10 families with a released reasoning summary. 36 pages. No public expert reaction found.
221.summary: Proves the Mézard–Parisi hierarchical cavity formula for Poisson-diluted even-arity Ising models satisfying the Panchenko–Talagrand factorization and positivity assumptions, with only first-moment integrability. The limiting free energy equals the infimum over finite-depth hierarchical trial laws. This includes the Viana–Bray model, symmetric diluted even-spin models, and weighted soft even-K satisfiability.

papers.title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses

222.explainer: The perceptron is the simplest neural-network capacity problem and a mean-field model of jamming. The family proves the Gardner-type variational formulas at positive temperature and, remarkably, the microscopic jamming exponents predicted by full-RSB physics for the negative-margin spherical perceptron.
222.caveats: Positive temperature only for (1)-(3); zero-temperature Ising capacity not claimed here. Jamming result uses an order of limits and a computer-assisted numerical certificate; holds also for a specific Gaussian mixture. Lean: spherical perceptron pressure formula formalized; Ising part only finiteness of the variational value. No public expert reaction found.
222.summary: Determines finite-temperature variational free energies for Gaussian Ising perceptrons with bounded Borel log-potentials and Gaussian spherical perceptrons with bounded continuous potentials, at every positive pattern density. A spherical extension treats bi-orthogonally invariant disorder with compact limiting singular-value distributions and no outliers. At margin −1, the quadratic-penalty spherical model has a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws, with system size, zero temperature, and critical density taken in that order.

papers.title: The free energy of the Ising random perceptron
Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron
The spherical perceptron with bi-orthogonally invariant disorder
The free energy of the spherical random perceptron

223.explainer: Smirnov's breakthrough worked only on special lattices with an exact discrete-holomorphic observable. The family claims conformal invariance for the square-lattice random-cluster model across the whole continuous-transition range, via finite connection comparisons and a boundary observable that determines the Loewner driving function.
223.caveats: 602 pages, unformalized. Cardy's formula for Z^2 bond percolation and FK conformal invariance for all q∈[1,4] would be among the biggest results in 2D statistical mechanics; scrutiny needed. q<1 only in smooth domains. Overlaps internally (two papers both claim 1≤q≤4 and Cardy). No public expert reaction found.
223.summary: Proves chordal SLE_κ limits for critical square-lattice random-cluster interfaces for 0 < q ≤ 4, with κ=4π/arccos (-√q/2): bounded Jordan domains are allowed for q ≥ 1, and smooth Jordan domains for q < 1, under the stated marked-boundary approximations. For 1 ≤ q ≤ 4, complete nested plane loops converge to CLE_κ.

papers.title: Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4
Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one
Quenched SLE Universality for Weakly Disordered FK–Ising Interfaces
Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE
Natural Occupation Measures for Critical Square-Lattice FK Interfaces
Conformal Limits of Critical Square-Lattice Random-Cluster Interfaces

224.explainer: Cardy's formula, known only for triangular-lattice site percolation, should hold for any 2D percolation; Voronoi percolation is the canonical isotropic random-lattice test case. The family proves it (annealed) and then lifts it to near-critical universality.
224.caveats: Annealed (averaged over the tessellation) Cardy, not quenched; two of three papers take Cardy as an input. No Lean. No public expert reaction found.
224.summary: Proves Cardy's formula for annealed critical Poisson–Voronoi crossing probabilities in every bounded Jordan quadrilateral. With each model normalized by its own expected unit-square pivotal count, the conditional joint near-critical crossing-threshold laws for rational polygonal quads converge in environment probability to the triangular-lattice reference law. This establishes quenched near-critical universality for crossing thresholds.

papers.title: From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation
A Pivotal Amplitude for Voronoi Percolation from Cardy's Formula
Cardy’s formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation

225.explainer: The six-vertex (ice) model has a height function expected to look like a Gaussian free field with a coupling constant fixed by Bethe ansatz; this was proved only at or near the free-fermion point. The result gives the full critical range with the predicted variance 1/arcsin(c/2).
225.caveats: Single 93-page paper, plane state from balanced tori (not arbitrary domains/boundary conditions). No Lean. No public expert reaction found.
225.summary: The balanced square-lattice six-vertex height field with a=b=1 and 0 < c ≤ 2 converges to a Gaussian free field, including at the endpoint c = 2. The plane state is defined by balanced-torus limits. For unit height increments and Green kernel -(2π)⁻¹log|x-y|, the exact variance multiplier is 1/arcsin (c/2).

papers.title: The Gaussian free field limit of the balanced six-vertex model with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2)

226.explainer: Overlaying two random domino tilings produces loops that should look like CLE_4, the loop ensemble tied to GFF level lines. Earlier work identified which punctures loops surround; this paper controls thin excursions and retraced pieces so the loops themselves converge.
226.caveats: Half-plane Temperleyan geometry only; builds on Dubédat and Basok–Chelkak's topological convergence and upgrades to curve convergence. 33 pages. No Lean. No public expert reaction found.
226.summary: Resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer scaling-limit conjecture: the complete loop ensemble formed by two independent dimer coverings of the Temperleyan square lattice converges to nested CLE₄. Convergence matches every macroscopic loop as an unparametrized curve, upgrading convergence of loop observables to convergence of the loops themselves.

papers.title: The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers

227.explainer: Glauber dynamics is the standard MCMC sampler for spin glasses; whether it mixes fast throughout the high-temperature phase β<1 was a central question in sampling theory. The family proves fast mixing (with cutoff) up to β=1, pins the critical slowdown at n^{2/3}, and proves exponential-type slowdown below the transition.
227.caveats: Lean (docs/227.md) covers: the β<1 Poincaré inequality; ratio cutoff only for β<1/2 (paper claims β<1 with explicit location); critical mixing between n^{2/3-ε} and e^{εn} (weaker than the paper's n^{2/3+o(1)}); the covariance n^{2/3} bounds; the β>1 stretched-exponential obstruction. The universal autocorrelation limits are unformalized. 720 pages in 8 papers. No public expert reaction found.
227.summary: For zero-field Gaussian SK heat-bath dynamics with rate-one updates per spin, proves worst-start cutoff on the log n scale for fixed 0 ≤ β < 1, mixing time n^(2/3+o(1)) at β = 1, and stretched-exponential mixing from a Gibbs-sampled fixed starting configuration for β > 1, in probability over disorder. At criticality, rescaled stationary and quench autocorrelation processes have universal random limits for Gaussian and Rademacher disorder; the quench limit relaxes to the stationary limit.

papers.title: Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
Functional universality of critical SK autocorrelations
A spectral gap throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase
Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase
Critical slowing down in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
Stretched-exponential barriers for typical SK initial states
A typical-start upper bound for low-temperature SK Glauber dynamics
Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

228.explainer: Proving that any realistic continuum gas has a phase transition is a famous open problem; lattice models are much easier. This family designs a radial pair potential where a packing structure forces a kink in the free energy at one temperature — an existence proof of the phenomenon, not a proof for natural potentials.
228.caveats: The potentials are engineered for the proof (not Lennard-Jones or physically motivated), and the transition is a temperature singularity at fixed density in the canonical ensemble, not liquid–gas coexistence or crystallization. Both theorems formalized (ContinuumTransition, RadialTransition in yaml main_results; RadialDensityInterval), standard axioms. No public expert reaction found.
228.summary: Constructs stable distance-dependent pair interactions for three-dimensional classical particles with a first-order phase transition: the canonical free energy has a derivative jump at one inverse temperature throughout an open density interval. One potential has a divergent repulsive core; another is bounded and continuous with an integrable power-law tail, realizing the type of transition sought in Simon's continuum problem.

papers.title: A continuum temperature singularity for a radial pair potential
A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay

229.explainer: Broadcasting a colour down a tree with noise, can you guess the root from the leaves? Above the Kesten–Stigum bound you always can; the question is whether that bound is exact. For 3 and 4 colours (ferromagnetic) the answer is yes in every degree, which pins the community-detection threshold for 3-community block models.
229.caveats: The 4-state proof uses 'reproducible exact-arithmetic verification of polynomial inequalities' (computer-assisted). Lean formalizes only the supercritical direction (reconstruction above KS), which is the classical easy direction (Kesten–Stigum); the new nonreconstruction-at-threshold is not formalized. SBM consequence combines with known tree-to-graph and algorithmic results.
229.summary: Proves the exact reconstruction threshold dλ² > 1, with nonreconstruction at equality, for three-state symmetric and four-state ferromagnetic broadcasting on regular trees (d ≥ 2) and observed Poisson trees (mean d > 1 and d > 0, respectively), with Poisson advantage averaged without conditioning on survival. The three-state theorem allows both signs of λ and gives the exact weak-recovery threshold for the symmetric three-community stochastic block model.

papers.title: The Reconstruction Threshold for the Ferromagnetic Four-State Potts Model
A Capacity Criterion for Four-State Potts Reconstruction on Trees
The exact reconstruction threshold for the three-state symmetric channel

230.explainer: SLE curves are fractal with dimension 1+κ/8; the natural question is which exact gauge function makes their Hausdorff measure a nontrivial length. The answer has an iterated-logarithm correction with exponent (2-d)/2, analogous to the classical Brownian-path gauge.
230.caveats: Lean (SLELowerPositivity) only proves the positivity half; finiteness not formalized. Answers Schramm's question with a different exponent than he suggested. No public expert reaction found.
230.summary: Resolves Schramm’s Hausdorff-measure question for chordal SLE_κ, 0 < κ < 8. The explicit gauge rᵈ(loglog (1/r))^((2-d)/2), d=1+κ/8, gives almost surely positive finite measure to every trace segment γ([s,t]) with 0 < s < t < ∞, and finite expected measure to the trace in every bounded disk.

papers.title: An exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE
An explicit exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE

231.explainer: A 'factor of IID' is a process built by a local-ish deterministic rule from independent coin flips at each vertex — the measurable analogue of a parallel algorithm. Showing the free spanning forest is one, even on nonamenable groups, answers Lyons's question and covers all strongly Rayleigh invariant processes.
231.caveats: Lean (FreeUniformSpanningForest, StronglyRayleighDPP challenges, docs/231.md) covers both claims; not in yaml main_results. 19 pages. Factor of IID, not finitary. No public expert reaction found.
231.summary: On every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph, the free uniform spanning forest is a factor of independent vertex labels, by one isomorphism-equivariant rule using no root. Translation-invariant strongly Rayleigh binary processes on every countable group, including invariant determinantal processes with Hermitian positive-contraction kernels, are also factors of IID.

papers.title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID

232.explainer: Random Lipschitz height functions (neighbouring heights differ by at most one) are natural random surfaces expected to look like the Gaussian free field; Schramm asked for this and for SLE_4 level lines. The proofs use reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule and Gaussian moment identities.
232.caveats: Interface result for the integer model (the SLE_4 half of Problem 2.2) is not claimed; only the field part. Tuned boundary amplitude for real heights is implicit. No Lean. No public expert reaction found.
232.summary: Proves Gaussian free field limits on bounded smooth simply connected domains for triangular-lattice height models: uniform odd heights with increments 0,±2 and two-arc boundary values ±1, and zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by fixed x ∈ [1/√2,1]. Uniform real Lipschitz heights also converge to a Gaussian field; at a tuned opposite-boundary amplitude, their interface converges to chordal SLE₄, establishing Schramm’s real-field/interface predictions.

papers.title: Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights
The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data
Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice

233.explainer: The Ashkin–Teller model couples two Ising models; along its critical line it is described by a Gaussian free field. The paper identifies the joint scaling limit of its height function and current clusters as canonical GFF level-set structures.
233.caveats: Single 100-page paper; recent conjecture with a narrow audience. No Lean. No public expert reaction found.
233.summary: Identifies the joint scaling limit of Ashkin–Teller heights and both complete current-cluster collections throughout the critical line, including the four-state Potts endpoint. In bounded Jordan domains with admissible lattice approximations and wired primal/free dual boundaries, the height converges to the predicted Gaussian free field, and the clusters to canonical recursive sets of that same field, retaining every nesting depth.

papers.title: The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents

234.explainer: Most rigorous spin-glass theory needs independent Gaussian couplings; orthogonally invariant models (rotation-invariant coupling matrices with arbitrary spectrum) break that and were only solved at high temperature. The paper gives the free energy at every temperature.
234.caveats: Lean challenge InvariantIsing (Unconditional module, 495-line statement file) with docs/234.md; not in yaml main_results. I did not check the variational formula against the physics (Parisi–Potters) predictions. No public expert reaction found.
234.summary: Gives an exact variational formula for the limiting pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses at every fixed temperature, both almost surely and in expectation. The coupling matrix is a Haar-random rotation of a deterministic spectrum converging to a compactly supported law, with extreme eigenvalues converging to its support edges. The zero-field ground-state energy follows as temperature tends to zero.

papers.title: All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses

235.explainer: The satisfiability threshold conjecture says random k-SAT flips from almost surely satisfiable to unsatisfiable at a fixed clause density; Friedgut showed a sharp threshold that might wobble with n. The alternative proof shows concentration of the last satisfiable index and compares system sizes; computability comes from certificates on both sides that a fair search can enumerate.
235.caveats: OpenAI explicitly credits Carenini with priority for threshold existence; this family is an alternative proof plus new variance and computability results. Lean: threshold existence (FixedClauseThreshold), variance with O(n log n) upper bound at k=3 (the Θ(n) k=3 sharpening is a separate paper; SATSharpness supplements), and computability (SATComputability) all have challenges; not in yaml main_results. No value of the 3-SAT threshold is computed. No public expert reaction to the OpenAI papers found.
235.summary: For random k-SAT with independent uniformly signed proper clauses sampled with replacement, proves finite positive limiting thresholds and hitting-time variance Θₖ(n) for every fixed k ≥ 3, and computability of the 3-SAT threshold. We credit Gaia Carenini with priority for resolving the threshold-existence conjecture in her concurrent ECCC TR26-229, made public October 5, 2026; this family supplies another proof and the sharper variance and computability results.

papers.title: A Limiting Satisfiability Threshold for Every Fixed Clause Size
Linear Variance of the Random 3-SAT Hitting Time
Variance of the Random k-SAT Hitting Time
Computing the Random 3-SAT Threshold

236.explainer: On a regular tree the free Ising state is a factor of IID exactly up to the reconstruction (Kesten–Stigum) threshold; past it, the root's information about distant spins rules out any IID construction. The positive direction, including the critical point, is the new part.
236.caveats: In yaml main_results (FreeIsing, OAI.Problem367.free_ising_factor_iff_threshold, standard axioms) — strong signal. Ferromagnetic case only. Finitary coding not covered. No public expert reaction found.
236.summary: Determines when the free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising state on the infinite d-regular tree is a factor of independent vertex labels: exactly when tanhβ ≤ (d-1)^(-1/2), including equality, for d ≥ 3 and β ≥ 0. The construction uses no root and is almost surely equivariant for each fixed tree automorphism, resolving the ferromagnetic case of Lyons's question.

papers.title: The sharp factor-of-IID threshold for the free Ising model on regular trees

237.explainer: A self-avoiding walk is a random path that never revisits a site; physicists have long believed its end-to-end distance in 2D scales as n^{3/4}. Building on Duminil-Copin–Smirnov's honeycomb observable, the family derives sharp strip and cylinder partition-function exponents and transfers them to fixed-length walks.
237.caveats: 1067 pages in 13 papers, the largest family in the group; the diameter result is the 'o(1)' exponent form on the honeycomb lattice only (not Z^2, not the scaling limit SLE_{8/3}). Lean formalizes only supporting summability statements, the free energy, and the strip-crossing mass ≍ N^{-1/4}; the 3/4 law itself is not formalized. Some statements hold only on density-one sets of lengths. No public expert reaction found.
237.summary: Proves the diameter form of Nienhuis's predicted three-quarter exponent: a uniformly chosen n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter n^(3/4+o(1)). Its local mass and covering numbers have exponent 4/3. These estimates hold at every sufficiently large fixed length, simultaneously across scales, with arbitrarily high polynomial probability.

papers.title: Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks
Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints
Cylinder loop weights and planar nesting
Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length honeycomb walks
Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice
Cylinder amplitudes and logarithmic bridge-length windows on the honeycomb lattice
Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds
Disk transfer representations and confined bridge mass
Polynomial vacuum representations and bridge mass for honeycomb walks
Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks
Critical strip-crossing mass on the honeycomb lattice
Uniform marked-polygon estimates and sharp finite bridge moments
Cap-selected amplitudes and triangle chords for honeycomb walks

238.explainer: The Thorp shuffle cuts the deck and, for each pair of cards at matching positions, flips a coin for their order; it is used in format-preserving encryption, where how many rounds are needed for a truly random permutation matters. After d shuffles each single card is uniform, but the joint law was only known to mix in O(d^3); the family shows O(d) suffices, by showing partial-permutation information (7/8 of the labels uniform on average) transfers to Fourier bounds for the full law.
238.caveats: Power-of-two decks only. Lean main_results include ThorpRouting (OAI.ThorpNine.main), BinarySweep, CoordinateSweeps (conditional_main), ThorpWeightedCompatibility; docs/238.md: the formalized full-deck bound uses 16,040,400·d steps, not 1600d. 683 pages over 12 papers giving many alternative proofs. No public expert reaction found.
238.summary: Proves that the Thorp shuffle randomizes N=2ᵈ labeled cards in Θ(log N) physical shuffles, settling its optimal mixing order for power-of-two deck sizes. Convergence is in total variation from the worst initial ordering and concerns the entire permutation, not just individual card positions.

papers.title: Optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle
Random coordinate frames and partial permutation laws
From partial permutation information to Fourier bounds
Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps
Conditional permutations in a revealed switching environment
Routing densities and representation contraction for Thorp sweeps
Row–column symmetry and contraction of coordinate sweeps
Random-subspace tests and trace smoothing for coordinate sweeps
Compatibility entropy and the spectrum of a Thorp sweep
Signed tensor densities and diagram budgets for the Thorp shuffle
Conditional coordinate sweeps and analytic transfer
A strict four-row permanent inequality and permutation moments

239.explainer: How likely is a random symmetric ±1 matrix to be singular? The obvious way is two identical rows, probability about 2^{-n}; the conjecture was that nothing else contributes at exponential scale. Following Tikhomirov's resolution for non-symmetric matrices, this proves the symmetric analogue, where row dependence makes inverse Littlewood–Offord arguments much harder.
239.caveats: Unformalized; no Lean docs. Plausibility: the unbiased constant 1/2 matches the natural lower bound from two equal rows/columns (probability ~2^{-n}). No public expert reaction found.
239.summary: Determines the sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices with independent entries on and above the diagonal. Uniform signs give Pr (det Aₙ=0)=(1/2+o(1))ⁿ; for fixed bias p ∈ (0,1)∖{1/2}, the rate is (p²+(1-p)²+o(1))ⁿ. In the biased case, agreeing rows attain this rate.

papers.title: The sharp exponential rate of singularity for symmetric Bernoulli matrices
The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices

240.explainer: Morley's theorem says a countable first-order theory with exactly one model (up to isomorphism) in one uncountable size has exactly one in every uncountable size. Shelah conjectured the same eventually holds for abstract elementary classes, a framework that covers infinitary logics where compactness fails. The claim proves it in ZFC with a uniform threshold, by building a minimal type and a geometry on it inside sufficiently large models and transferring categoricity up.
240.caveats: The landmark claim is the unformalized one. 121 pages of AEC theory, a field where several announced proofs have needed long correction cycles. The formalized CH obstruction refutes a specific threshold, which is a much smaller statement.
240.lean: partial formalization: only the CH obstruction (b) is formalized (CHObstruction.main). The ZFC eventual-categoricity theorem (a), the 121-page main paper, is NOT formalized.
240.summary: Proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC: for each bound on the Löwenheim–Skolem number, a uniform threshold makes categoricity of an abstract elementary class in one cardinal above that threshold imply categoricity throughout the same tail. Categoricity means uniqueness up to isomorphism at a given cardinality. Under the continuum hypothesis, a proposed specific Hanf threshold need not suffice.

papers.title: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold
Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes

241.explainer: The Turing degrees order information content: A <= B if B can compute A. The rigidity question asks whether this order has any symmetry other than the identity. Slaman and Woodin showed any symmetry is induced by a fairly explicit (arithmetic) map on reals and fixes everything above 0''. The claim finishes with a Baire-category trick: from four values of such a map at affine combinations of a real t and two generic reals, one can recover t, which forces the automorphism to fix every degree.
241.caveats: The paper itself is only 10 pages because it takes as an external input the Slaman-Woodin theorem that every automorphism is induced by an arithmetic (Borel) function on reals, cited from an unpublished 2005 manuscript. If the Lean formalization really derives that input (its directory structure suggests so; I did not audit it), the formal check is much stronger than the paper. Statement uses Mathlib's TuringReducible, so it is faithful.
241.lean: main theorem formalized (DegreeRigidity: TuringRigidity.ManuscriptMain.rigidity, stated with Mathlib's TuringReducible on N -> Bool oracles; every order isomorphism Degree ~o Degree is the identity). The extra representation corollaries are not formalized.
241.summary: Every order automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity, resolving their rigidity problem. Thus no nontrivial relabeling of degrees preserves the ordering by relative computability.

papers.title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees

242.explainer: Matiyasevich showed every computably enumerable set is the set of parameters for which some polynomial equation has a solution. Those encodings usually have many solutions per parameter; unique solutions would mean Hilbert's tenth problem stays undecidable even when you are promised a unique solution, with consequences for counting and complexity. The key is a single-fold Diophantine definition of exponentiation, here via multiples of a point on a rank-one elliptic curve whose height grows quadratically in the index with bounded error.
242.caveats: 27 pages. Uses a rank-one elliptic curve and Neron-Tate height to get a single-fold growth relation replacing Pell-equation exponentiation. Constants exist but are not specified numerically.
242.lean: main theorem formalized (SingleFold.main); the promise-undecidability consequence not separately formalized.
242.summary: Every recursively enumerable set of tuples of natural numbers has a Diophantine representation with exactly one auxiliary solution for each member and none for nonmembers. This proves the single-fold conjecture and hence the finite-fold conjecture. Diophantine solvability over the nonnegative integers remains undecidable even with an at-most-one-solution promise.

papers.title: Single-fold Diophantine representations

243.explainer: Is there a logic that expresses exactly the polynomial-time properties of unordered structures? CPT was the leading candidate: it computes with sets symmetric under all automorphisms and can count. The claim exhibits a polynomial-time solvable linear-algebra problem over F_3 on grid-like structures whose symmetric hereditarily finite sets are too sparse for CPT to solve it, settling the Blass-Gurevich-Shelah conjecture.
243.caveats: The separation is unconditional and does not separate P from NP or settle whether some other logic captures PTIME (Gurevich's question). The formal statement defines CPT inside Lean; faithfulness depends on that encoding (interpretation-program formulation) matching the standard one, which the paper argues.
243.summary: Confirms the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah noncapture conjecture: consistency of a linear system over 𝔽₃ defines a polynomial-time query on unordered finite structures that choiceless polynomial time with counting cannot express. A separate result shows that adding witnessed symmetric choice strictly increases expressive power. Both separations hold for the full counting formalism, allowing hereditarily finite sets of arbitrary finite rank.

papers.title: Choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture polynomial time
Witnessed symmetric choice is strictly stronger than choiceless polynomial time with counting

244.explainer: Choice implies that a surjection can be reversed by an injection; the question since 1902 is whether this weaker cardinal comparison already implies choice. The claim builds a symmetric forcing model from a 'monoid of diagrams' where every partition injects back into its set, yet some family has no choice function.
244.caveats: The formalized consistency statement requires formalizing syntax, ZF and forcing/symmetric extensions in Lean, so faithfulness of those encodings matters; the second Lean target assumes a ground model with an internal inaccessible cardinal (the paper's Theorem 1.2 does not).
244.lean: main theorem formalized (PartitionConsistency.main_consistency: Con(ZF) -> Con(ZF + PP + AC_WO + not AC); PartitionPrinciple: transitive-model construction from an internal-inaccessible ground). Stronger transitive-model preservation claims outside Lean.
244.summary: Assuming ZF is consistent, constructs a model in which every surjective image of a set injects into that set, yet the axiom of choice fails. Choice for ordinal-indexed families still holds. From any countable transitive model of ZFC, a separate construction gives a transitive symmetric extension with these properties and no new countable sequences of ground-model elements.

papers.title: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice

245.explainer: In typed lambda calculi, 'weakly normalizing' means some evaluation order terminates, 'strongly' that every order does. Many proofs show WN easily but SN is what proof assistants need. BGK conjectured that for any pure type system WN implies SN. The claim proves it with a diagonal argument coded in a typed calculus, showing a forbidden infinite-reduction configuration would let one build a non-normalizing legal term.
245.caveats: 72 pages. Formal statement defines PTS syntax inside Lean; faithful as far as the doc describes (full annotated syntax, arbitrary specifications).
245.summary: Proves that weak normalization implies strong normalization for every pure type system: if every legal expression in every valid context has a β-normal form, every β-reduction sequence terminates. This resolves the β-Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture, including nonfunctional rules and open contexts.

papers.title: Weak and strong normalization in pure type systems

246.explainer: A hyperbolic group's boundary at infinity is a topological space; for fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds it is the 2-sphere. Cannon conjectured the converse: if the boundary is S^2 the group is (virtually) such a 3-manifold group. The standard route is to show the boundary is quasisymmetric to the round sphere, which reduces to a uniform bound on how 'thick' curve families are at every scale (combinatorial modulus); the claim proves that bound directly from hyperbolicity and the sphere topology.
246.caveats: 31-page analytic proof: reduces via Bourdon-Kleiner's modulus criterion to a uniform bound on combinatorial 2-modulus and proves it by contradiction in two growth cases (exponential records vs a probability flow), then Sullivan-Tukia straightening. If both the paper and the Lean hold up, this resolves the main open problem in geometric group theory's 3-dimensional program. Review status unchecked; I did not build the Lean.
246.lean: main theorem formalized (CannonGeometricAction: CannonRelease.cannon). I read the target: hyperbolicity = uniformly thin geodesic triangles in a Cayley graph of a finite symmetric generating set; boundary = based geodesic rays modulo bounded synchronous distance with the quotient of the pointwise topology.
246.summary: Every word-hyperbolic group with boundary homeomorphic to S² admits a proper cocompact isometric action on hyperbolic three-space with finite kernel, proving Cannon's conjecture. Every torsion-free such group is therefore the fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic three-manifold.

papers.title: A Modulus Proof of Cannon’s Conjecture

247.explainer: Burnside asked whether a finitely generated group where every element has finite order must be finite; Golod showed no. The finitely presented version (finitely many relations, not just generators) stayed open because known constructions need infinitely many relations. The claim builds a finitely presented algebra R over F_2 whose Steinberg group is periodic yet infinite, transferring nilness of a graded algebra to periodicity of the group.
247.caveats: The family title leads with the residually finite 2-group, which is the unformalized companion (25 pages); the formalized part is the periodic group itself. Element orders are unbounded (no common exponent), as expected.
247.lean: partial formalization: the infinite finitely presented periodic group (PeriodicGroup: SourceBurnside.thm_main, with a Steinberg-group witness) is formalized; residual finiteness / the 2-group statement in the family headline and the nil-algebra conclusions are NOT formalized.
247.summary: Constructs an infinite finitely presented residually finite group whose elements all have finite 2-power order, answering the finitely presented Burnside problem negatively even in this class. The construction also yields an infinite-dimensional finitely presented nil associative 𝔽₂-algebra and a finitely presented infinite-dimensional algebraic unitization, giving negative answers to the corresponding nilpotence and Kurosh finiteness questions.

papers.title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group
An infinite finitely presented periodic group

248.explainer: Amenable groups admit an averaging operator invariant under translation; groups with free subgroups do not. F has no free subgroups yet resisted every attempt to decide. The claimed proof assumes Følner sets exist and builds a coloring of dyadic partitions by a Lipschitz map f on a Hilbert ball with no approximate fixed point; F-invariance of averages makes the mean colour almost fixed by f, a contradiction.
248.caveats: 13 pages, astonishingly short for a 60-year-old problem with a history of failed claims. The proof is elementary in outline: a fixed-point-free Lipschitz self-map of a Hilbert ball (Benyamini-Sternfeld) plus a recursive colouring of dyadic partitions; F's ability to move any separated pair of dyadic intervals to any other makes averaged correlations nearly constant, forcing an approximate fixed point.
248.lean: main theorem formalized (ThompsonNonamenability.thompson_F_nonamenable_composition). I read the target: F is defined as strictly monotone homeomorphisms of [0,1] with finitely many dyadic breakpoints and slopes 2^k.
248.summary: Proves that Thompson's group F, the group of dyadic piecewise linear homeomorphisms of the interval, is nonamenable, resolving its longstanding amenability problem.

papers.title: Thompson's group F is nonamenable

249.explainer: Cohomological dimension (algebra) and geometric dimension (smallest aspherical complex) agree except possibly in dimension 2. Bestvina and Brady built groups that break either this or Whitehead's conjecture without knowing which. The claim computes enough of the homotopy theory of one such kernel to show it has no 2-dimensional classifying space.
249.caveats: 25 pages. Since Bestvina-Brady showed one of Eilenberg-Ganea and Whitehead fails for these groups, this result says Eilenberg-Ganea is the one that fails; it does not settle the Whitehead conjecture. The group is finitely generated but not finitely presented, so the conjecture restricted to finitely presented groups is not addressed.
249.summary: Constructs a finitely generated residually finite group with integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture. It has no two-dimensional classifying space, even with infinitely many cells.

papers.title: A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

250.explainer: Higman showed finitely generated subgroups of finitely presented groups are exactly the recursively presented ones. Boone and Higman conjectured the algebraic counterpart for decidable word problem: these are exactly the subgroups of finitely presented simple groups. The claim constructs finite 'algebraic envelopes' that make the embedding into Thompson-like simple groups finitely presentable.
250.caveats: 35+30+18 pages. Faithfulness depends on the Lean encoding of finite presentation, word problem decidability and type F_infinity; the docs describe standard definitions.
250.lean: main theorem formalized (BooneHigman: full equivalence; SimpleOvergroups; UniversalFInfinity). The converse about recursively presented subgroups in (c) is not formalized.
250.summary: A finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, proving the Boone–Higman conjecture. The target can have type F_∞: a classifying space with finitely many cells in each dimension. A single group of type F_∞ can also contain every finitely presented group.

papers.title: Finite algebraic envelopes and the Boone–Higman conjecture
Simple F∞ overgroups of groups with decidable word problem
A universal group of type F∞

251.explainer: Amenable groups have every bounded representation conjugate to a unitary one; Dixmier asked if that characterizes amenability. Free subgroups give counterexamples, but nonamenable groups without free subgroups (like Burnside groups) are the hard case. The claim builds, for any nonamenable group, a representation whose similarity to a unitary would yield an invariant mean.
251.caveats: Only 19 pages for Dixmier. Note the interaction with 248: if F is nonamenable, Dixmier gives non-unitarizable representations of F. Lean source directory is small (~4k lines) because it builds on general analysis.
251.lean: main theorem formalized (DixmierAllDiscrete; Dixmier with a separable witness of bound 101 for countable groups). Strong Ulam stability (b) not formalized.
251.summary: Resolves Dixmier's problem for all discrete groups: amenability is equivalent to every uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation being similar to a unitary representation. For countable discrete groups, amenability is also equivalent to strong Ulam stability: sufficiently accurate unitary approximate representations are uniformly close in operator norm to genuine representations on the same, possibly infinite-dimensional, Hilbert space.

papers.title: Unitarizability implies amenability for discrete groups
Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability

252.explainer: Residual finiteness means every element is detected by a finite quotient; for hyperbolic groups it was conjectured (Gromov) and is known for cubulated ones, which covers almost every example people use. A counterexample shows coarse negative curvature alone is not enough. The claim constructs a CAT(0) triangle complex whose fundamental group traps an element in all finite quotients.
252.caveats: 21 pages; existential: proves one member of a finite family is in the finite residual without saying which. Combined with Kapovich-Wise, this implies there is a hyperbolic group with no proper finite-index subgroups at all, a striking consequence the summary does not mention; worth checking the paper states it.
252.lean: main theorem formalized (TorsionFreeHyperbolic: Release075.main, non-residual-finiteness). Nonlinearity follows by Malcev's theorem but is not separately formalized.
252.summary: Constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, answering the residual-finiteness question negatively. One fixed nonidentity element is killed by every finite-dimensional linear representation over every commutative field, so the group is not linear over any such field.

papers.title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite

253.explainer: Finitely presented infinite simple groups (like Thompson's T, V) tend to be nonamenable, and amenable simple examples were only finitely generated. The claim finds one in polygon exchange transformations (piecewise isometries of square tilings), whose dynamics gives amenability via Juschenko-Monod-type extensive amenability while finite presentation comes from local rewriting.
253.caveats: 58 pages; existence only, no explicit size. Lean development ~85k lines.
253.lean: main theorem formalized (SimpleAmenable.main, amenability via Følner condition).
253.summary: Constructs an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group, answering the longstanding question of whether these properties can occur simultaneously.

papers.title: An infinite finitely presented simple amenable group

254.explainer: Artin groups generalize braid groups: one generator per node of a Coxeter diagram and braid relations of the given lengths. The K(pi,1) conjecture says a natural finite complex built from the diagram (the Salvetti complex) already has no higher homotopy, giving every Artin group a finite classifying space, torsion-freeness and computable cohomology. The claim proves contractibility of the universal cover by a 'harmonic height' filtration that removes cells layer by layer, with an obstruction argument showing no layer can create homotopy.
254.caveats: 62+29+55 pages. Arguably the single most important group-theory claim in the release together with Cannon and Thompson F. Note the Lean target bakes in the combinatorial model of the Salvetti cover; an independent check of that definition is worthwhile.
254.lean: main theorem formalized (HarmonicArtin.salvetti_cover_contractible; ArtinCAT0.main; ArtinParabolicIntersections). The Lean SalvettiCover is the geometric realization of the nerve of a poset of lifted cells (Artin group element x spherical subset, with a face relation given by reduced words minimal in the parabolic…
254.summary: The Salvetti complex of every finite-rank Artin group is aspherical, proving the Artin K(π,1) conjecture. Arbitrary intersections of its parabolic subgroups are parabolic, proving the Parabolic Intersection Conjecture. An explicit Artin group admits no proper cocompact isometric action on any nonempty proper CAT(0) space.

papers.title: Harmonic heights and the Artin K(pi,1) conjecture
An Artin group with no geometric CAT(0) action
Parabolic intersections in Artin groups

255.explainer: Quasi-isometry forgets everything but large-scale shape. Gromov showed groups shaped like nilpotent groups are virtually nilpotent; the solvable analogue (polycyclic groups, lattices in solvable Lie groups) was open beyond special cases. The claim controls the 'height' coordinate of self quasi-isometries of solvable Lie models up to bounded error, which forces an algebraic structure on any group with that shape.
255.caveats: 73 pages. One of the largest Lean developments in this group.
255.lean: main theorem formalized (PolycyclicRecognition: group_recognition, lattice_recognition, uniform bounded height). Lean ~262k lines.
255.summary: Proves that every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic, resolving the Eskin–Fisher–Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture. Equivalently, a group quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group is virtually a uniform lattice in some such Lie group, possibly a different one.

papers.title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups

256.explainer: Can adding one generator and one relation kill a nontrivial group? Kervaire conjectured no. For finite groups, Gerstenhaber-Rothaus used topology of unitary groups (a degree argument); the hard case is groups that do not embed in compact Lie groups. The claim gets injectivity for all groups by a spectral-phase argument and a theorem that a certain planar surface cannot have exactly one nontrivial boundary.
256.caveats: Kervaire itself is formalized in its standard equivalent strengthening; the headline 'Howie's conjecture' is not. 13-page Kervaire proof via spectral phase in unitary groups and a fixed-space theorem: again very short for a 60-year-old problem, but the Lean check is direct.
256.lean: partial formalization: the unimodular coefficient-injectivity theorem underlying Kervaire is formalized (Kervaire.coefficient_injective, for any group A); Howie's nonsingular-systems theorem (part b) is not.
256.summary: Proves that every finite system of equations over an arbitrary group whose exponent-sum matrix has full row rank over ℚ has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup, resolving Howie's conjecture. The coefficient group embeds in the presented quotient. A companion proves Kervaire's conjecture: adjoining one generator and one relation cannot trivialize a nontrivial group.

papers.title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
The Kervaire theorem for groups

257.explainer: Hyperbolic groups are defined by coarse negative curvature; the question is whether they can always be realized as symmetries of a genuinely nonpositively curved space. The claim builds a random-like triangle complex with linear filling where a limiting energy configuration shows any CAT(0) action would force a contradiction.
257.caveats: 43 pages; existence argument, no effective size. Combined with 252 (a non-residually-finite hyperbolic group) it is consistent: CAT(0) cubulated hyperbolic groups are residually finite, so a non-RF hyperbolic group cannot be cubulated; the two results point the same way.
257.lean: main theorem formalized (HyperbolicObstruction.main), but the 2-dimensionality of the witness and the locally-CAT(0) metric exclusion are not included per the Lean doc.
257.summary: Answers negatively whether every word-hyperbolic group is a CAT(0) group. Constructs one with a finite classifying space but no proper cocompact isometric action on any proper complete CAT (0) space, in any dimension.

papers.title: A hyperbolic group with no geometric CAT(0) action

258.explainer: One-relator groups (one defining relation) are a classical testing ground. Baumslag-Solitar subgroups are the obvious obstruction to hyperbolicity; Gersten conjectured they are the only one. The claim follows the Magnus-Moldavanskii hierarchy, proving hyperbolicity is preserved at each HNN step using stationary currents and annulus arguments.
258.caveats: Not formalized; 53 + 145 pages. Each paper uses the other: Gersten's paper cites the companion for virtual compact specialness in its corollary.
258.summary: Proves Gersten's conjecture: every finitely generated one-relator group containing no Baumslag–Solitar subgroup BS(m,n), with m,n ≠ 0, is word-hyperbolic. It also proves that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special.

papers.title: Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic
Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups

259.explainer: Cost measures how many edges per point you need to connect the orbits of a measure-preserving action; Gaboriau asked whether it depends only on the group. The claim uses a group where one action admits a cheap graphing (a height coordinate lets a-edges propagate) while the Bernoulli action provably needs more, via a rank bound on finite permutation models.
259.caveats: Not formalized; 27 pages. Constants explicit but tiny (K = e^96 99^99/95^95, alpha < 1/200, K alpha^3 < 1/2). The counterexample does not address whether all groups with cost-1 Bernoulli shifts have fixed price, or the fixed-price-1 question for specific groups like SL_3(Z).
259.summary: Constructs a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs, answering the general fixed-price problem negatively. Its Bernoulli action has cost bounded away from one, while a sequence of finite height extensions has costs tending to one.

papers.title: A group without fixed price

260.explainer: The Penrose inequality says a spacetime containing a black hole must carry at least the mass of a Schwarzschild black hole of the same horizon size; a violation would undermine cosmic censorship. The proof here deforms the original data into a time-symmetric-looking comparison (new end with zero momentum, conformal changes, a 'filled' scalar identity coupling a height function to the metric) so that mass and enclosing area can be controlled at once, then compares every enclosing cut back to the original data.
260.caveats: 13 manuscripts, ~1,355 pages: the largest family in the group and effectively unreviewable quickly. The headline uses the minimum-enclosing-area formulation with only future trapping, plus explicit decay hypotheses; the 'every dimension' claim would include dimensions >=8 where even the Riemannian case was previously open, which is a strong extra claim. Kerr-Newman version assumes zero ADM momentum, Coulomb asymptotics and the physical-area condition A>=4 pi sqrt(Q^4+4J^2) as a hypothesis.
260.lean: partial formalization: only the Cha-Khuri-Sakovich end-replacement construction and Schwarzschild equality examples (CKSBondiPenrose.lean, standard axioms); lean/docs/260.md says the general Penrose inequality remains unformalized and a retained connected-case inequality is conditional on the asymptotically flat…
260.summary: Proves the sharp enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended asymptotically flat initial data in every spatial dimension n ≥ 3, under dominant energy, weak future trapping, positive enclosing area, and the stated decay assumptions. It bounds invariant ADM mass below using minimum enclosing area, with equality rigidity under additional horizon hypotheses. Charged upper-area bounds treat dyonic three-dimensional data; the higher-dimensional purely electric extension uses the matched neutral theorem.

papers.title: The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity
A Charged Reduction of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality in Spatial Dimensions at Least Four
Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity
The Kerr–Newman Penrose Inequality for Axisymmetric Electrovacuum Exteriors
Electromagnetic tails and the Kerr–Newman Penrose inequality
The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity
The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data
A local Penrose inequality for conformal perturbations of Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter data
The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area
Conformal flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality with minimizing frontiers
Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality
Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality
Area-controlled end replacement and the Bondi Penrose inequality in the CKS class

261.explainer: Electrons in a random crystal either diffuse (metal) or get trapped (insulator); in 3D weak disorder should leave them mobile (ac spectrum), while in 2D any disorder should trap them (pure point spectrum). The d>=3 paper builds a multiscale scheme that marks uncertain 'pending' sites and controls their effect through unitary scattering matrices and martingale estimates; the 2D paper proves an impedance estimate uniform in exterior data and then applies the Simon-Wolff rank-one criterion.
261.caveats: Two of the most famous open problems in mathematical physics claimed at once, neither formally checked (the formalized statement is a textbook fact). Restricted to the uniform single-site law; ac spectrum only on an interval near the band centre at weak disorder, not the full predicted mobility-edge picture. 171 pages of multiscale/probabilistic arguments (pending sites, scattering-matrix martingales) would need expert refereeing.
261.lean: partial formalization: only a supporting statement (PlanarAndersonSpectrum.lean) identifying the almost-sure spectrum on Z^2 as [-4-h,4+h]; lean/docs/261.md says the pure-point spectral type is not formalized. Nothing for d>=3.
261.summary: Resolves the predicted spectral contrast for the lattice Anderson model with independent uniform site potentials. In dimension two, every positive disorder strength gives almost surely pure-point spectrum. In every fixed dimension d ≥ 3, sufficiently weak positive disorder gives purely absolutely continuous spectrum on a fixed open interval with nonzero spectral weight.

papers.title: Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three
Pure-Point Spectrum for the Two-Dimensional Anderson Model at Every Positive Disorder

262.explainer: Lieb-Thirring inequalities bound the sum of powers of a Schrodinger operator's bound-state energies by an integral of the potential; they underlie the stability-of-matter proof. The conjecture says that in 1D, for intermediate exponents, a potential with a single bound state is already the worst case. The proof is a finite-interval action inequality obtained through a rank-one comparison for an energy-dependent matrix field and a continuation argument.
262.caveats: The gamma=1 case had just been settled by Read-Schulz (Sept 2026), so 'remaining cases' is accurate; the matrix extension and equality classification are unformalized. Scalar theorem is Lean-checked (modulo statement fidelity). Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
262.lean: main theorem formalized for the scalar case (LiebThirring.lean, standard axioms): bound with the one-bound-state constant for 1/2<gamma<3/2, optimality attained by (r+1)sech^2(rx). Matrix version and equality classification not formalized.
262.summary: Proves the sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequality for 1/2 < γ < 3/2 and arbitrary finite-matrix potentials W ≥ 0 with ∫tr (W^(γ+1/2)) < ∞: the optimal constant is the scalar one-bound-state value, independent of matrix size. All equality cases are direct sums, in one constant unitary basis, of scalar sech² solitons with independent scales and centers, and zero channels.

papers.title: Equality cases in the sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb–Thirring inequality
Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequalities for matrix potentials
Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constants

263.explainer: How many electrons can a nucleus of charge Z hold? Experiment says at most about Z+1, but the best theorem gave roughly 1.22Z. The papers prove local screening estimates showing that, outside a universal radius, the outer electrons see an essentially neutral system, which caps the excess at a constant per nucleus.
263.caveats: The headline Z+CM theorem (the actual ionization conjecture) is unformalized; what is formalized is the asymptotic 'generalized' part, itself a strong claim. Constant C is existential, not explicit. Strict-binding formulation (E_n<E_{n-1}); threshold states not addressed. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
263.lean: partial formalization: the generalized-ionization energy asymptotics I_m(Z)/m^{7/3}->a_TF and the outer-radius asymptotics are formalized (CoulombIonization.lean, CoulombRadii.lean, standard axioms).

Neutral-atom first ionization energies and radii containing all but an expected half-electron have universal positive upper and lower bounds. The energy cost of removing m electrons has Thomas–Fermi asymptotics as m → ∞ and Z/m → ∞; neutral-atom outer radii have the corresponding iterated-limit asymptotics, taking Z → ∞ first.

Generalized ionization energies for full Coulomb atoms

264.explainer: Strong cosmic censorship says generic black-hole interiors end in a singularity bad enough that physics cannot be continued, preserving determinism. The proof shows that if an extension existed, averaging holonomies of tiny loops would force a curvature block to be small, while an injected late gravitational wave packet makes it measurably large; a Baire category argument turns this contradiction into genericity.
264.caveats: Local and generic only: a Baire-category statement in a small neighbourhood of each fixed Kerr bridge, no |a|->0 or extremal uniformity, inextendibility not shown open, neighbourhood depends on the fixed Kerr. Avoids needing full Kerr exterior stability by using finite Cauchy stability plus late wave packets, a clever but unrefereed design. Not full SCC. No formalization; ~278 pages across three mutually dependent papers. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g.
264.summary: Proves local strong cosmic censorship near each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge. A dense G_δ subset of a weighted smooth neighborhood of smooth complete two-ended asymptotically flat vacuum data has full maximal globally hyperbolic developments with no future continuous nondegenerate extension whose weak connection is locally square-integrable. No symmetry is imposed; extensions need not satisfy the vacuum equations.
