265.explainer: An area law says ground-state entanglement scales with a region's boundary, not its volume; it is why tensor-network methods work. The paper builds approximate ground-state projectors from the global gap alone, organized by history trees and depth partitions across layers of the square lattice, and converts them into entropy bounds and PEPS approximations.
265.caveats: No formalization. Only the global gap is assumed (no local gaps, frustration-freeness or translation invariance), which is exactly the hard case. The PEPS result is existential with polynomial bond dimension and 1/L error, not an efficient algorithm and not the 'injective with gapped parent' structural form of the PEPS conjecture. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
265.summary: Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains, using only a uniform full-system spectral gap and bounds on the local interactions. On open L× L squares, uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor ground states also admit projected entangled-pair state approximations with polynomial bond dimension and global vector error at most L⁻¹.

papers.title: A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap
Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states

266.explainer: Mutually unbiased bases are measurement settings where knowing one outcome tells you nothing about another; d+1 of them give optimal state tomography, and they exist when d is a prime power. Dimension 6 is the smallest unknown case. The proof covers the space of candidate vectors by small 'phase balls', certifies with interval-style inequalities which pairs could be orthogonal or unbiased, then shows by exhaustive graph search that two further bases would need a pattern of two 6-cliques that never survives.
266.caveats: The headline N(6)=3 rests on a floating-point verification pipeline with 'stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions'; that is weaker evidence than an exact certificate. The Lean-checked part (<=5, i.e. no complete set of 7) is itself a notable result that was open. Ref: equality N(6)=3 appears as Conjecture 1 in Klappenecker-Rotteler (2004). Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
266.lean: partial formalization: MUBSix.lean (standard axioms) formalizes 'every MUB family in C^6 has at most 5 members' plus the Fourier-vanishing statement for Hadamards not equivalent to Tao's matrix. The headline bound of 3 (floating-point computer search) is explicitly NOT formalized per lean/docs/266.md.
266.summary: Proves N(6)=3, resolving Zauner's dimension-six mutually unbiased bases conjecture: three such bases exist in ℂ⁶, but four cannot. The exclusion is a complete certified computation under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions. An independent companion proves the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner Fourier-vanishing conjecture for order-six complex Hadamard matrices outside Tao's cubic equivalence class.

papers.title: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
Exact Fourier certificates for complex Hadamard matrices of order six

267.explainer: Bose-Einstein condensation (a macroscopic fraction of particles in one quantum state) is proven for free bosons but, for interacting particles in the infinite-volume limit, only in special scaling regimes. The papers use a path/loop representation of the Gibbs state with random routes between cells and encounter estimates to show long cycles carry a positive fraction of particles.
267.caveats: The positive-temperature result gives some small T(a,rho)>0 and is not meant to locate the transition; it is unformalized. The formalized ground-state BEC in the true thermodynamic limit would by itself be a landmark claim if the statement is faithful. Five mutually supporting papers, ~279 pages. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
267.lean: partial formalization: HardSphere.lean (standard axioms) formalizes ground-state BEC for the dilute hard-sphere gas with fraction >= c_0 uniform for rho a^3 < eps_0. The positive-temperature theorem and the depletion laws are not formalized.
267.summary: Proves Bose–Einstein condensation for the exact canonical Gibbs state of the three-dimensional hard-sphere gas: each fixed exclusion distance and sufficiently small fixed density admit a strictly positive temperature, independent of volume, with positive condensate fraction in the thermodynamic limit. At zero temperature, proves the Bogoliubov leading quantum-depletion law for hard spheres and fixed bounded nonnegative radial finite-range potentials of positive scattering length, taking the thermodynamic limit before the dilute limit.

Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas
Quantum Depletion for Fixed Bounded Repulsive Potentials
A density-uniform condensate bound for dilute Bose gases
Ground-state condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas

268.explainer: Haldane predicted that chains of spin-1 magnets have an energy gap while spin-1/2 chains do not, a cornerstone of topological phases. The proof writes the partition function both as a sum over physical energies and, through a transfer operator, as a spatial moment; 'purity' of both distributions improves quadratically when length and inverse temperature are doubled together, so two finite numerical certificates bootstrap to every larger even length and force a unique ground state with a gap.
268.caveats: Short (30 + 28 pages) for a 40-year-old problem; relies on rigorous enclosures of matrix-exponential traces of small twisted chains computed at inverse temperatures 21/2 and 49/4 (finite computer-assisted certificates) plus variational MPS inputs. Proven bound log(20)/784 is about 0.0038 vs the numerical 0.41; fine for existence. Periodic even-length formulation only (the companion handles odd open chains with a field). Not formalized; the certificates need independent rerunning.
268.summary: Proves the spin-one Haldane gap conjecture for the pure antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings: the spectral gap stays uniformly positive as the chain grows. A companion establishes a gap for odd open chains with endpoint field h=3/5 and gives boundary-selected infinite-volume states with topological index −1.

papers.title: The periodic spin-one Haldane gap
A boundary-field gap for the spin-one Heisenberg chain

269.explainer: The fractional quantum Hall effect needs the Laughlin state to be separated from excitations by an energy gap that does not close as the system grows (incompressibility). The proof establishes an operator inequality H^2 >= gamma H on the whole Fock space by an orthogonal decomposition that tracks flux, particle and hole numbers, which immediately gives a uniform gap, and then perturbs it.
269.caveats: 'Full V1 interaction' with unit coefficients on the sphere; the gap is uniform only for sufficiently large N and constants for stability are existential. Formalized core is strong evidence for the gap claim. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
269.lean: partial formalization: Laughlin*.lean (standard axioms) formalize the uniform unperturbed gap (>= 1/25 at flux 3(N-1) for large N; finite spherical bound 1/100; Fock-space inequality H^2 >= gamma H for gamma < gamma_* = 0.4616733319001 > 1/25...
269.summary: Proves the fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full V₁ interaction at filling 1/3 on the round sphere. The unique ground state remains uniformly gapped under sufficiently weak bounded real scalar one-body potentials projected to the lowest Landau level. Both the gap and disorder threshold are uniform over all sufficiently large particle numbers and all normalized potential profiles.

papers.title: Uniform Stability of the Spherical Laughlin Gap
A Fock-space inequality and the Laughlin spectral gap

270.explainer: In matrix theory each graviton with N units of momentum is a bound state of N D0-branes sitting exactly at zero energy, at the bottom of a continuum, which makes it notoriously hard to prove. The paper computes a Fredholm index of a massive deformation, controls the charge near separated and nested clusters of eigenvalues with explicit norm estimates, and passes to the massless limit by a tightness argument to count the kernel exactly.
270.caveats: The threshold-state result is consistent with physics expectations and would make the index arguments rigorous. The positive-energy embedded eigenvalues claim is surprising and contradicts a statement in the original BFSS paper; it depends on the specific closure of the gauge-invariant supercharge form and deserves scrutiny by physicists. Unformalized. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
270.summary: Proves that the undeformed relative SU(N) BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every finite N ≥ 2, resolving the threshold-bound-state conjecture. For SU(2), a companion proves infinitely many normalizable positive-energy eigenstates with unbounded energies, contradicting the original BFSS paper's exclusion of additional bound states at N = 2.

papers.title: The unique threshold bound state of the SU(N) BFSS model
Positive eigenvalues of the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian

271.explainer: Iron is magnetic, but proving that the textbook quantum model of a ferromagnet actually magnetizes at low temperature in 3D has been open for decades because the trick used for antiferromagnets (reflection positivity) fails. The proof uses Toth-style exchange-cycle representations: pin boundary spins up, then show by a downward induction (with stable polynomials and a determinant identity) that interior cycles almost always reach a pin, so an interior spin is up with probability bounded away from 1/2.
271.caveats: Magnetization bound is S/4, not the physical value; beta_0 is existential. The formalized statement defines its own quasi-local algebra, dynamics and KMS condition from scratch; fidelity of those definitions should be audited, but they read as standard. Bloch-law papers (b)-(d) are unformalized and long. OpenAI released an abridged reasoning summary for this result. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
271.lean: partial formalization: the spontaneous-magnetization theorem (a) is fully formalized in Heisenberg.lean (standard axioms): a translation-invariant KMS state with omega(S^z_0) >= l/8, l=2S, for d>=3 and all beta >= beta_0, plus convergence of the finite-volume dynamics.
271.summary: Proves Bloch's T^(3/2) law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every positive quantum spin, allowing nonnegative symmetric finite-range couplings whose support generates ℤ³. The thermodynamic limit precedes the zero-field derivative and low-temperature limit. The family also proves spontaneous magnetization for nearest-neighbor models in every dimension d ≥ 3 and determines the first lattice correction for three-dimensional nearest-neighbor couplings.

papers.title: Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions
The first lattice correction to Bloch's law
The spherical magnetization law for the three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet

272.explainer: PPT^2 asked whether applying a 'positive-partial-transpose' noisy channel twice always destroys all entanglement; it was a favourite open problem in quantum information. An explicit channel on 21-level systems whose square keeps entanglement settles it negatively and in Lean; the same structure gives an entangled state from which no secret key can be extracted.
272.caveats: Zero key is proved only for the protocol class 'specified here' (local instruments that complete almost surely); whether that captures every operational protocol in the standard definition should be checked. The PPT^2 disproof is formally verified and is the cleanest headline. 272.lean: partial formalization: DimensionTenChannel.lean and DimensionTenPair.lean (standard axioms) formalize the PPT-composition and PPT^2 counterexamples (21x21 trace-preserving PPT channel whose square is not entanglement breaking). The zero-distillable-key statement is not formalized.
272.summary: Constructs an entangled state on ℂ¹⁰⊗ℂ¹⁰ with zero distillable secret key for the specified local-instrument protocols that complete almost surely. These allow joint local processing and authenticated two-way public communication, with no other shared private resource and an eavesdropper holding the input purification and public record. A trace-preserving PPT channel on M₂₁(ℂ) whose square is not entanglement breaking disproves Christandl's PPT-square conjecture.

papers.title: Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten

273.explainer: Mixing two light beams on a beam splitter cannot produce less entropy than mixing thermal light of the same entropies; this 'quantum entropy power inequality in photon-number units' was the missing step for several optical channel capacities. A short (32-page) proof that Lean accepts is one of the cleaner wins in the group.
273.caveats: Finite-energy, finite-mode setting (the natural one). Formal verification covers the main inequality; consequences unformalized. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).

273.summary: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes: the output's entropy photon number is at least the transmissivity-weighted average of the inputs'. Arbitrary entanglement within each input is allowed, and product thermal inputs attain equality even when their entropies differ.

papers.title: The entropy photon-number inequality

274.explainer: AC0 can't compute parity; the quantum analogue was open for 25 years because quantum fan-in gates can spread information in non-classical ways. The proof localizes the circuit with a 'product-projection' estimate and shows, by an induction over depth, that the measured output's correlation with parity decays with n while the qubit count stays polynomial.
274.caveats: 'Measured-output model' (one output qubit measured, garbage discarded); a clean-computation variant or exact-parity-on-coherent-registers variant is a different question, though bounded-error measured parity is the standard reading. Lean-checked. The circuit model's definitions in Lean define gates and depth from scratch and should be audited for fidelity. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).

274.summary: Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage. Ancillas start in zero, one output qubit is measured, and all other registers may be discarded. Xu–Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority.

papers.title: Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound
Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity

275.explainer: Quantum chemistry's central problem, the electronic ground-state energy of a molecule, is shown to be as hard as any problem verifiable by a quantum computer, even with only hydrogen-like nuclei and no artificial fields. The reduction encodes a local-Hamiltonian instance into arrangements of nuclei.

Deterministic polynomial-time reductions work even with only unit-charge nuclei at distinct rational positions, polynomially many electrons and an energy-threshold separation of at least one.

276.explainer: Generalized amplitude damping models a qubit relaxing in a warm environment (e.g. superconducting qubits). Knowing its exact classical capacity requires showing entangled inputs never help (additivity); the paper proves an entropy inequality for block matrices that gives this.

An explicit one-variable optimization gives the capacity, attained by independent two-state signal ensembles with collective decoding. Holevo capacity, minimum output entropy and regularized classical capacity are additive when tensoring with any finite-dimensional quantum channel.

papers.title: Classical capacity and entropy inequalities for generalized amplitude damping

277.explainer: Parallel repetition asks whether playing a game many times in parallel makes cheating exponentially unlikely; for quantum-entangled players this underpins MIP*-style protocols. The paper turns a known 'conditioning' estimate into concentration of the number of rounds won.
277.caveats: The hard part (exponential all-wins parallel repetition for general entangled games) is attributed to prior work, one of which is an earlier OpenAI publication and another a very recent ECCC report; this family's contribution is the transfer from conditioning to threshold bounds. Family summary does not mention that the Lean statement uses delta^13. Arbitrary joint finite-dimensional entangled strategies and correlated question distributions are allowed.

papers.title: Threshold parallel repetition for finite-dimensional entangled games

278.explainer: Kohn-Sham density functional theory, the workhorse of computational chemistry, presumes every real electron density can be reproduced by non-interacting electrons in some potential. The paper builds a three-electron molecule whose density cannot, so the foundational assumption is false in general.
278.caveats: Unformalized; the nuclear charge is specified only by a formula (likely huge). Concerns one potential class (L^{3/2}+L^inf); other classes are not addressed. This disproves Kohn–Sham ensemble representability for that potential class; the required nuclear charge is specified nonnumerically.

papers.title: A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation

279.explainer: Shor's algorithm succeeds with high probability and uses arbitrary rotation angles; this result removes both the error and the continuous angles, so a fixed finite instruction set factors exactly in polynomial time.

papers.title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set

281.explainer: QAOA is a leading near-term quantum optimization heuristic; this shows that in the infinite-size limit it can get arbitrarily close to the true SK ground state, matching what Montanari-style classical algorithms achieve, via full-support (no-gap) properties of the Parisi measure.

282.explainer: Physicists expect any scale-invariant unitary QFT to be conformally invariant; this is proven in 2D. The paper proves a 4D version inside a strongly axiomatized framework, showing the stress tensor's trace can be improved away.

The stress tensor has a traceless improvement with unchanged spacetime charges. The conclusion concerns local Ward identities, not a global conformal action on the whole net.

283.explainer: Can a quantum computer with access to a cleverly chosen classical oracle implement any unitary efficiently? This relates quantum state/unitary complexity to classical complexity. The paper constructs a uniform oracle circuit that, for some oracle depending on the target, gets within constant diamond distance.
283.caveats: Constant-error (1/2 in diamond norm) formulation; whether error can be driven to any epsilon with poly(n, log 1/eps) queries is not stated in the summary. Unformalized, short paper. 283.summary: Solves the constant-error Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem: a uniform polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit approximates every n-qubit unitary channel within diamond-norm error 1/2, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Gates, qubits, oracle calls and query length are polynomially bounded. The target-dependent oracle may have an unrestricted truth table; its efficient classical construction is not asserted.

284.explainer: For total Boolean functions quantum computers can only give polynomial query speedups; the question is the largest possible power over randomized algorithms. A cheat-sheet construction whose certificate address is computed by Forrelation-type partial functions, with pointers and circuit transcripts certifying the address, pushes the separation to the quartic upper bound.

Short (19 pages) and unformalized; query-complexity experts can check it quickly, which makes it a good early test of the release. Here R and Q are randomized and quantum worst-case bit-query complexities with error at most 1/3; computation between queries is unrestricted.

285.explainer: Baum-Connes predicts that the K-theory of a group's reduced C*-algebra is computed by geometry (an index map); a famous consequence is that torsion-free groups have no nontrivial projections in that algebra. The constructions build groups from labelled expander-like graphs so that a matrix over the group algebra has a spectral gap; continuous functional calculus then produces a genuine projection in C*_r(G) with irrational (or fractional) trace, which the assembly map cannot hit.
285.caveats: Unformalized, 184 pages of graphical small-cancellation/expander constructions ('infinite graphical presentation', voltage covers, nilpotent deck groups). The projection lies in C*_r but not the group ring (the group ring has no nontrivial idempotents per a companion); the groups are necessarily far from a-T-menable or hyperbolic. If correct, this is the biggest news in the group for noncommutative geometry, so it is the first thing experts should referee.
285.summary: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly. A finitely generated torsion-free example witnesses the injectivity failure. Separately, a torsion-free group has a nontrivial projection in its reduced group C*-algebra, disproving the Kadison–Kaplansky conjecture.

papers.title: A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity

An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes

The arithmetic category and stable recovery of lattice factors

287.explainer: L(F_n) is the von Neumann algebra generated by the free group on n letters acting on l^2; the 80-year-old question is whether it remembers n. The proof starts from free Haar unitaries (A_1..A_n, C) generating L(F_{n+1}), runs trace-preserving polynomial flows driven by a free-group cocycle so that a word in the moved A_j's approximates the extra generator C while each A_j moves arbitrarily little, iterates with adaptive error budgets, and shows the limiting n-tuple is free Haar and still generates everything, giving L(F_n) = L(F_{n+1}).
287.caveats: Surprising direction (most experts expected non-isomorphism), but the paper is short, constructive and Lean-checked; the remaining risk is statement fidelity and the build actually passing (I did not run Lean). The paper notes Shlyakhtenko's recent related preprint but says it uses no result from it. The family summary matches the paper. Public expert reaction: none found in a limited search beyond news summaries (e.g. kingy.ai blog).
287.lean: main theorem formalized: ComparatorChallenges/InterpolatedFactors.lean (statement at lines 216-219, solution module OAI.Analysis.InterpolatedFactors.Interpolation, ~17.6k lines plus OAI/Analysis/FreeGroupFactor; permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice only).
287.summary: Resolves the free group factor isomorphism problem: L(𝔽₂) ≅ L(𝔽₃), and hence all interpolated free group factors, including L(𝔽_∞), are isomorphic. Their common factor has fundamental group ℝ_(> 0).

papers.title: An isomorphism of the free group factors

288.explainer: Kadison asked whether a representation of a C*-algebra that respects multiplication but not adjoints can always be 'straightened' into an honest *-representation by a change of inner product. By Haagerup and Kirchberg, this reduces to showing inner derivations are completely bounded with a uniform constant; the paper gets that constant from a free-product corner estimate (Schur-Weyl averaging, Hankel matrices) placed inside any II_1 factor via Popa's independence theorem.
288.caveats: Lean-checked with standard axioms (fidelity audit and actual build not done by me). Uses Popa's relative independence theorem and Kirchberg's equivalence as cited inputs, which the formalization must have reproved or the statement depends on library facts; the solution module compiles them per the release. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
288.lean: main theorem formalized: KadisonSimilarity.lean (standard axioms) contains similarityTheorem (every bounded unital hom from any C*-algebra into B(K) is similar to a *-hom), universalCommutatorTheorem and universalHyperreflexivity with explicit constant 3*factorConstant+2. Paper has 31 pages.
288.summary: Proves Kadison's similarity conjecture: every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex C*-algebra to operators on a Hilbert space becomes a *-homomorphism after conjugation by a bounded invertible operator.

papers.title: Kadison's similarity theorem through uniform derivation estimates

289.explainer: If two algebras of operators are uniformly close, are they the same up to a small rotation of the Hilbert space? Yes for von Neumann algebras, with a universal tolerance; no for norm-separable C*-algebras, where close algebras can fail to be conjugate.
289.caveats: For von Neumann algebras (the original setting); the C*-algebraic spatial form is disproved in the separable case. The positive result is plausibly downstream of 288's uniform derivation/hyperreflexivity estimates (the CCSSWW 'similarity and perturbation' link), which is consistent rather than suspicious. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
289.lean: main theorem formalized: StrongKadisonKastler.lean (standard axioms), universal strong stability for von Neumann algebras. Counterexample papers not formalized.
289.summary: Proves that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity, with a universal tolerance in the operator-norm distance between unit balls. Counterexamples show that near-identity conjugacy fails for one-sided near inclusions, and that arbitrarily close norm-separable C*-algebras need not be ambiently unitarily conjugate.

papers.title: Universal strong Kadison–Kastler stability
Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras Without Small Spatial Embeddings
Close Separable C*-Algebras Without Spatial Conjugacy

290.explainer: For type III_1 factors (the algebras of local quantum field theory), Connes asked whether the 'bicentralizer' of a state is always trivial; Haagerup's solution in the hyperfinite case was the key to classifying hyperfinite factors. The proof recovers spectral information of the modular group on uniformly bounded elements.
290.caveats: Main conjecture unformalized; formal content is a supporting analytic lemma. Short papers (19+16 pages) for a 45-year-old problem. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
290.lean: partial formalization: BoundedRecovery.lean (standard axioms) formalizes the bounded spectral recovery theorem only; lean/docs/290.md states the absolute bicentralizer conjecture is not included.
290.summary: Proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for every type III₁ factor with separable predual and every faithful normal state. More generally, for every inclusion N ⊂ M of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals admitting a faithful normal conditional expectation, constructs an amenable expected subalgebra P ⊂ N with P'∩ c(M)=N'∩ c(M), resolving the relative bicentralizer conjecture.

papers.title: Expected amenable subalgebras preserving core commutants
Bounded recovery for modular spectral averages

291.explainer: The Elliott classification programme classifies simple nuclear C*-algebras that are 'Z-stable'; Toms and Winter conjectured this regularity is equivalent to a comparison property of projections/positive elements and to finite nuclear dimension. The family proves the missing comparison-implies-regularity step via uniform property Gamma.
291.caveats: Four papers bundling several distinct conjectures; summary title emphasizes the equivariant case while the bigger news is the Toms-Winter implication. Check exactly which hypotheses enter the formal comparison statement before citing it as the full unital Toms-Winter. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
291.lean: partial formalization: UniformGamma.lean (standard axioms) formalizes (d) and, per lean/docs/291.md, the linked comparison results prove Jiang-Su absorption and uniform property Gamma for simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear algebras with strict comparison, i.e. the unital Toms-Winter implication.
291.summary: Proves equivariant Jiang–Su stability for every countable discrete amenable group action on a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Jiang–Su-stable C*-algebra, resolving this case of Szabó's conjecture without restrictions on trace dynamics. The family also proves the unital Toms–Winter conjecture, equating strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability in the simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear setting.

papers.title: Equivariant Jiang–Su Stability for Amenable Actions in the Unital Stably Finite Case
Cuntz comparison and Jiang–Su absorption
Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability without elementary subquotients
Tracial projection methods and uniform property Gamma

292.explainer: Kirchberg asked whether a single nuclear 'universal' algebra, the ultrapower of the Cuntz algebra O_2, contains every separable C*-algebra. A property (T) group extended by a doubling automorphism has a full group C*-algebra whose finite-dimensional representations cannot be matched consistently in any nuclear ultrapower, so the answer is no.
292.caveats: Only 14 pages and Lean-checked; explicit group known from prior non-finiteness work. Clean and checkable. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
292.summary: Constructs an explicit separable unital full group C*-algebra that cannot embed unitally into the norm ultrapower of any fixed nonzero unital nuclear C*-algebra, for any free ultrafilter on the natural numbers. Taking the target to be O₂ answers Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem negatively.

papers.title: An explicit obstruction to nuclear norm-ultrapower embeddings

293.explainer: Does every operator have a closed subspace that every operator commuting with it preserves? The construction produces a quasinilpotent operator whose commutant acts transitively (moves any nonzero vector arbitrarily close to any other), so no such subspace exists; the II_1-factor companion builds weighted rotations whose weight has a sharp zero to destroy all invariant projections.
293.caveats: Does NOT resolve the invariant subspace problem itself (T may have invariant subspaces that are not hyperinvariant). The claim that the commutant is a proper WOT-closed transitive algebra also settles the transitive algebra problem; the family summary does not stress this but the companion abstract does. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
293.lean: main theorem formalized: HyperinvariantSubspaces.lean and BackwardIntertwiners.lean (standard axioms) state existence of T != 0, quasinilpotent (||T^n||^{1/n}->0), with transitive commutant, commutant != all operators, and commutant SOT-closed, on any separable infinite-dimensional H.
293.summary: Constructs a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nonzero proper closed subspace invariant under every commuting operator. The construction also gives operators with no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite type II₁ factor.

papers.title: Invariant-projection counterexamples for every irrational rotation
Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant

294.explainer: A quasitrace is additive only on commuting elements; Kaplansky asked whether it must be fully additive (a trace). Haagerup's theorem says yes for exact algebras; the counterexample is non-exact, and it also shows stable finiteness is not preserved by tensor products.
294.caveats: The algebra is necessarily non-exact (Haagerup). Very short (16 pages) and Lean-checked. Note the family summary says 'all of which are nonadditive'; the abstract says 'no tracial state', which is the same thing for normalized quasitraces. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
294.lean: main theorem formalized: KaplanskyQuasitrace.lean and KaplanskyStableFiniteness.lean (standard axioms), including the 1/144 non-additivity and the properly infinite tensor product.
294.summary: Disproves Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex C*-algebra admitting normalized 2-quasitraces, all of which are nonadditive. As a consequence, two unital simple stably finite C*-algebras can have a properly infinite minimal tensor product, with one factor C_r*(𝔽₂).

papers.title: A counterexample to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness

295.explainer: Hochschild cohomology measures obstructions to deforming an algebra; Kadison and Ringrose conjectured that von Neumann algebras have none with coefficients in themselves. The standard route (Christensen-Effros-Sinclair) needs every bounded cocycle to be completely bounded; uniform estimates of the 288 type supply that for II_1 factors without property Gamma, the remaining case.
295.caveats: 28 pages, Lean-checked. By Christensen-Effros-Sinclair, vanishing reduces to the completely bounded case plus a cb-ness statement, which plausibly follows from 288's uniform derivation estimate; worth noting the families are linked. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
295.lean: main theorem formalized: KadisonRingrose.lean (standard axioms), vanishing in every degree >= 2 for any W*-algebra; degree one (Kadison-Sakai) is outside the selected statement.
295.summary: Proves that every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a complex von Neumann algebra, with coefficients in the algebra itself, has a bounded primitive. Equivalently, all higher bounded Hochschild cohomology groups vanish, resolving the Kadison–Ringrose conjecture.

papers.title: Vanishing of higher bounded Hochschild cohomology

296.explainer: Is every separable von Neumann algebra generated by one operator? The proof embeds an irreducible hyperfinite subfactor P (Popa) and shows a generic unitary u together with P generates the whole factor; P itself is singly generated, so two operators suffice, and they combine into one.
296.caveats: 18 pages, Lean-checked. Proof uses Popa's irreducible hyperfinite embedding and free-independence theorems; does not appear to rely on family 287 (I grepped: it mentions free group factors only for the free-entropy corollary). Consistent with 287 (L(F_inf) singly generated). Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
296.lean: main theorem formalized: FactorGeneration.lean and RelativeGeneration.lean (standard axioms).
296.summary: Proves that every type II₁ factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators, resolving the generator problem. More strongly, for every irreducible inclusion P ⊂ M of such factors, the unitaries u with M=W*(P,u) form a dense G_δ subset in the trace 2-norm topology.

papers.title: Relative generation and the generator problem for finite factors

297.explainer: Naimark asked whether 'only one irreducible representation' forces an algebra to be the compact operators. Under extra set-theoretic axioms the answer was known to be no; this (and Tanaka's paper) show no in plain ZFC, using pure-state excision and unique-extension arguments in a nonseparable construction.
297.caveats: Not the first ZFC solution: Tanaka's human-authored paper predates it by two days, and OpenAI's summary says so. Separable case is impossible by Rosenberg. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
297.lean: main theorem formalized: Naimark.lean (standard axioms); statement quantifies over Hilbert spaces in arbitrary universes.
297.summary: Gives an alternative to Tanaka's ZFC construction of a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state and exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence. Thus the unrestricted compact-operator characterization fails without additional set-theoretic assumptions; the counterexample is nonseparable.

papers.title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC

298.explainer: Free probability has two candidate notions of entropy: counting matrix approximations (microstates) and integrating a free Fisher information. The paper finds operators where both are finite but disagree by at least 1/2.
298.caveats: Uses a large but fixed number of variables; specific normalization (norm cutoff, limsup). Lean-checked; formalizing microstates free entropy is itself notable and its definitions deserve an audit. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
298.summary: Constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple in a tracial von Neumann algebra whose microstates and nonmicrostates free entropies satisfy -∞ < χ < χ* < ∞. This answers Voiculescu’s finite-entropy equality question negatively: the matrix-approximation and free-Fisher-information definitions differ even when both are finite.

papers.title: A finite-entropy separation of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy

299.explainer: Z-stability (absorbing the Jiang-Su algebra) is the regularity property behind classification; this gives a clean intrinsic test: Z-stable exactly when no character exists on the central sequence algebra.
299.caveats: Lean-checked main criterion; tensor-power consequence not separately listed in the formal scope. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
299.lean: main theorem formalized: CharacterCriterion.lean (standard axioms) for the character criterion.
299.summary: A nonzero unital separable complex C*-algebra is Jiang–Su stable exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, for every free ultrafilter. This answers the Kirchberg–Rørdam character question. Also, the infinite minimal tensor power of every such algebra without characters is Jiang–Su stable, answering the Dadarlat–Toms question.

papers.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion

300.explainer: Paving says an operator can be cut into a few blocks along a commutative subalgebra, each with small off-diagonal part; MSS proved this for the diagonal of B(l^2). This extends a strong-operator version to every maximal abelian subalgebra with the optimal-order eps^-2 block count.
300.caveats: Unformalized; constants explicit but huge. Significance mostly within the Kadison-Singer circle of ideas. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
300.summary: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with O(ε⁻²) blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.

papers.title: Approximation Paving over Arbitrary Maximal Abelian Subalgebras
Quadratic Strong-Operator Paving over Arbitrary Maximal Abelian Subalgebras

301.explainer: Tensoring with the Razak-Jacelon algebra kills K-theory, leaving traces as the only invariant; the paper shows the full cone of tracial weights is a complete invariant for all separable nuclear algebras after this stabilization.
301.caveats: Unformalized; specialist classification result. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
301.summary: Classifies separable nuclear complex C*-algebras after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, using their full topological cones of extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights. This answers Robert’s trace-cone question, including algebras with arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients.

papers.title: The trace cone classifies Razak–Jacelon stabilizations

302.explainer: Mean dimension measures how many 'dimensions per unit time' a dynamical system has; the radius of comparison measures failure of regularity of its crossed-product C*-algebra. The conjecture that one is exactly half the other is proved for all minimal Z-actions, using a compression theorem from complex cobordism.
302.caveats: Unformalized; the topological input is an algebraic-topology theorem in complex cobordism, an unusual route that needs checking by homotopy theorists as well as operator algebraists. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
302.summary: For every minimal homeomorphism h of an infinite compact metrizable space X, the radius of comparison of C(X)⋊_hℤ equals 1/2mdim(X,h), including infinite values. Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang–Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.

papers.title: Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism
Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension

303.explainer: Purely infinite C*-algebras are the 'type III' side of the classification programme; there were several inequivalent-looking definitions. The paper shows the natural ones coincide, which yields O_inf absorption for nuclear algebras without simplicity assumptions.
303.caveats: Answers the pi => spi part; the full weak-pi equivalence is for exact algebras. Public expert reaction: none found specific to this family in a limited search (news coverage of the release as a whole exists, e.g. officechai.com, unite.ai).
303.lean: main theorem formalized: ExactInfiniteness.lean and IndividualStrongInfiniteness.lean (standard axioms).
303.summary: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and Rørdam for complex C*-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs O_∞, without unitality or simplicity assumptions.

papers.title: Weak pure infiniteness and O-infinity absorption

304.explainer: A Lie group is a group you can do calculus on; Hilbert-Smith says a group acting faithfully on a manifold cannot be wilder than that. Everything reduces to ruling out actions of the p-adic integers. The paper defines a signature-like invariant (a Witt group of self-dual sheaf complexes) on a high-dimensional test sphere whose values sit in a fixed lattice; a faithful Z_p-action would split one class into p^k equal integral parts summing to 4u, impossible once p^k exceeds four times the lattice denominator.
304.caveats: 46 pages for a ~80-year-old problem, via a new invariant (Witt groups of real sheaf complexes generated by proper images of polyhedra under arbitrary continuous maps) with no Lean support. The proof needs Verdier duality on non-constructible generated categories and a Balmer-Walter localization theorem; those are exactly the places where a subtle error could hide. Not formalized; no external check known to me.
304.summary: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.

papers.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

305.explainer: Freedman's 1982 proof of the 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture rests on embedding discs in 4-manifolds when the fundamental group is 'good'; whether every group is good (above all the free group on two letters) has been open for 40 years. The release claims an explicit 4-manifold where all algebraic preconditions hold but no disjoint embedded discs exist, detected by an algebraic invariant of how 3-dimensional cuts of a hypothetical filling would have to fit together. Reflecting the construction produces a Poincare duality group that no closed aspherical 4-manifold realizes.
305.caveats: Three papers (133 pp), no Lean. The obstruction is a new 'marked tensor / Frobenius-Koszul' invariant built from polarized Chern-Simons functions on cut data; this is far from the known toolkit and would need expert scrutiny. The PD4 paper and the companion Borel-conjecture paper (family 320) import the marked tensor obstruction as a black box, so one error would propagate to three headline claims. Note that 'F_2 not good' does not by itself say surgery fails for F_2, though family 320 claims a surgery-type failure (Borel in dim 4).
305.summary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group F₂ is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.

papers.title: A boundary-only obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
A PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model

306.explainer: Dehn surgery cuts out a knot and glues the solid torus back with a twist labelled by a fraction; the conjecture says different fractions always give genuinely different (oriented) 3-manifolds. Years of Floer theory had cornered the only possible counterexample: slopes +2 and -2 on a genus-two knot. The paper rules that out by computing one integer count of instantons two ways on a 1-parameter family of cobordisms built from a hypothetical homeomorphism: one way it is nonzero, the other way the boundary of a 1-dimensional moduli space of spinor-coupled instantons forces 2^eta times it to vanish.
306.caveats: Uses the prior reduction (only slopes +-2 on genus-2 knots remain) as input, which is legitimate. The new part is a 144-page SO(3)-monopole cobordism argument in the Pidstrigach-Tyurin / Okonek-Teleman / Feehan-Leness style with families of metrics, toric metric sectors and regularization of mixed strata. That program is notoriously hard; Feehan-Leness's own work took decades and parts are long and technical. I would treat the result as plausible-but-unverified until gauge theorists check the compactness/gluing sections (9-10). No Lean.
306.summary: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot in S³ never produce orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds, proving the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture. The statement includes the meridional slope.

papers.title: Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere

307.explainer: The coarse Novikov conjecture is the large-scale-geometry cousin of the Novikov conjecture: it predicts that the 'index' map from coarse topology to operator K-theory never loses rational information on spaces of bounded geometry. The release builds a union of finite graphs (short cycles allowed, so the Willett-Yu girth theorem does not apply) and a degree-one K-homology class whose index dies, borrowing the Bott-class-plus-Kazhdan-projection trick of Higson-Lafforgue-Skandalis.
307.caveats: Lean: OAI.CoarseAssembly.bounded_geometry_graph_counterexample_unconditional (OAI/Topology/CoarseAssembly/UnconditionalConclusion.lean:38), 335 files, ~34.5k lines, no sorry. It formalizes the ordinary (reduced) coarse Novikov counterexample; the maximal-assembly paper (the family's headline title) is not covered. Whether the bespoke Lean definitions of KX_* and Roe-algebra K-theory match the literature is a review question. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
307.summary: Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. The example is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, with an infinite-order kernel class. A companion gives the analogous failure for reduced coarse assembly, disproving the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.

papers.title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture

308.explainer: Smith-Toda complexes are the 'atoms' of chromatic homotopy: finite spectra whose homology kills exactly the first n+1 periodicity generators. Nobody knew whether V(4) exists at any prime. The paper works in an ultraproduct over primes where the obstruction theory becomes algebraic, builds the tower of cofibers there, and descends the finitely many maps needed to an actual large prime.
308.caveats: Existence only for some (non-explicit, 'sufficiently large') prime depending on n, via ultraproducts of p-local categories; consistent with Nave since the prime grows with n. The explicit p=1009 V(4) paper is a separate 44-page construction I did not check. No Lean.
308.summary: For every n ≥ 0, constructs a finite Smith–Toda spectrum at a prime p depending on n, with Brown–Peterson homology BP_*/(p,v₁,…,vₙ) and the canonical comodule structure. Thus Smith–Toda complexes exist at every height when the prime may vary; an explicit example realizes V(4) at p = 1009.

papers.title: Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes
A finite Smith–Toda complex V(4) at the prime 1009

309.explainer: The Kervaire invariant problem asks in which dimensions certain exotic framed manifolds exist; at p=2 Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel famously settled it with equivariant homotopy theory. This paper runs the analogous program at the prime 3 using the group of order 9 acting on height-6 Morava E-theory: classes with index >= 4 would have to survive in a detector where finite Euler-class 'deadlines' force them to die, while a new class in stem 322 is built explicitly from the known stem-106 class.
309.caveats: 90 pages; proves a conjectured coefficient-action model (Belmont-Ray Conj. 0.3) along the way and refutes the 'full gap' clause of their Conjecture 0.1 (claims an infinite-order element in pi_2n(E_6^{hC_9})). Heavy finite spectral-sequence bookkeeping (lengths 9, 13, 17, 53, 93 differentials) and an appendix recurrence 'for the algebraic calculations' that I could not audit. No Lean.
309.summary: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: exactly the standard classes with indices 0, 2, and 3 survive in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence, in stems 10, 106, and 322. Each surviving detection coset contains an element of exact additive order three.

papers.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three

310.explainer: Quillen asked whether the simplicial complex of elementary abelian p-subgroups 'sees' whether a group has a nontrivial normal p-subgroup. Decades of work reduced the problem, using the classification of finite simple groups, to specific configurations at the prime 2. The paper finishes those cases by constructing explicit nonzero homology cycles (full-chain propagation and 'sign group' flags) in the remaining classical-group extensions.
310.caveats: The genuinely new content is the p = 2 endgame plus a self-contained unitary dimension property; it rests on CFSG and on a long chain of human reductions which the paper uses 'in the precise form recalled in Section 2'. That is a sound structure but makes correctness depend on matching hypotheses exactly with Piterman's theorems. 63 pages. No Lean.
310.summary: Proves the rational-homology form of Quillen's conjecture for every finite group and every prime. If the largest normal p-subgroup of G is trivial, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology and is therefore not contractible.

papers.title: Rational homology and Quillen's conjecture

311.explainer: The Hopkins-Smith thick subcategory theorem says finite spectra are classified by chromatic height; Hovey and Strickland conjectured the same for dualizable objects in the K(n)-local world. Barthel-Heard-Naumann reduced this to an algebraic statement about ideals of the Lubin-Tate deformation ring that are stable under the Morava stabilizer group; the paper proves that statement by analysing stabilizer orbits.
311.caveats: 34 pages; relies on the Barthel-Heard-Naumann implication. Arithmetic core (orbit arguments in characteristic p and 0) is short; I could not check it. No Lean.
311.summary: Proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture for Lubin–Tate deformation rings over finite residue fields, at every prime and positive height n. Through the implication of Barthel–Heard–Naumann, this proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: dualizable K(n)-local spectra have exactly n+2 thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of n+1 points.

papers.title: Stabilizer orbits and thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra

312.explainer: Grothendieck guessed that 'spaces up to homotopy' are the same as fully weak infinity-groupoids: algebraic gadgets with composition defined only up to coherent higher cells. Henry showed it suffices to prove that freely adding a new cell together with a 'witness' cell connecting it to an old one doesn't change homotopy groups. The paper proves that by controlling all composites and coherence cells the free construction creates, using tree-shaped pasting data.
312.caveats: Only 26 pages because Henry's reduction does most of the bridging. Lean formalizes the elementary-expansion theorem (OAI.Grothendieck.elementary_expansion, ComparatorChallenges/GrothendieckElementaryExpansion.json; OAI/CategoryTheory/Globular, 58 files ~12.8k lines, no sorry) but not the semi-model structure or the comparison with spaces. Result is for the Ara-Henry convention of coherators; other formalizations of the hypothesis (e.g. Batanin-Leinster operads) are not addressed. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
312.summary: Proves the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for ∞-groupoids associated with every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention: these algebraic objects recover the homotopy theory of spaces.

papers.title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis via elementary expansions

313.explainer: The K(n)-local sphere is the main object of chromatic homotopy theory; its homotopy groups are huge profinite groups, and it was unknown whether each one is at least finitely generated over the p-adic integers. Combined with the known rational answer this pins down free ranks. The proof bounds torsion degree by degree using a descent spectral sequence with a vanishing line at a finite page.
313.caveats: 103 pages; no uniform bound. Relies on continuous Morava descent and the smash-product theorem's horizontal vanishing line. No Lean.
313.summary: Answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland: every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is a finitely generated ℤₚ-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree. The same conclusion holds after K(n)-localizing any finite p-local spectrum.

papers.title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere

314.explainer: Chromatic Smith theory asks how much 'chromatic height' you lose passing from fixed points of a subgroup to fixed points of the whole group. The upper bound by cyclic subnormal chains was known; the paper constructs finite spectra showing it is sharp for every p-group.
314.caveats: 30 pages; completes the Balmer spectrum topology for p-groups if correct. No Lean.
314.summary: Determines the optimal chromatic loss from geometric H-fixed points to geometric G-fixed points for every subgroup H of a finite p-group G. At every nonnegative height, the loss equals the shortest subnormal-chain length from H to G with cyclic quotients. Each quotient counts once regardless of order, and finite spectra witness sharpness.

papers.title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss

315.explainer: L2-Betti numbers measure homology of an infinite cover 'per unit of group'. Singer predicted that for aspherical manifolds all of it sits in the middle dimension; in dimension 4 that reduces, by duality, to showing the first L2-Betti number is zero. The paper proves that for every 4-dimensional Poincare duality group with a finite model.
315.caveats: 45 pages for a well-known open case; proof is combinatorial-group-theoretic (interval/annular chain arguments) rather than analytic. Applies directly to the PD4 complex of family 305. No Lean.
315.summary: Proves that the L²-Betti numbers of the universal cover of every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold vanish outside degree two. More generally, the same conclusion holds for every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, proving the four-dimensional Singer conjecture in this wider class.

papers.title: The Singer conjecture in dimension four

316.explainer: The Hurewicz map asks which homology classes of the infinite loop space QS^0 come from actual maps of spheres. Curtis conjectured only the famous Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire classes do. The proof follows the successive adjoints of a single stable class and shows any other spherical class would force a forbidden Steenrod/Dyer-Lashof pattern.
316.caveats: 37 pages for a 50-year-old conjecture; depends on HHR for the finiteness corollary. No Lean.
316.summary: Proves Curtis’s conjecture: the positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.

papers.title: The Stable Hurewicz Image of the Sphere at Two

317.explainer: Thomason showed ordinary small categories model all homotopy types; the conjecture asks the same for strict n-categories with every n. The missing ingredient was that categorical pushouts along certain maps behave homotopically like pushouts of nerves; the paper proves this for all dimensions, and the whole statement is machine-checked.
317.caveats: Lean: OAI.Thomason.main and OAI.Thomason.nerveDetection_allDimensions (OAI/CategoryTheory/Thomason/RankedFaithfulness.lean:683; 225 files, ~160k lines, no sorry). Impressive if the Comparator statement faithfully encodes strict omega-categories and orientals. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
317.summary: Resolves the Ara–Maltsiniotis conjecture: for every n ≥ 1 and n = ω, small strict globular n-categories admit proper combinatorial Thomason model structures Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Thus strict higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every stated dimension.

papers.title: Thomason Model Structures in Every Strict Higher Dimension

318.explainer: Chromatic splitting predicted that the 'overlap' between adjacent chromatic layers of the sphere is a simple wedge of shifted local spheres. The release shows that at height 3 a natural rational map that would vanish on the predicted wedge does not vanish on the real thing, so the prediction fails, while a weaker filtered version holds for large primes.
318.caveats: Five papers, 372 pages; mixed positive and negative results. The rational obstruction paper (49 pp) is the cleanest; the finite-assembly failure at p = 3 is a different (module-category) question than the classical conjecture. No Lean.
318.summary: Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes p ≥ 5, and weak splitting for the derived p-completed sphere at heights p (p ≥ 5) and p+1 (p ≥ 7). Nevertheless, for n ≥ 1 and p > n+1, the overlap Lₙ₋₁L_(K(n))Sₚ^∧ admits a 2ⁿ-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces. At height three and prime three, even finite assembly from such pieces fails in the category of E(2)-local modules over the derived completed sphere.

papers.title: Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes
The height-three chromatic overlap: an explicit filtration and its attachments
A rational obstruction to strong chromatic splitting at height three
Failure of finite assembly for a chromatic overlap at the prime three
Counterexamples to weak chromatic splitting: sphere kernels and descent exponents

319.explainer: fp-type spectra are those whose mod-p cohomology is finitely presented over the Steenrod algebra; Hahn and Wilson conjectured they are all finitely built from truncated Brown-Peterson spectra. The paper builds an exotic one by gluing pieces along an operator with many independent defects, then shows no finite construction can produce it.
319.caveats: Only 'sufficiently large p'; depends on 'the specified standard form' of BP<2>. 79 pages. No Lean.
319.summary: Refutes the Hahn–Wilson conjecture at chromatic height two. For every sufficiently large prime p, constructs a connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two that cannot be built from completed BP⟨2⟩ by finitely many sums, shifts, cones and retracts. The examples nevertheless satisfy the finite and telescopic localization comparisons.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height two

320.explainer: The Borel conjecture says an aspherical manifold is determined by its fundamental group; it is known in high dimensions for hyperbolic groups. In dimension 4 surgery needs 'good' groups, and family 305 claims free groups aren't good. Here a Poincare chamber whose cyclic d-fold covers have marked fillings only for even d gives two manifolds with the same homotopy type that can't be homeomorphic: a parity (odd-cycle 2-colouring) argument on red/blue plumbing caps does the work.
320.caveats: Imports the marked tensor obstruction (family 305) and the PD4 realization machinery as black boxes ('principal inputs ... [MT, Theorem 5.1], [PD, Sections 3-5]'); so it is only as solid as 305. The combinatorial core (odd-cycle colouring argument) is checkable. 60 pages. No Lean.
320.summary: Constructs closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group. This disproves even the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.

papers.title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds with the same homotopy type

321.explainer: Wall asked whether a 3-complex that 'looks 2-dimensional' to every cohomology test is homotopy equivalent to a genuine 2-complex. The paper's trick: on a finite 2-complex, if a rank-one twisted second homology vanishes, the twisting character must be trivial on every element of finite order (a Howie-style tower of infinite cyclic covers forces a strictly growing but bounded simplex count). Then it writes down a five-generator, four-relator group and a perfect normal subgroup, applies Quillen's plus construction to get a D(2) 3-complex, and exhibits an order-2 element with character value -1 while the twisted H_2 vanishes, which no 2-complex allows.
321.caveats: Only 9 pages of mathematics and fully elementary. I re-derived the key computation: the four relators hold under the character rho (x1->-1, a1->zeta, x2->zeta^2, a2->-1, s->1), the Fox-derivative matrix matches (15), and the minor on columns (x1,a1,x2,s) equals -4(1-zeta^2) != 0 numerically; I also re-checked the perfectness argument for K and the logic of the tower obstruction (Thm 2.2). I found no gap. Caveat: the most-studied form of the D(2) problem is for finite fundamental groups, which remains open; this counterexample has infinite pi_1.
321.summary: Constructs a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex whose universal cover has no integral homology above degree two and whose third cohomology vanishes for every local coefficient module, but which has no finite two-dimensional homotopy model. This disproves Wall's finite D(2) conjecture; the example has infinite fundamental group.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Wall's D(2) Problem

322.explainer: Mazur-Ulam says distance-preserving maps between normed spaces are affine; Tingley asked whether knowing only the unit sphere's metric already pins down the whole space linearly. The answer is yes in complete generality. The proof measures the worst error in preserving distances between different radii, realizes a hypothetical positive maximal defect in an ultrapower-type enlargement, propagates extremal aligned chords through common supporting functionals to an invariant convex set, applies Darbo's fixed-point theorem, and derives a contradiction from convexity.
322.caveats: Remarkably short (12 pp.) for a 39-year-old problem, but the full statement is Lean-checked against Mathlib definitions, which substantially raises confidence (residual risk lies only in the faithfulness of the comparator statement, which reads correctly). Real-linear only for complex spaces (standard). Paper 324 in the same release cites this result for comparison but does not depend on it. No public expert reaction found.
322.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/TingleySphereIsometry.lean: for complete nontrivial real normed spaces and an isometric surjection of unit spheres, there is a linear isometric equivalence agreeing with f on the sphere, given by the radial formula, unique among real-linear extensions.
322.summary: Resolves Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. No dimension restriction is imposed, so the metric geometry of the unit sphere determines the Banach space up to linear isometry.

papers.title: A positive solution to Tingley’s problem

323.explainer: Every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a small (separable) infinite-dimensional subspace, but whether it always has a small infinite-dimensional quotient is a decades-old question. The answer depends on set theory: under CH, a Gowers-Maurey/James-tree style dual space with path functionals coded by countable ordinals, combined with a perturbed predual, has no separable infinite-dimensional quotient; if instead the continuum carries a real-valued measure, Fubini-type arguments extract an unconditional basic sequence in the dual, which forces such a quotient.
323.caveats: Kind recorded as 'proof' (an independence result is a full answer in the usual relative sense), though only the CH half is Lean-checked. Not a ZFC answer: independence is relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal (equiconsistent with a real-valued measurable c), so 'independent of ZFC' is in the standard relative sense. kind='partial' reflects that the problem is settled only as independence and only half is formally verified; one could also call it a full resolution.
323.lean: partial formalization — ComparatorChallenges/SeparableQuotientNegative.lean proves only the CH direction: CH (#R = aleph_1) implies failure of SQ over both R and C (OAI/Analysis/SeparableQuotients/Main.lean:9, 76 files, ~18.2k lines, no sorry, standard axioms).
323.summary: Establishes, relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal, that the separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC. The assertion that every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient can hold for all real and complex Banach spaces, whereas the continuum hypothesis yields counterexamples over both fields.

papers.title: Relative independence of the separable quotient problem

324.explainer: If two Banach spaces are the same metric space up to bounded distortion, must they be the same linear space? Aharoni-Lindenstrauss showed no for huge nonseparable spaces in 1978; the separable case was a central open problem of nonlinear Banach space theory. The construction builds a nearly isometric non-linear change of variables on a Hilbert space whose nonlinear part has 'locally orthogonal' high coordinates, linearizes it on the Lipschitz-free space (making it completely continuous), and assembles graph spaces in which one side contains c_0(l_2) and the other provably does not.
324.caveats: Real scalars only; no reflexive or complex analogue claimed. The obstruction is block-valued (c_0(l_2), not c_0). Cites the same-release Tingley result only for comparison. Consistent with known positive results (c_0(l_2) is separable, so it linearly embeds in Y** by Heinrich-Mankiewicz/Godefroy-Kalton-type arguments, which the construction does not contradict). No public expert reaction found.
324.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/LipschitzEquivalence.lean states separable complete real X,Y, an equivalence with the explicit 4/21 and 76/25 bounds, no continuous linear equivalence, an isometric embedding of c_0(l_2) into X and no bounded-below linear map from c_0(l_2) into Y…
324.summary: Constructs separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic, resolving the separable Lipschitz-isomorphism problem negatively. Thus even the complete metric structure up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence does not determine a separable Banach space's linear isomorphism class.

papers.title: Lipschitz Equivalent Separable Banach Spaces Need Not Be Linearly Isomorphic
Bi-Lipschitz Absorption of c0 Without a Linear Copy of c0

325.explainer: Crouzeix asked whether the numerical range W(A) (all values u*Au over unit vectors) controls polynomials of a non-normal matrix as well as the spectrum controls normal ones, up to a factor 2. The scalar case fell in summer 2026; this result proves the stronger 'complete' form where polynomial coefficients are themselves matrices, which is what operator-algebra theory (Paulsen/Arveson) needs: it says one similarity of condition number <= 2 turns the conformal image of A into a contraction. The direct proof expands the Cauchy kernel of an exterior conformal map in Faber polynomials, uses a nonnegative kernel K=1+s+conj(s) to bound coefficient norms between weights 1 and 2, and compares two diagonal functionals built from F*G and G*F so that non-commuting coefficients never need to commute.
325.caveats: The headline 'Crouzeix conjecture' (scalar) was solved by humans+AI in July-Aug 2026, ~2 months before this release; the new content is the COMPLETE (matrix-valued coefficients, any base dimension, infinite-dimensional) version, which the scalar papers explicitly left open and which was known only for n<=3 (Ahag-Czyz-Virtanen). The structural paper cites those preprints, so the novelty claim is the complete case, honestly stated in the papers.
325.lean: main theorem formalized — DirectCrouzeix.lean (OAI.DirectCrouzeix.complete_crouzeix, uniform_sharpness), CompleteCrouzeix.lean, CrouzeixHilbert.lean (OAI.CrouzeixHilbert.hilbert: arbitrary complex Hilbert space incl.
325.summary: Resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture: for every bounded operator A on a complex Hilbert space and every finite matrix-valued polynomial P, one has ‖ P[A]‖ ≤ 2sup_(z ∈ W(A))‖ P(z)‖, where W(A) is the numerical range. The constant 2 is sharp, independent of the matrix size, and valid in infinite dimensions.

papers.title: A direct proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality
The complete Crouzeix theorem: optimal similarity and a common positive boundary representation

326.explainer: Type and cotype measure how random +-1 sums of vectors grow; K-convexity is the property that lets type and cotype dualize cleanly, and Pisier showed it is the same as 'no uniformly embedded copies of l1^n'. The question was whether finite cotype of a space and of its dual already forces it, given some approximation structure. The proof shows Walsh transforms of finite-rank operators decay at a rate independent of rank (via 'moment lifts' and a Fourier lemma over F_2 using rank-2 binary-matrix indices), then transfers that decay to the identity of X through compact factorizations supplied by AP; uniform l1^n copies would contradict the decay.
326.caveats: Restricted to spaces with AP (necessarily: false without it) and real scalars. Proves under ordinary AP what was conjectured even under BAP, so stronger than the Gupta-Misra-Ray formulation. Entropy-duality corollary relies on the announced AMSTJ04 Theorem 5 (bounded K-convexity constant implies duality) and E. Milman 2007 derivation. Consistent with family 329 (counterexample uses cube, i.e. l_infinity^n, which has no uniform cotype). No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06.
326.lean: main theorem formalized — Cotype.lean, OAI.Cotype.mainTarget_proved: for nontrivial complete real X, AP -> (KConvex <-> FiniteCotype X and FiniteCotype X*); K-convexity, cotype, AP defined from scratch on finite sign cubes. Solution OAI/Analysis/Cotype (~11.8k lines, 125 files) has no sorry/axiom by grep.
326.summary: Resolves the cotype–cotype conjecture for real Banach spaces with the approximation property. Such a nonzero space is K-convex if and only if both it and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, with possibly different exponents. Equivalently, these cotype assumptions force nontrivial Rademacher type.

papers.title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property

327.explainer: Markov type asks whether a random walk mapped into a space spreads like a diffusive walk (distance^p growing at most linearly in time); it is a purely metric property. The result shows that only 'uniformly round' (superreflexive) spaces have it nontrivially, closing a Ribe-program question. Proof: if X is not superreflexive, James-Enflo yields a spreading norm in which merging adjacent coordinates is contractive; in it one builds finite reversible chains whose odd edge labels sum, with constant probability, to a vector of norm proportional to time n (via reduced words acting on the line), which violates Markov type p>1.
327.caveats: Short (14 pp) and uses classical inputs (James-Enflo finite representability, Brunel-Sucheston spreading/ESA norms, finite Ramsey). Real scalars only. Answers a Ribe-program question that experts considered natural; the mechanism (a reversible walk with linear displacement in any non-superreflexive space) is concrete and plausible. Lean formalization of the full iff substantially increases confidence. No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06; HN threads have essentially no discussion yet).
327.lean: main theorem formalized — MarkovType.lean, OAI.MarkovSuperreflexivity.hasNontrivialMarkovType_iff_hasEquivalentUCNorm (complete real normed X): Markov type over finite reversible chains on Fin m with explicit path weights <-> equivalent uniformly convex seminorm-norm.
327.summary: Proves that every real Banach space with Markov type p for some p > 1 admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, answering Naor's renorming question. Together with the known converse, this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type.

papers.title: Nontrivial Markov Type Forces Superreflexivity

328.explainer: Banach's fixed-point theorem needs strict contractions; for maps that merely do not increase distances, existence of a fixed point depends on the geometry of the space. Since 1965 it was known for uniformly convex spaces and under 'normal structure', and the central open question was whether reflexivity alone suffices. The proof assumes a minimal fixed-point-free invariant set, where approximate fixed points are almost diametral, and builds a tree of convex combinations of approximate-fixed-point images whose telescoping differences produce a vector detected by functionals along an infinite branch that must also tend weakly to zero, contradicting weak compactness.
328.caveats: Calling this 'landmark' is conditional on the Lean proof checking (I could not build it); the statement in the comparator is faithful. Prior claimed proofs (Hanebaly) were not accepted, so independent expert scrutiny of the 19-page argument matters. The proof is a contradiction argument from a minimal invariant set (Goebel-Karlovitz diametral approximate fixed points) via an adaptive anchor, compact families of predicted outputs and a weighted telescoping estimate on a tree; this is new machinery, not a classical reduction.
328.lean: main theorem formalized — ReflexiveFixedPoints.lean, OAI.ReflexiveFixedPoints.exists_fixedPoint_of_canonicallyReflexive: complete real normed X with surjective canonical map into the bidual, C nonempty closed bounded convex, F: C->C 1-Lipschitz => fixed point. Statement is exactly the problem.
328.summary: Resolves Kirk's reflexive-space fixed-point problem: every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. The result uses the original norm, without assuming uniform convexity.

papers.title: Fixed Points of Nonexpansive Maps in Reflexive Banach Spaces
