329.explainer: Covering numbers measure how many translates of one convex body it takes to cover another; the conjecture said this complexity is essentially unchanged (up to universal constants) when both bodies are replaced by their polars, a geometric form of 'an operator and its adjoint have comparable entropy numbers'. The counterexample builds a 0-1-ish matrix whose rows are far apart in sup norm (large primal entropy) while the convex hull of its columns has a short uniform approximation list (small dual entropy), using partitions coming from symmetric h-linear forms over a large finite field and log-distance profiles in partition graphs.
329.caveats: Disproves the fully general dimension-free conjecture; does not contradict AMS04 (Euclidean-ball case) or the K-convex case (and is consistent with family 326's corollary, which proves duality under cotype bounds; the cube is far from K-convex). Dimensions grow with a,b, nothing said about fixed dimension. Construction uses symmetric multilinear forms over F_p and Schwartz-Zippel; mostly combinatorial and formalized, so high plausibility. No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06.
329.lean: main theorem formalized — MetricEntropyDuality.lean, OAI.MetricEntropyDuality.exists_entropy_duality_counterexample_with_covers: for all a,b>=1 there is K in positive finite dimension with log N(K,B_inf) > b log N(B_inf°, a^{-1}K°) (N = least number of translates).
329.summary: Disproves Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy. Origin-symmetric convex bodies violate every proposed choice of universal constants in the conjectured comparison between covering numbers and those of the polar bodies, even when the covering body is a cube.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the duality conjecture for metric entropy

330.explainer: Lipschitz-free spaces linearize metric spaces: each point becomes a vector and Lipschitz maps become linear operators, so Banach-space properties of F(M) encode metric geometry. Kalton asked whether points being uniformly separated forces the approximating finite-rank operators to have bounded norms. The answer is no: blocks built from large-degree graphs with random-like colourings and finitely many 'anchor' points force any finite-rank operator of norm <= p to move some anchor by 1/2; wedging blocks for all p at a common basepoint gives AP (finitely many blocks at a time) but no uniform bound.
330.caveats: Answers Kalton's question negatively; the human result of Smith (2025-26) already gave the discrete (not uniformly discrete) version, so this is the sharpened form. The equivalent-norm-on-l1-failing-MAP corollary is a nice standalone answer. Space is necessarily non-proper. No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06; HN threads have essentially no discussion yet).
330.lean: main theorem formalized — DiscreteLipschitzFree.lean (OAI.DiscreteFree.source_endpoints: block statement + uniformly discrete countable M with AP and no BAP) and RealL1Renorming.lean (quantitative l1 renorming). Solution OAI/Analysis/LipschitzFree (~4.6k lines), no sorry/axiom by grep.
330.summary: Constructs a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free Banach space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively. Finite-rank operators approximate the identity on every compact set, but their norms cannot share a finite bound.

papers.title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces

331.explainer: AUC norms gain length uniformly when you move in any far-out direction; AMUC only requires a gain when you test a direction and its opposite together. Which of these can be achieved by renorming is a question in the nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces, tied to whether 'diamond graphs' embed with bounded distortion. The new reflexive example uses James-style square sums over disjoint tree segments on countably branching trees of growing heights: long root paths kill any AUC renorming, while a corrected norming test at the first exit vertices proves the midpoint gain and hence the diamond distortion lower bound.
331.caveats: The overview summary is garbled: it says 'midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion', but AMUC is already known to PREVENT uniform diamond embeddings; the actual new point is that failure of AUC-renormability does not force uniform diamond embeddings even for reflexive spaces (negative answer to the reflexive diamond converse, Baudier-Lancien Problem 39). The non-reflexive separation was obtained by Baudier five days before the earliest OpenAI paper.
331.lean: main theorem formalized — ForestSpace.lean (OAI.ForestSpace.main_theorem: reflexive, separable, AMUC modulus bound, no equivalent AUC norm, diamond distortion >= sqrt(1+k/12)); also MidpointLenses, DiamondDistortion (headline_all_pairs, unconditional.
331.summary: Constructs a real reflexive Banach space with an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, extending Baudier's separation to reflexive spaces. In the same space, depth-k countably branching diamonds require distortion at least √(1+k/12), so midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion even under reflexivity.

papers.title: Asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity and unbounded diamond distortion in a reflexive tree space
Midpoint lenses in segment spaces
Distortion of countably branching diamonds from midpoint and tree energies
Exact asymptotic moduli in a Daugavet subspace of L1
Midpoint convexity from bounded tree potentials and path costs
Independent products in real L1: asymptotic midpoint convexity without AUC renormings
Midpoint convexity from two recursive potentials

332.explainer: Extending Lipschitz maps (keeping the stretch factor under control) is a basic problem in metric geometry; Ball reduced it to two random-walk inequalities, one for the source and one for the target. The open case was l1 as target, where the natural linear averaging fails. The proof writes finite l1 configurations as weighted cuts (binary vectors in a Hilbert space), averages them along a geometrically stopped random walk, applies the cubic phi(r)=3r^2-2r^3 coordinatewise (flat at 0 and 1), and maps back; a quartic Hilbert potential and martingale identity control both the approximation cost and the one-step variation, so each new point is an expected coordinatewise median of three walk endpoints.
332.caveats: Only 9 pages and elementary (cut decomposition of finite l1 subsets, cubic smoothing, a fourth-power martingale potential), which makes it quick for experts to check; not formalized. The extension consequence is quoted from Mendel-Naor rather than reproved. Shares the nonlinear cut-smoothing idea with a human preprint from one month earlier (Cheng-Wang-Xiang), which the paper credits. Published Oct 5 2026, the day before release, so least time for internal review. No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06.
332.lean: none — no lean/docs/332.md and no matching file in lean/.
332.summary: Proves that real ℓ₁ has metric Markov cotype two, answering Mendel and Naor's question. Consequently, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into ℓ₁ extends to the whole space with a universal multiplicative loss in its Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.

papers.title: Metric Markov Cotype Two of ℓ₁

333.explainer: Can every abstract smooth surface metric be realized by a smooth (self-intersecting) surface in 4-dimensional space? Gromov did it in 5 dimensions. The paper starts with any immersion into a small round 3-sphere in R^4 (so the starting map is 'short'), then adds oscillatory rank-one corrections to make up the missing metric, keeping a usable normal direction and smoothing to control derivative loss.
333.caveats: Lean: OAI.ClosedSurfaceR4.FiniteOrderSmoothing.smooth_isometric_immersion (OAI/Geometry/SurfaceImmersion/Main.lean:16), 2050 files ~175k lines, no sorry. Immersion, not embedding. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
333.summary: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ⁴, resolving the closed-surface form of the four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem. This includes nonorientable surfaces and metrics of arbitrary Gaussian curvature.

papers.title: Smooth isometric immersions of closed surfaces into Euclidean four-space

334.explainer: Can every smooth surface metric be realized, near a point, as a piece of a smooth surface in ordinary 3-space? Analytic metrics yes; the smooth case was open. The paper glues infinitely many shrinking patches where the curvature changes sign and shows any immersion would give a height function obeying the Darboux equation that a boundary-saddle argument rules out on one of the patches.
334.caveats: Lean: OAI.SmoothLocal.Geometry.exists_local_metric_without_local_immersion (OAI/Geometry/IsometricImmersion/Main.lean:49), 447 files ~57k lines. Uses both signs of curvature, so it does not settle the problem under K >= 0 or K <= 0. Prior-status ambiguity (Nadirashvili-Yuan preprint) acknowledged by the paper itself. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
334.summary: Constructs a smooth positive-definite metric on (-1,1)² for which no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ³. This answers the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces negatively, even after shrinking the neighborhood.

papers.title: A Smooth Metric with No Local Isometric Immersion into Three-Space

335.explainer: A metric of positive scalar curvature makes small balls slightly smaller than Euclidean ones; the conjecture says aspherical manifolds (like tori and hyperbolic manifolds, which are 'large') can never carry such metrics. Earlier proofs used Dirac operators (needing spin) or minimal surfaces (limited to dims <= 5). The paper instead turns the group-cohomology class into a map of nonzero degree to a sphere on a fibred cover and then repeatedly reshapes the metric (adding warped circles) to shrink that map while paying only a logarithmic scalar-curvature cost, until a torical obstruction of Cecchini-Schick is violated.
335.caveats: 121 pages total. The quantitative bound depends on the rational-inessentiality paper. The method (graph deformations with one warped circle per coordinate and a telescoping trace bound) is new and analysis-heavy; correctness hinges on the logarithmic-in-q scalar cost estimate. Family 336 gives an independent proof of the aspherical corollary for n >= 4 via width, which is a weak consistency check (same model). No Lean.
335.summary: Proves ∫_M(Scal_g⁻)^(n/2) dV_g ≥ aₙ‖ M‖ for every closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 3, and every smooth metric, with aₙ > 0 depending only on dimension. Here Scal_g⁻=max{0,-Scal_g} and ‖ M‖ is real simplicial volume. Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov–Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.

papers.title: An integral scalar curvature bound for real simplicial volume
Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality

336.explainer: Positive scalar curvature should make a manifold 'thin in two directions': you can squash it onto a lower-dimensional skeleton (two dimensions lower) with uniformly bounded fibres. The papers prove this in every dimension, also under the weaker spectral condition that appears in Ricci-flow and Kaluza-Klein settings.
336.caveats: 147 pages over three papers; the spectral 3-d paper gives an explicit constant 500. No Lean. The macroscopic-dimension corollary is the 'continuous' version (distinct from the Lipschitz/uniform version, as the paper notes).
336.summary: Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying -4Δ+Scal ≥ 1 as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most n-2 whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by n in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most n-2 for every n ≥ 2.

papers.title: Spectral scalar curvature and uniform Urysohn width
Spectral scalar curvature and Urysohn width in dimension three
Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width

337.explainer: In flat space the round ball is the best way to enclose volume. Cartan-Hadamard says that in any simply connected space that curves 'outward' (nonpositively), you can't do better than flat space; it was known only in dimensions 2, 3 and 4. The CAT(0) paper proves an even more general sharp filling inequality for integral currents in singular nonpositively curved spaces, and the main theorem of that paper is machine-checked.
337.caveats: Lean: OAI.CAT0Fillings.sharp_integral_filling (OAI/Geometry/CAT0Fillings/Main.lean:111; 330 files ~50.5k lines) and coefficient optimality (OAI/Geometry/IntegralFillings/Main.lean:60). The Comparator file defines metric currents, mass, integer-rectifiability and CAT(0) from scratch (my reading: the CAT(0) inequality is the correct comparison formula; the current definitions look reasonable but are bespoke and unreviewed, e.g. Jacobians via fderivWithin on Borel chart domains).
337.summary: Proves generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for κ = 0 are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral n-cycles, n ≥ 2, in arbitrary proper CAT(0) spaces.

papers.title: Generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and Euclidean equality rigidity
Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces

338.explainer: Yau conjectured that positive 'complex' curvature on a complete noncompact Kaehler manifold forces it to be plain C^n, the noncompact analogue of the Frankel conjecture. Earlier proofs needed maximal volume growth. The paper runs Kaehler-Ricci flow, proves a Harnack inequality for it with no curvature bound by minimizing a norm over holomorphic discs, and uses a 'volume clock' to build shrinking charts whose transition maps are controlled well enough to cover all of C^n.
338.caveats: 77 pages, no Lean. Constructs a Kaehler-Ricci flow from an initial metric with unbounded curvature and possible collapsing, a regime where standard existence theory fails; the scalar comparison 'before completeness is known' and the disc-infimum viscosity argument for the Harnack inequality are the critical new steps. Note the paper's own footnote: prior partial progress already used ChatGPT assistance.
338.summary: Proves Yau's uniformization conjecture: every complete connected noncompact Kähler manifold with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to ℂⁿ.

papers.title: Uniformization of complete Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature

339.explainer: On a negatively curved manifold, two natural ways to pick a 'random geodesic' (by volume, and by maximal complexity) agree on hyperbolic and other symmetric spaces. Katok conjectured they agree only there. The proof shows that equality forces the stable and unstable foliations of the geodesic flow to be smooth, after which a classical theorem identifies the flow with a symmetric one.
339.caveats: 66 pages; ends with Benoist-Foulon-Labourie after proving global smoothness of the stable/unstable distributions; heavy formal normal-form and Cartan-Guillemin classification of transitive Lie pseudo-algebras. No Lean.
339.summary: Proves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture for closed connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with strictly negative sectional curvature: normalized Liouville measure maximizes entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric.

papers.title: Entropy equality and local symmetry in negative curvature

340.explainer: The conjecture says the only exact Lagrangians in a cotangent bundle are the obvious ones, the zero section moved around by Hamiltonian flows; a decade of Floer-theoretic work showed such an L must be homotopy-, then simple-homotopy-equivalent to the base. The paper uses the finer invariant of generating-function 'tube' spaces, connected to Waldhausen's algebraic K-theory, to build an L that is even diffeomorphic to the base yet carries a nontrivial tube class the zero section does not.
340.caveats: Only 28 pages to disprove a central conjecture of symplectic topology, with a non-explicit 'sufficiently large even N'. The obstruction (a nonzero stable tube class / Waldhausen-K-theory torsion) must survive the passage from Legendrians in J^1Q to embedded Lagrangians in T*Q; the paper claims to separate all coincident cotangent branches. Lean: in-progress files under OAI/Geometry/NearbyLagrangian (93 files) but no catalogued main result. Highest-risk landmark in this group by length-to-claim ratio.
340.summary: Disproves the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture. For some sufficiently large even N, constructs a closed exact embedded Lagrangian in T*(S⁹× S^(N-1)) that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to its zero section.

papers.title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture

341.explainer: A hypersymplectic structure is three symplectic forms that 'look like' a hyperkaehler triple but needn't be parallel. Donaldson conjectured you can always deform it to a true hyperkaehler one without changing cohomology classes; since compact hyperkaehler 4-manifolds are K3 or tori, this pins down the topology. The paper combines the positive-current estimates of the tamed-to-compatible proof with a continuity/deformation argument.
341.caveats: 72 pages; builds on the current estimates of family 342 (which is formalized) but the prescribed-class deformation arguments are not formalized. The K3/T^4 corollary is a striking topological consequence (smooth classification) that experts would test first.
341.summary: Proves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture in a cohomology-preserving form. Every positive triple of smooth closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold, normalized by ∫ωᵢ∧ωⱼ=δᵢⱼ, deforms through positive closed triples to a hyperkähler triple while preserving all three cohomology classes. Any positive triple can first be normalized by a constant linear change.

papers.title: Deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkähler triples

342.explainer: A symplectic form 'tames' J if it is positive on every J-complex line; it is 'compatible' if, in addition, it is J-invariant. Averaging a taming form makes it invariant but destroys closedness. Donaldson asked whether a compatible closed form must nonetheless exist. If not, Hahn-Banach gives a positive current that kills all closed invariant forms; the paper shows such a current, after an elliptic correction, would have to be closed on its positive-density part and then forces the correction to vanish, contradicting the existence of the taming form.
342.caveats: Only 18 pages, but the main theorem is formalized: OAI.TamingCompatibility.taming_implies_compatibility (OAI/Geometry/TamingCompatibility/Main.lean:30; Comparator statement ComparatorChallenges/TamingCompatibility.lean:58), 582 files ~83.6k lines, no sorry, standard axioms. I read the Comparator statement: it defines smooth/closed 2-forms via pullbacks along smooth chart maps, taming, J-invariance and compatibility in the expected way on a compact connected T2 second-countable smooth 4-manifold; it looks faithful.
342.summary: Proves Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible symplectic form. The almost complex structure stays fixed; the form's cohomology class may change.

papers.title: Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds

343.explainer: In 4 dimensions packing balls symplectically is governed by intricate algebraic-geometry obstructions; in 6 and up, Siegel and Yao conjectured only volume and Gromov's two-ball non-squeezing matter. The paper constructs the packings explicitly (folding/surface-packing comparison) and the result is machine-checked.
343.caveats: Lean: OAI.HigherDimensionalBallPacking.main_theorem (OAI/Geometry/BallPacking, 207 files ~107k lines) plus necessity; Comparator statement (ComparatorChallenges/BallPacking.lean) defines symplectic embeddings via derivatives preserving the standard form on an open neighbourhood; reads faithfully. Fails in dim 4 (more obstructions), as stated. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
343.summary: Resolves the Siegel–Yao conjecture for arbitrary capacities in every dimension 2n ≥ 6. Finitely many closed symplectic balls of capacities R₁,…,Rₖ embed disjointly into an open ball of capacity R exactly when ∑ᵢRᵢⁿ < Rⁿ and Rᵢ+Rⱼ < R for every distinct pair i, j.

papers.title: Symplectic Ball Packings in Higher Dimensions

344.explainer: On a round sphere every geodesic is minimizing until it reaches the antipode; Blaschke asked whether only the compact rank-one symmetric spaces have this 'all geodesics close up at the same time' property metrically. Spheres and RP^n were done by 1980 via Kazdan's inequality; the paper extends the volume-comparison method to the projective cases, then upgrades equal volume to isometry.
344.caveats: 41 pages, uses Schur-complement Jacobi-determinant comparisons plus a Kazdan-type inequality; 'the homeomorphism hypothesis in the result recorded by Wilking ... will be verified at their uses' is a step worth checking. No Lean.
344.summary: Proves the metric Blaschke conjecture: every closed connected Riemannian manifold of positive dimension whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scaling, a standard compact rank-one symmetric space.

papers.title: The metric Blaschke theorem

345.explainer: Does every metric on a sphere have infinitely many closed geodesics? For the 2-sphere yes (1990s); in higher dimensions it was known only for generic metrics. The difficulty is distinguishing genuinely new geodesics from repeated traversals of old ones when the metric is degenerate. The proof uses a cut construction ('native cut') and degree-interval arguments in loop-space Morse theory to force new prime geodesics.
345.caveats: 50 pages; the S^n (n >= 3) case is a famous open problem for degenerate metrics; the paper criticizes a competing claim (Charles), so expert adjudication is needed. The 3-manifold statement relies on topology (most 3-manifolds have infinite pi_1 or are spherical space forms) plus the sphere case. No Lean.
345.summary: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on Sⁿ, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.

papers.title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on every Riemannian sphere

346.explainer: Stationary integral varifolds are the most general 'soap films': weak minimal surfaces allowed to have multiplicity and singularities. Allard showed the regular part is dense; whether the singular part can have positive area has been open for 50 years because higher multiplicity breaks his theorem. The papers use measure-valued blow-ups that keep height and slope information and a unique-continuation upgrade to show singular points are negligible, indeed of codimension at least one.
346.caveats: 112 pages over two papers; this is one of the central open problems of geometric measure theory, so the burden is high. A single-file Lean stub (OAI/Geometry/Varifold/NullComparison.lean) exists but no main result is formalized. Two papers dated Sept 23 and Oct 5, the second strengthening to the sharp dimension bound.
346.summary: Proves that every stationary integral m-varifold in a Euclidean open set has singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most m-1, a sharp bound in every positive dimension and codimension. On round spheres, the family also proves almost-everywhere regularity: the singular set has zero m-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

papers.title: A Codimension-One Bound for the Singular Set of a Stationary Integral Varifold
Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds

347.explainer: Arnold conjectured a Hamiltonian map has at least as many fixed points as a function has critical points. The homological version is a theorem (Floer theory); the stronger topological versions were open. The release gives an explicit degenerate example on the 6-dimensional quadric with 3 fixed points where every function needs 4 critical points, and nondegenerate families where integral torsion inflates the stable Morse number beyond the fixed-point count.
347.caveats: Five papers (87 pp). Lean formalizes only the degenerate quadric example (OAI.ArnoldCounterexample.main, OAI/Geometry/Arnold/Main.lean:14, 36 files ~5.9k lines). These refute strong/unrestricted variants while the standard homological Arnold conjecture stands. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
347.summary: Disproves stable-Morse lower bounds for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points: on simply connected closed Kähler manifolds of real dimension 22, the deficit below the stable Morse number is unbounded. A separate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold has exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points required of every smooth function.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number in Dimension Twenty-Two
Sharpness of the Cyclic Integral Floer Bound Below the Stable Morse Number
Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number
A nondegenerate counterexample to the Morse-number Arnold bound
Three fixed points on the symplectic quadric threefold

348.explainer: Which 4-manifolds carry Einstein metrics with positive sectional curvature? Only the obvious symmetric ones were known; proofs needed extra pinching or topology. The paper shows one of the two Weyl curvature blocks must vanish by balancing their second moments and an exact polynomial inequality, then identifies the symmetric model. The positive-curvature statement is machine-checked.
348.caveats: Lean: positive-sectional classification only (OAI.PositiveEinsteinFour.classification, OAI/Geometry/EinsteinFour/Classification.lean:13; 408 files ~209k lines). The sec >= 0 extension (zero-plane rigidity) and the L^2 gap (which explicitly takes the classification as a 'Classification Assumption 1.1') are not formalized. The paper itself relies on 'exact polynomial certificates' with an accompanying checker; the Lean proof subsumes those. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
348.summary: Classifies closed connected Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature: up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round S⁴, Fubini–Study ℂℙ², or a product of equal round two-spheres. A closed simply connected nonnegatively curved four-manifold is diffeomorphic to one of these whenever the scale-invariant L² norm of its trace-free Ricci curvature lies below a universal positive constant.

papers.title: Zero-Plane Rigidity for Einstein Four-Manifolds
An L² Einstein Gap for Nonnegatively Curved Four-Manifolds
Positively curved Einstein four-manifolds

349.explainer: The equator is the smallest minimal hypersurface in a round sphere; the question is what comes next. Clifford tori products are the natural candidates. Marques-Neves settled surfaces via the Willmore conjecture; the paper extends the canonical-family min-max strategy to all dimensions.
349.caveats: 32 pages; uses a variational min-max family with a topological test and dimension induction ruling out singularities below the Clifford threshold; min-max regularity in high dimensions (singular sets) is the delicate point. No Lean.
349.summary: Proves the Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres. For every m ≥ 2, a closed connected minimal immersion into the unit sphere Sᵐ⁺¹ with non-totally-geodesic image has volume at least that of the smallest minimal Clifford product, counting covering multiplicity.

papers.title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume theorem

350.explainer: How long is the zero set of a high-frequency vibration mode of a surface or drum? Yau predicted it grows like the square root of the frequency on any closed manifold. The release says: true for every smooth surface, false in every dimension >= 3 for suitably wild smooth metrics (localized quasimodes glued into exact eigenfunctions concentrate huge nodal sets). Both halves are machine-checked.
350.caveats: All three directions formalized: NodalLength (OAI.SharpNodal.Main, OAI/Analysis/NodalLength/Main.lean:377), SmoothYau (sphere_three, sphere_two_torus_two), YauCounterexample (S^4 x S^1). Counterexamples are for smooth (non-analytic) metrics only; Donnelly-Fefferman remains for analytic metrics. Lower bound untouched (Logunov). Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
350.summary: Proves the sharp C√λ upper bound for nodal length on every fixed smooth closed surface, completing Yau's conjecture there. The upper bound fails for fixed smooth metrics in dimensions three and four, including metrics on S³ arbitrarily close to round. In dimension five, nodal measure can grow faster than λ^(1/2+ε₀) for some fixed ε₀ > 0, ruling out even arbitrarily small power losses.

papers.title: Sharp nodal length on smooth surfaces
Smooth counterexamples to Yau's nodal upper bound in dimensions three and four
Power-law violations of Yau's nodal upper bound

351.explainer: Ricci flow can only stop when curvature blows up; is it enough to watch the scalar curvature? The release says yes in dimension 4, by ruling out Ricci-flat ALE bubbles that would carry the blow-up, and no in high dimensions, where a doubly-warped conical singularity can blow up while scalar curvature stays bounded.
351.caveats: 118 pages across three papers; the 4d theorem relies on the companion tree inequality (Lojasiewicz-type estimate without integrability), and the high-dimensional counterexample builds on Stolarski's construction. No Lean.
351.summary: Proves that a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold extends past any finite time at which scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded. A higher-dimensional counterexample has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at its finite maximal time, disproving the unrestricted scalar-curvature extension conjecture.

papers.title: A closed Ricci flow with bounded scalar curvature and finite-time curvature blowup
Bounded scalar curvature and smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow
Path selection and an elliptic inequality on degenerating Ricci-flat trees

352.explainer: The Calabi flow is a fourth-order geometric flow meant to deform any Kaehler metric toward a canonical one; Chen conjectured it never breaks down. The paper builds a symmetric starting metric on 10-dimensional projective space whose flow develops a point singularity in finite time, even though the class contains the perfectly round Fubini-Study metric.
352.caveats: 54 pages; specific to dimension >= 10 (U(10)-symmetric reduction to an ODE/PDE in one variable). No Lean.
352.summary: Disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow by constructing a smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler metric on ℂℙ¹⁰ whose flow develops a finite-time singularity. The metric lies in the Fubini–Study class, so the failure occurs even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

papers.title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow on projective space

353.explainer: The affine maximal equation is a fourth-order cousin of the minimal surface equation, and the question is the analogue of Bernstein's theorem: must entire solutions be quadratics? Trudinger and Wang solved dimension 2 and found a singular counterexample in dimension 10. The release proves rigidity exactly in dimensions 3-9 and smooths out the dimension-10 counterexample, so the answer flips precisely at 10, like the classical Bernstein problem flips at 8.
353.caveats: Lean formalizes the dims 3-9 Euclidean-complete graph theorem (OAI.AffineBernstein.affine_bernstein, OAI/Analysis/AffineBernstein/Main.lean:18; 326 files ~41k lines); the affine-complete hypersurface extension and the dim-10 smooth example are not. Note: the formalization of a fourth-order PDE Bernstein theorem is itself remarkable. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
353.summary: Proves that every smooth locally uniformly convex affine-maximal graph of dimension three through nine, complete for its induced Euclidean metric, is an elliptic paraboloid. A smooth entire nonquadratic example in dimension ten makes this range sharp. In dimensions three through nine, the paraboloid classification also holds for connected open locally uniformly convex affine-maximal hypersurfaces complete for the affine Berwald–Blaschke metric.

papers.title: A Smooth Nonquadratic Entire Affine Maximal Graph in Dimension Ten
The affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions three through nine

354.explainer: What is the least-area way to enclose a given volume in a 3-torus made by gluing opposite faces of a cube? The 20-year-old conjecture: a ball, then a tube, then a slab. The proof excludes higher-genus minimizers using reflection symmetry and curvature-area estimates, and the full classification is machine-checked.
354.caveats: Lean: OAI.CubicTorus.unit_cubic_isoperimetric (OAI/Geometry/CubicTorus/Main.lean:1103; 162 files ~141k lines), including all equality cases. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
354.summary: Determines the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus and classifies every finite-perimeter minimizer: balls, circular tubes around shortest closed geodesics, coordinate slabs, and their complements. The transition volumes are 4π/81 and 1/π, with exactly the adjacent two types minimizing at each transition.

papers.title: The Isoperimetric Conjecture for the Cubic Flat Three-Torus

355.explainer: When a surface shrinking under mean curvature flow develops a singularity, zooming in gives a 'tangent flow', but different zoom sequences might a priori give different limits. Uniqueness was known for compact, cylindrical and conical models separately. The paper handles every possible model at the first singular time via a localized gradient (Lojasiewicz) inequality for the Gaussian area that copes with ends of different types.
355.caveats: Restricted to the first singular time and fixed centre; uniqueness for general shrinkers with mixed ends (cylindrical + conical) is what is new. 100 pages of Lojasiewicz-type analysis with Gevrey remainders and a 'finite-jet obstruction' via a Stokes constant; hard to check. No Lean.
355.summary: Proves the first-singular-time case of tangent-flow uniqueness for smooth compact connected embedded surfaces without boundary in ℝ³. At every singular point, all fixed-center backward tangent flows agree as area measures at every negative time in the original ambient coordinates, without mean-convexity or a prescribed tangent model.

papers.title: Uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of embedded surface mean-curvature flow

356.explainer: Gigli defined a curvature tensor on very singular spaces with Ricci lower bounds; he conjectured that a lower bound on that tensor exactly characterizes Alexandrov spaces (triangle comparison). The paper proves it, with a key step (Hessian bounds hold along every geodesic, not just almost every) formalized.
356.caveats: Lean formalizes only the companion weak-Hessian-along-every-geodesic theorem (OAI.WeakHessian.every_geodesic, OAI/Geometry/WeakHessian/Main.lean:38; 542 files ~66k lines), not the characterization. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
356.summary: Proves Gigli's conjecture: in every integer dimension n ≥ 2, Alexandrov curvature at least κ is characterized by the full-support RCD ((n-1)κ,n) condition with reference measure Hⁿ and distributional sectional curvature at least κ in the original global test classes. The RCD condition is unreduced.

papers.title: Gigli’s distributional curvature characterization of Alexandrov spaces
Weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic in RCD spaces

357.explainer: Spaces with lower Ricci curvature bounds can be singular, but at 'regular' points they look Euclidean under every zoom. The paper upgrades that infinitesimal statement to an actual bi-Lipschitz coordinate chart around each regular point, answering a question going back to Cheeger and Colding.
357.caveats: 43 pages; an in-progress Lean development exists (OAI/Geometry/RCD, ~2,900 files) but no catalogued main result. No external review known.
357.summary: Proves that every regular point of a noncollapsed RCD (K,n) space, for K ∈ ℝ and integer n ≥ 2, has an open neighborhood bi-Lipschitz to an open subset of ℝⁿ. Regularity requires all pointed tangents to be Euclidean, the reference measure is exactly Hⁿ, and the chart compares ambient distances with a point-dependent finite constant.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz Coordinates at Regular Points of Noncollapsed RCD Spaces

358.explainer: No conjugate points (geodesics never refocus) follows from nonpositive curvature; is the converse true at the level of which manifolds admit such metrics? The paper takes a graph manifold that Leeb showed cannot be nonpositively curved and builds a careful metric on it whose geodesics still never refocus.
358.caveats: The nonpositive-curvature obstruction is Leeb's known example; the new content is the no-conjugate-points metric. Lean: OAI.ThreeManifold.main_theorem (OAI/Geometry/ConjugatePoints/ThreeManifold.lean:260; 19 files ~25k lines). Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
358.summary: Constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. This answers negatively, already in dimension three, whether the first metric-existence property implies the second.

papers.title: A Three-Manifold Without Conjugate Points and Without a Nonpositively Curved Metric

359.explainer: In one complex dimension, negative curvature forces a simply connected surface to be the disc. In higher dimensions people hoped negative pinched curvature would force a bounded domain. The release builds a Hartogs-type tube domain in C^3 with a carefully controlled Kaehler potential: curvature pinched negative, but any bounded holomorphic map degenerates somewhere.
359.caveats: Lean formalizes the pinched threefold construction (OAI.PinchedHartogs.main_theorem with controlled_potential and metric_transfer, OAI/Geometry/Kahler/Main.lean:38; 120 files ~19k lines); companion one-sided example not formalized. The example still has two bounded coordinates; the obstruction is to a full bounded coordinate system. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'.
359.summary: Constructs a contractible domain in ℂ³ with a complete negatively pinched Kähler metric but no bounded holomorphic coordinates, disproving bounded-domain uniformization in this setting. A higher-dimensional example has sectional curvature at most −1 and only constant bounded holomorphic functions; its curvature is not bounded below.

papers.title: A negatively pinched Kähler threefold without bounded holomorphic coordinates
One-sided negative sectional curvature and the holomorphic Liouville property

360.explainer: MTW curvature is the condition that makes optimal transport maps continuous. Villani conjectured it also forces the region where geodesics stay minimizing to be convex, which earlier proofs could only show when cut points come before conjugate points. The paper handles conjugate cut points directly and derives Hoelder-regular transport.
360.caveats: Both papers' main results formalized (WeakMTWGlobalSupport: OAI/Geometry/WeakMTW/Convexity.lean:65; BiholderTransport: OAI/Analysis/BiholderTransport/Main.lean:27, 645 files ~75k lines); the docs note the finite-target local-injectivity result does not cover the paper's arbitrary-potential assertion. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
360.summary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are Hölder continuous.

papers.title: Global Support and Convex Injectivity Domains under Weak MTW
Uniform Bi-Holder Transport from Weak MTW

361.explainer: On flat R^3 the harmonic functions of polynomial growth at most k are the harmonic polynomials, (k+1)^2 of them. Yau asked whether nonnegative Ricci curvature can only reduce that count. The release builds metrics that are Euclidean near the origin but oscillate at infinity (many different tangent cones), creating more harmonic functions of a given integer growth than flat space has.
361.caveats: The metric depends on k (no single manifold violates it for all k). Lean formalizes the earlier companion's dimension-16, degree-50000 example (OAI.HarmonicCounterexample.main, OAI/Geometry/HarmonicGrowth/Main.lean:475), not the 3-dimensional theorem. Lean catalogue review status is 'unchecked'; I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
361.summary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ³ has at least (k+2)² independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count (k+1)². The metric may depend on k.

papers.title: A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
A Three-Dimensional Counterexample to Integer-Degree Harmonic Dimension Comparison

362.explainer: Vlasov-Maxwell describes a collisionless plasma: a particle density moving in the electromagnetic field it generates. Since Glassey-Strauss (1986) it was known that smooth solutions can only break down if some particles are accelerated to infinite momentum in finite time, but nobody could rule that out for large 3D data. The paper proves a signed impulse bound |V(t2)-V(t1)| <= M P sqrt(t2-t1) + A (t2-t1) P^2 log P / w for a particle at energy ~w, which makes each doubling of the maximal momentum take time >= c/log(momentum), a divergent sum, so momentum stays finite. The key step integrates the retarded (Lienard-Wiechert-type) force along source trajectories before taking absolute values in a thin angular sector, turning the worst term into a total derivative plus a receiver-acceleration error, and closes the estimate by a bootstrap that also counts how often particles change direction.
362.caveats: This is the headline PDE claim of the chunk and would resolve a ~40-year-old problem; the paper is only 49 pages and its own reasoning trace (reasoning_traces/relativistic-vlasov-maxwell.pdf, 6 pp) says the final assertion 'rests on the occupation bound, direction-count estimate, and cutoff cancellations needed to close the signed momentum bootstrap', i.e. the trace itself flags where the risk lies (it also records discovered errors, e.g. intervals too long, repaired by shortening by a factor ~M^2+A log P).
362.lean: main theorem formalized — VlasovMaxwell.lean, OAI.RVM.global_classical_solution: for admissible data (smooth, compactly supported nonnegative f0; E0,B0 smooth with all derivatives bounded, L^2, Gauss laws) there is a solution that is C^1 on t>=0, nonnegative, with E,B continuous into L^2, compact phase support on…
362.summary: Proves large-data global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional, one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. Smooth admissible initial data may be arbitrary provided the particle density is compactly supported and the electromagnetic fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives of every order; the solution remains smooth on every finite time interval.

papers.title: Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system

363.explainer: The Boltzmann equation's large-data theory (DiPerna-Lions) gives solutions that exist for all time but are so weak that it was unknown whether they are determined by their initial data. This shows they are not: from one carefully built initial gas (cold jets on a hot background, concentrated at ever smaller scales) a selection-and-compactness scheme produces two different global solutions, one in which a rare 'cap' event triggers a branching cascade of collisions that is forced to leave a nonzero trace, and one in which it does not. It is the kinetic analogue of convex-integration nonuniqueness for weak fluid solutions, but here the solutions keep entropy dissipation and, in the newer paper, exact local conservation laws.
363.caveats: The summary's headline (exact local conservation) comes from the 78-page Oct-5 paper which is NOT formalized; the formalized statement is the weaker renormalized version (still a genuine nonuniqueness theorem). Data are deliberately singular (unbounded amplitudes at shrinking spatial scales, irrational axis, annular jets), so it does not contradict uniqueness results in bounded/near-Maxwellian classes. Hard spheres, periodic box only. No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06.
363.lean: partial formalization — BoltzmannNonuniqueness.lean (OAI.BoltzmannNonuniqueness.nonuniqueness) formalizes the Sept-23 renormalized-solution paper only: two distinct global renormalized solutions, local mass + total momentum conservation, global energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities, L^1 continuity and…
363.summary: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions of the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation from the same nonnegative initial density, with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy. Both are strongly continuous in L¹ and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
Nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation

364.explainer: Deriving Boltzmann's kinetic equation from Newton's laws for many particles (Hilbert's sixth problem) was for decades only known for short times; Deng-Hani-Ma in 2024 extended it to the whole time the kinetic solution stays regular, for hard spheres. These papers extend that to realistic smooth interactions with attractive wells (where collisions take time and particles can briefly cluster) by expanding over whole interaction components rather than binary collision trees, and prove the next-order statement that fluctuations of the empirical measure are Gaussian and follow the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.
364.caveats: Conditional in the same way as Deng-Hani-Ma: assumes the Boltzmann solution exists with Gaussian bounds on [0,T]; no global Boltzmann regularity is claimed. Paper A is an extension of DHM's layered expansion to potentials (a problem DHM explicitly listed); paper B gives finite-dimensional laws only, not process-level tightness, and in whole space rather than torus. Heavy (123 pp) and unformalized; relies on DHM's hard-sphere framework (version of 18 July 2025). No public expert reaction specific to this result found (release 2026-10-06.
364.lean: none — no lean/docs/364.md and no matching file in lean/.
364.summary: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from three-dimensional grand-canonical Newtonian gases throughout every regular kinetic interval with uniform Gaussian decay. Stable finite-range radial potentials may have attractive wells and a singular repulsive core; initial pair exclusion and spatially summable Gaussian density and gradient bounds are assumed. A companion gives finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations, centered at the exact microscopic expectation and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

papers.title: The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals
Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan

365.explainer: Calderon's problem asks whether voltage-to-current measurements at the boundary of a body determine the conductivity inside (the math of electrical impedance tomography). For smooth isotropic conductivities in 3D this was solved in 1987, but for anisotropic (metric) conductivities, for measurements on only part of the boundary, and for rough conductivities the answers were open. The uniqueness papers recover the metric by matching harmonic coordinates and Green kernels outward from the measured patch and extending the isometry across hypersurfaces using an estimate on shrinking spheres; the nonuniqueness paper builds a nested fractal of scalar blocks so that every harmonic function has equal averages on cell surfaces, which lets one rescale the conductivity by rho^2 with rho=1+delta*w without changing any boundary response.
365.caveats: The family title (metric+connection) undersells it: the Sept-24 companion claims to resolve the smooth anisotropic Calderon problem (Lee-Uhlmann conjecture) in all n>=3, and with same-patch partial data, plus same-patch partial-data uniqueness for smooth scalar conductivities; each would be a landmark, and neither is formalized.
365.lean: partial formalization — only the L^infinity nonuniqueness paper is formalized: Conductivity.lean, OAI.ScalarConductivity.main_nonuniqueness (two measurable conductivities on B(0,3), c<=gamma<=C a.e., equal 1 near boundary, differing on positive measure, same weak DN operator on H^1/H^1_0.
365.summary: Zero-frequency measurements on any nonempty open boundary patch determine a smooth metric and smooth unitary connection on a trivial Hermitian rank-two bundle over a compact connected manifold of dimension at least three, up to diffeomorphism and gauge fixed on that patch. Inputs and observations use the same patch. In contrast, distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a three-dimensional ball can have identical full-boundary data.

papers.title: Determination of a metric and a unitary connection from one boundary patch
Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch
Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions

366.explainer: Mumford–Shah image segmentation picks a smooth approximation u plus an edge set K by trading off smoothness, edge length and fidelity; the 1989 conjecture says minimizing edge sets are tidy: smooth curves, loose ends and 120° Y-junctions. Decades of work reduced this to one scenario: a bounded island of edge floating in a whole-plane blow-up limit. The paper splits the gradient into a field carrying the jumps across that island and a harmonic part, shows the energy interaction is harmonic in the island's translation and hence constant by minimality, and concludes the field vanishes, so deleting the island saves length — a contradiction.
366.caveats: Priority: a human-posted (Astra-assisted) proof of the same interior conjecture (Deangelis, arXiv:2609.26732) predates this by two days, and the paper itself says Deangelis 'gives a proof of the global classification'; the OpenAI argument differs (scalar harmonic interaction from finite translations + value variations on a regular subarc vs. Deangelis's combined inner/outer second variations), so this is an independent second proof, not the first.
366.lean: partial formalization — not listed in lean/docs or ComparatorChallenges, but lean/OAI/Analysis/MumfordShah/ (24 files, ~8.2k lines, no sorry/axiom) proves the core compact-piece exclusion step (theorem compactPieceExclusion, CompactExclusion.lean:354) for zero-fidelity global absolute minimizers with linear energy…
366.summary: Resolves the interior regularity conjecture for reduced absolute planar Mumford–Shah minimizers with bounded fidelity data. Locally, the closed discontinuity set is a C^(1,α) arc, a regular crack tip, or three arcs meeting at 120^∘; only finitely many global connected components meet any compact interior region.

papers.title: Interior regularity of planar Mumford–Shah minimizers

367.explainer: In the one-phase Bernoulli free-boundary problem the boundary of the positive set is smooth except possibly at singular points, whose size is governed by the first dimension d* in which a non-flat minimizing cone exists. It was known that d* is 5, 6 or 7; the paper proves it is 7, mirroring how Simons' cone makes 8 critical for minimal surfaces. The proof follows Jerison–Savin's Hessian-based stability approach but pairs a scalar test built from the normalized Hessian with a vector field whose divergence dominates its energy, verified by exact tensor-inequality certificates.
367.caveats: The Lean certificate covers only the previously known half (De Silva–Jerison 2009), so the novel exclusion of cones in dimensions 5–6 rests on the paper alone; it uses a Simons-type stability argument with a hand-built test function and vector field verified by 'weighted sums of tensor squares and exact rational remainder bounds' (Appendix A) — computer-algebra-style certificates that need checking. Reduction to a smooth link uses a suspension trick for d=5 introducing two tip singularities handled by cutoffs.
367.lean: partial formalization — per lean/docs/367.md and ComparatorChallenges/BernoulliNonflatInSeven.lean, only the existence side is formalized (OAI.Bernoulli.nonflat_in_seven, OAI/Analysis/BernoulliCone/Main.lean:10; ~13.5k lines, no sorry/axiom, standard axioms only): a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer in R^7, i.e.
367.summary: Establishes seven as the first dimension admitting a nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy. Consequently, minimizing free boundaries are smooth through dimension six, and their singular sets have dimension at most n-7 in higher dimensions.

papers.title: The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers

368.explainer: In nonlinear elasticity a deformation is a Sobolev homeomorphism, and numerical and variational methods want to approximate it by smooth, injective maps without losing derivative accuracy; convolution destroys injectivity. In the plane this was settled around 2010–2018, while dimension four and up has counterexamples, leaving dimension three open. The papers build a locally bi-Lipschitz replacement whose energy is paid for by counting how often image curves and surfaces cross a target triangulation, rebuild the derivative on retained full-rank, rank-one and rank-two patches, and then smooth the piecewise-linear result.
368.caveats: Very long (62 + 130 pp) intricate geometric constructions (target triangulations, intersection 'budgets', rank-dependent local models, Moise/Bing PL topology) with no formal verification; this is exactly the kind of argument where gaps hide. The two papers are self-contained (p>2 paper includes the common smoothing in an appendix), which is good for checking. The full Ball–Evans programme (dimensions ≥4 for p≥⌊n/2⌋, approximation with inverse control or energy convergence) remains open; this is the n=3 case only.
368.lean: none — no lean/docs entry or comparator for 368; no matching Lean directory found.
368.summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem: every W^(1,p) homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in ℝ³, for 1 ≤ p < ∞, is a strong W^(1,p) limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.

papers.title: Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for 1≤p≤2
Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2

369.explainer: If you heat an insulated plate and wait, the hottest and coldest points should migrate to the edge; mathematically, the first non-constant Neumann eigenfunction should take its extremes on the boundary. This fails for domains with holes but was open for every convex or simply connected planar shape except triangles and symmetric cases. The proof conformally maps to the disk, uses Rohleder's principle that gradients of first eigenfunctions are exactly the minimizers of a div–curl energy for tangent fields, and builds boundary multipliers from a Nevanlinna–Pick-type Green-kernel theorem so that an interior critical point would force too many independent eigenfunction gradients.
369.caveats: Smooth boundary only: Lipschitz/convex domains with corners (e.g. polygons beyond triangles) are not covered, though an approximation argument might give the nonstrict version — not claimed. The Lean statement assumes the eigenfunction is C^∞ up to the boundary (true by elliptic regularity, but an input rather than proved). Short paper whose key analytic step is a new kernel theorem (conditional negative-definiteness of K(p,s)K(p,t)/N(s,t), via McCullough–Quiggin complete Nevanlinna–Pick theory and Schoenberg).
369.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/369.md; ComparatorChallenges/HotSpots.lean states OAI.StrictHotSpots.main_theorem (proved at OAI/Analysis/HotSpots/Main.lean:78; 31 files, ~29k lines, no sorry/axiom, only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice permitted): for bounded, open, simply connected Ω⊂R² with C^∞ boundary…
369.summary: Proves a strict form of Burdzy's simply connected hot spots conjecture. On every smooth bounded simply connected planar domain, each nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has no interior critical point, so all global extrema lie on the boundary. Eigenvalue multiplicity is allowed.

papers.title: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on smooth simply connected planar domains

370.explainer: The Lane–Emden system is the coupled version of the classical equation −Δu=u^p whose positive entire solutions exist exactly at or above the Sobolev critical exponent (Gidas–Spruck). The conjecture says the same threshold — a hyperbola in (p,q) — governs the system, and such Liouville theorems feed blow-up and a priori estimates across nonlinear PDE; it was proved only up to dimension four. The paper proves a virial identity localized with a compactly supported kernel, controls it by an elementary interval inequality along near-radial directions, gets a uniform energy bound from subcriticality, and contradicts it by dilating about the origin.
370.caveats: Remarkably short (20 pp) for a conjecture open in n≥5 for ~30 years; the method (localized potential-kernel virial identity + an 'interval-pair' pressure inequality giving a uniform localized energy bound, then dilation) is new and unconventional versus the Rellich–Pohozaev/doubling approach. The Lean formalization of the full nonexistence statement substantially raises credibility. The existence half of Phan's Conjecture C is imported from Bidaut-Véron–Giacomini. 'Positive' means strictly positive everywhere including the origin.
370.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/370.md; ComparatorChallenges/HenonEmden.lean, OAI.HenonLaneEmden.main_nonexistence (OAI/Analysis/HenonEmden/Main.lean:9; 96 files, ~12.7k lines, no sorry/axiom, standard axioms only): nonexistence for n≥2, p,q>0, real A,B in the strict subcritical range, positive solutions…
370.summary: Resolves the subcritical Lane–Emden conjecture and its weighted Hénon extension. For n ≥ 2, p,q > 0 and real A, B, the system -Δ u=|x|^A v^p, -Δ v=|x|^B u^q has no positive entire solution when (n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1) > n-2, with solutions continuous at the origin and classical elsewhere. No symmetry or growth assumption is needed. Known radial existence gives the exact existence criterion for n ≥ 3 and A,B > -2.

papers.title: The Subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden Conjecture

371.explainer: For the defocusing (repulsive) NLS, conserved energy stops controlling regularity in high dimension, and whether smooth data can blow up was open until 2019–2022 constructions, which only worked on a thin, non-generic set of data. This paper finds blow-up that survives every small high-regularity perturbation, so it shows up with positive probability for random data. It takes the large-power limit where the self-similar profile becomes a flat core plus free exterior solved by confluent hypergeometric functions, certifies the spectrum exactly, transfers decay from R^12 to large tori, and uses a degree argument to turn a stable manifold into an open set.
371.caveats: Summary says 'for a sufficiently large odd power'; the theorem and Lean only give existence of some (arbitrarily large) odd p — weaker than 'all large p'. Dimension fixed at 12 and p unspecified (large-power limit a→0); not cubic, not R^d, not physically canonical. Relies on exact rational certificates for confluent hypergeometric matching (Appendix A). Very large Lean development is a major credibility boost. Blowup is type I self-similar at Schrödinger scaling, unlike the hydrodynamic (T−t)^{1/r} profiles of MRRS.
371.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/371.md; ComparatorChallenges/DefocusingNLS.lean with theorems OAI.DefocusingNLS.stable_blowup, gaussian_blowup, gaussian_not_almost_sure_global (OAI/MathematicalPhysics/DefocusingNLS/MainTheorems.lean:20; ~2,578 files, ~191k lines, no sorry/axiom.
371.summary: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in Hᵏ(𝕋¹²), with k > 8, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.

papers.title: Stable self-similar blowup for a supercritical defocusing Schrödinger equation on the torus

372.explainer: Calderón's problem asks whether boundary measurements determine interior material parameters; for electrical conductivity Sylvester–Uhlmann settled it in 1987, but for isotropic elasticity (two coupled Lamé moduli, vector displacements) the 3D global case stayed open after a published proof was corrected. The paper glues exact physical solutions across the boundary, builds complex geometric optics solutions realizing full transport frames, and shows the comparison matrix between the two media varies holomorphically over the projective null conic, where vanishing of global holomorphic sections forces it to be the identity.
372.caveats: Only 24 pages for a problem whose earlier global proof (Nakamura–Uhlmann) had to be retracted to a small-gradient case; the paper explicitly diagnoses the Nakamura–Uhlmann and Eskin–Ralston gaps, which is a good sign, and the full Lean formalization (31k lines) of the global statement is strong evidence. Positivity hypotheses (μ>0, 3λ+2μ>0) are the standard strong-convexity ones; full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on all of ∂Ω is required.
372.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/372.md; ComparatorChallenges/ElasticityUniqueness.lean, OAI.Elasticity.global_uniqueness (OAI/MathematicalPhysics/Elasticity/Uniqueness.lean:94; 42 files, ~31.6k lines, no sorry/axiom). Uniqueness statement only; no reconstruction. Not run by me.
372.summary: Proves that full static boundary displacement-to-traction data determine both smooth real Lamé moduli on every bounded connected smooth domain in ℝ³, provided μ > 0 and 3λ+2μ > 0 on the closure. Neither analyticity, proximity to constant coefficients nor prior knowledge near the boundary is required.

papers.title: Global Uniqueness for the Smooth Isotropic Elasticity Inverse Problem

373.explainer: In the strong-interaction limit of density functional theory, electrons are assumed to sit at positions that are deterministic functions of one electron's position (the Monge or co-motion ansatz). The paper shows this can fail for three electrons even with a smooth density: the density is built so every optimal arrangement must split the central mass between two equally good families of triples, but each outer region holds only half the mass a deterministic choice would send there, so no map can be optimal, although maps can get arbitrarily close.
373.caveats: Counterexample, not a general theory: the density is engineered (five disjoint components, central mass ν/3, four outer components ν/6), not a physical ground-state density (paper says so). It adapts an existing mechanism (Gerolin–Kausamo–Rajala) to the Coulomb cost; the new work is a common supporting potential via local calculus. Short and formally verified, so high credibility.
373.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/373.md; ComparatorChallenges/CoulombCounterexample.lean, OAI.Problem356.coulomb_counterexample_and_equal_infima (OAI/Analysis/CoulombTransport/Conclusion.lean:7; ~10.7k lines, no sorry/axiom). Only the 3D Coulomb case; the d≥2 Riesz extensions are excluded. Not run by me.
373.summary: An optimal three-particle Coulomb configuration need not be a deterministic function of the first particle, even for smooth identical spatial densities. The Monge and Kantorovich infima agree, but the Monge infimum is not attained. The same phenomenon occurs for every inverse-power Riesz exponent in each dimension at least two, with a suitable density in each case.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Monge ansatz for the three-marginal Coulomb cost

374.explainer: Optimal transport maps are used in statistics and ML (e.g. estimating Monge maps from samples), so one wants to know how much the map moves when the target distribution moves. The paper shows the map moves at most like the cube root of the Wasserstein distance, uniformly over all targets, and that cube root is the truth: tilting the middle piece of a max of three affine functions keeps its mass but swaps a thin slab of source points between far-apart targets. The upper bound comes from a moment inequality for Laguerre cells plus convex-gradient interpolation.
374.caveats: Disproves a conjecture and settles the sharp exponent only within the uniform-convex-source class; W1 vs W2 distinction matters (a sharp W1^{1/4} estimate is consistent). Kind is both a disproof (of Letrouit's 1/2) and a sharp positive bound. Fully formalized, short — high credibility.
374.lean: main theorem formalized — lean/docs/374.md; ComparatorChallenges/Brenier.lean with OAI.Problem358.one_third_stability and one_third_exponent_is_sharp (OAI/Analysis/Brenier/Stability.lean:20,48; 89 files, ~33k lines, no sorry/axiom), both the upper bound and the three-atom sharpness. Not run by me.
374.summary: For uniform source measure ρ on a compact convex body with interior in dimension at least two, quadratic optimal transport maps satisfy ‖T_μ-T_ν‖_(L²(ρ)) ≤ C W₂(μ,ν)^(1/3) uniformly over targets in a fixed compact set. The exponent is sharp, even for three-atom targets, disproving Letrouit's conjectured square-root bound.

papers.title: Sharp One-Third Stability of Brenier Maps

375.explainer: De Giorgi conjectured in 1978 that a phase-transition profile that increases in one direction must be a flat wall in dimensions up to 8, the diffuse analogue of the Bernstein problem for minimal graphs; it was known only in dimensions 2–3 (4 as of Sept 2026), or in all dimensions up to 8 if one assumes the profile tends to ±1. The paper shows the limits in the monotone direction are stable solutions in one lower dimension, proves every stable solution in R⁷ is flat, and then runs a blow-down/minimal-cone argument. The heart is ruling out unbounded energy density for stable solutions in R⁷ via curvature-moment estimates on the zero set and a carefully built stability test.
375.caveats: Extraordinary jump: two days earlier the human frontier was stable rigidity in R³ (giving monotone n=4); this claims stable rigidity in R⁷ without energy growth — the sharp Allen–Cahn analogue of the stable Bernstein theorem in R⁷ (itself only just proved for minimal hypersurfaces in Sept 2026), and it also proves the finite-density case for n=5–7, previously open. Not formalized.
375.lean: none — no lean/docs entry or comparator for 375; no De Giorgi/Allen–Cahn rigidity development found under lean/OAI.
375.summary: Proves De Giorgi's conjecture at its sharp dimension-eight endpoint: every entire C² solution u:ℝ⁸ → (-1,1) of Δ u=u³-u that is strictly increasing in one direction depends on only one linear coordinate. A stronger theorem classifies all stable entire solutions v:ℝ⁷ → [-1,1] as constant wells or planar transitions, without an energy-growth assumption.

papers.title: A positive resolution of De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight

376.explainer: Tao proposed that a fluid able to run a computer might be programmed to blow up, which motivated showing fluids can simulate Turing machines. Here the fluid starts at rest on a 3-torus and an external force, compiled from the machine's instruction table, steers it so a tagged particle reaches a target region exactly when the machine halts. The trick is to encode the tape as real coordinates (Moore's generalized shifts), record each instruction's branch in a third coordinate so the area-preserving flow loses no information, and realize each step with smooth shear flows; the force is then read off from the chosen velocity.
376.caveats: The forcing makes the PDE side nearly trivial, as the papers admit: any smooth divergence-free velocity is an exact Navier–Stokes solution once f is defined as its material acceleration minus the viscous term (Lean doc: 'One velocity works for every viscosity ν>0, with zero pressure and force f0+νf1'). The content is a kinematic construction of incompressible flows simulating a machine with effective, decaying/periodic forces.
376.lean: partial formalization — lean/docs/376.md lists six comparator challenges (SolenoidalSheetPrograms, NavierStokesAlternating, NavierStokesVelocity, BalancedBoxRouting, BalancedThreeStack, ForcedNavierStokesComputation.
376.summary: Constructs viscous incompressible flows starting from rest on a fixed flat three-dimensional domain that perform universal computation under smooth external forcing. A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite program for the force, so a designated particle reaches a fixed region exactly when the machine halts. The viscosity is fixed, positive and computable.

A Fixed Particle Test for Computation in a Forced Viscous Flow
Universal Computation with Eventually Stationary Navier–Stokes Forcing
Geometric Programs for Solenoidal Forcing
Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows
Computation under Rapidly Vanishing Navier–Stokes Forcing
Velocity-Field Detection of Computation in Forced Navier–Stokes Flows
Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation
Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation

377.explainer: The infinity-Laplacian describes the 'best' Lipschitz extension of boundary data (used in image inpainting and tug-of-war games), and because the equation only sees second derivatives along the gradient, it was unknown for twenty years whether solutions in three or more dimensions have continuous gradients, though they were known to be differentiable at every point. The paper proves a uniform Hölder bound on the gradient: if no power-rate affine approximation held, a rescaling would produce a non-affine entire solution of a limiting equation with affine fits at every scale, and a new Liouville theorem shows no such solution exists.
377.caveats: Not formalized; dated 4 Oct 2026, the most recent in the chunk, so likely the least vetted. Proof is by contradiction/compactness with a new Liouville theorem for an anisotropic limiting equation (Evans–Savin's scaling), whose proof uses an extremal 'horizontal Jensen defect', variance-penalized envelopes and a stochastic-game-like 'fair choice' drift inequality — the delicate part that defeated the d≥3 extension of Evans–Savin. Exponent not explicit; optimal 1/3 not claimed.
377.lean: none — no lean/docs entry or comparator for 377; no infinity-Laplacian development found under lean/OAI.
377.summary: Proves uniform interior C^(1,α_d) regularity for bounded infinity-harmonic functions in every dimension d ≥ 3, for a positive exponent depending only on dimension. The gradient's supremum norm and Hölder seminorm on the half unit ball are bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times the oscillation on the unit ball. The exponent is not explicit.

papers.title: Uniform Interior C^(1,α) Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions

001.explainer: Hodge classes on an abelian variety are only known to be 'absolute Hodge', not algebraic. Milne asked whether, after reducing mod p, they still pair rationally with the new divisors that appear on the reduction; this is what is needed for a good theory of rational Tate classes and for Langlands-Rapoport style questions. The proof transports every specialized Hodge class to one pulled back from a CM abelian variety of balanced Weil type, where the pairing can be computed.
001.caveats: Theorem 1.1 itself is independent of other release results, but the headline 'represented by a single rational algebraic cycle' (Corollary 6.4) depends on the release's Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties manuscript (family 032), which the README says was produced outside the fixed procedure and which has no Lean proof. 36 pages; not refereed.
001.summary: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over ℚ̅ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory. Together with result 032, every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle simultaneously in all prime-to-p and crystalline realizations, for every residue characteristic p.

papers.title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties

002.explainer: BSD says the order of vanishing of an elliptic curve's L-function at s=1 equals its rank, and that the leading Taylor coefficient is an exact product of arithmetic invariants. Rank equality in analytic rank <= 1 has been known since the 1980s; the exact formula has resisted proof because each prime factor of the leading coefficient needs its own Iwasawa-theoretic argument with hypotheses. The claim removes all those hypotheses by integral determinant comparisons using Heegner points, theta series and CM-point interpolation, prime by prime.
002.caveats: Not formalized. Three manuscripts totalling ~340 pages. The exact-formula paper takes the rank/finiteness statement from the release's own Selmer-converse paper and the 2-part from the release's 2-primary paper, and the Selmer-converse paper in turn uses the release's Goldfeld/2-converse manuscript (family 006): a chain of unrefereed, unformalized results from the same model. 'Full BSD' is only the corank-<=1 case; nothing is claimed for rank >= 2. The 'density-one set of twists' corollary also depends on Smith's 2-Selmer distribution (arXiv 2022).
002.summary: Proves the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group. With result 006, this gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ.

papers.title: Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank
The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime
The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one

003.explainer: Primes are controlled by the zeros of zeta: a zero at real part sigma means prime counts can err by about x^sigma. Everyone expects sigma = 1/2 (RH), but no one could even rule out zeros creeping arbitrarily close to 1. The claim gets a fixed margin, 1/8, for zeta and every Dirichlet L-function at once, by embedding them in Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein integers and comparing two exact expansions (a cubic-theta reflection and a Poisson summation) of one character-weighted sum; a zero too far right would force 1/L to continue further left than the two expansions allow.
003.caveats: If correct this is among the largest results in analytic number theory in a century, so the bar is extraordinary. In its favour: the comparator target uses Mathlib's riemannZeta and DirichletCharacter.LFunction, so the formal statement cannot be a weakened reformulation; formalization.yaml still marks review: unchecked and I did not build the Lean. Not a proof of RH (1/2). The 7/8 boundary is not included. The 199-page main paper proves 11/12 in Part I and upgrades to 7/8 in Part II.
003.lean: main theorem formalized: zeta, all Dirichlet L-functions and all finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(sqrt -3) zero-free for Re s > 7/8, plus the uniform Siegel-zero gap (Comparator: QuasiRiemannHypothesis, DirichletSevenEighths, HeckeSevenEighths, SiegelZeros); only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice permitted.
003.summary: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s), is zero-free in Re s > 7/8, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over ℚ(√(-3)). A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane Re s > 11/12.

papers.title: The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s > 7/8
The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (alternate 11/12 proof)
Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros

004.explainer: Hilbert asked for an algorithm to decide whether a polynomial equation has integer solutions; Matiyasevich showed none exists. Over the rationals the question was open because integers cannot (conjecturally) be carved out of Q with polynomial equations alone.
