The claimed route sidesteps that: multiples nP of a point on a rank-one elliptic curve stand in for the integer n, and a sequence of rational-solvability tests forces any 'integer' that passes them all to be a genuine integer via a height contradiction.
004.caveats: Not formalized. 62-page main paper explicitly cites three other release manuscripts as inputs: the pointwise 2-converse for curves with rational 2-torsion (Theorem 1.1, this family), Fontaine-Mazur modularity at 2 (family 010), and the Goldfeld/2-converse paper (family 006). So the result inherits every risk in those (~300 more pages of unrefereed arithmetic geometry). It proves undecidability without an existential definition or Diophantine model of Z, so it is consistent with Mazur's conjecture.
004.summary: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ negatively.

papers.title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over the rational numbers
A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion

005.explainer: Proving a number is irrational needs integer combinations a_N G - b_N that are nonzero yet tend to zero; for G every known approximation family had denominators growing too fast. The claim builds large determinants whose entries are rational combinations of 1, G and pi^2/6, arranges polynomial rows so the pi^2 part cancels, and then plays a lower bound from prime-by-prime denominator control against an upper bound from an integral formula.
005.caveats: Lean statement is the bare irrationality of the explicit series, so faithful. The proof is a 44-page determinant argument (size-48N mixed determinants whose entries are moments combining 1, G and zeta(2), with Taylor-contact rows cancelling zeta(2)), not an Apery-style recurrence. No irrationality measure is claimed.
005.lean: main theorem formalized (Comparator Catalan: catalan_irrational; standard axioms only).
005.summary: Proves that Catalan's constant G=∑_(j ≥ 0)(-1)^j/(2j+1)² is irrational.

papers.title: Catalan's constant is irrational

006.explainer: Goldfeld predicted that if you twist a fixed elliptic curve by all quadratic characters, half the twists have rank 0, half rank 1, and higher ranks are negligible. Smith proved the Selmer-group version; the new ingredient is a converse at p = 2 that turns small 2-Selmer groups into the matching analytic rank, unconditionally, via Heegner points, auxiliary twists and a cube transfer argument.
006.caveats: Counts signed squarefree d ordered by |d|, slightly different from Goldfeld's fundamental discriminants (the paper says so). The density statement relies on Smith's Selmer-distribution theorem (arXiv 2022). The mean-rank paper needs an additional tail bound proved separately. Not formalized; ~171 pages; feeds the BSD and H10 families, so an error here propagates.
006.summary: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ: analytic ranks zero and one each have density 1/2, and the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2. Both statements order signed squarefree twist parameters by absolute value.

papers.title: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves
The mean analytic rank of quadratic twists of elliptic curves

007.explainer: Chowla predicts the parity of the number of prime factors of n and n+h are uncorrelated. Tao proved it with logarithmic weights, which average over many scales; plain averages must work at the final scale, which is harder. The claim gets a log-power saving via a graph/trace method on prime 'supplies', counting closed walks and showing exceptional words have arithmetic savings.
007.caveats: Two-point only (k-point Chowla still open). Constants ineffective; no uniformity in the shifts. The 'uniformly nonpretentious' hypothesis lets t range up to N, the corrected form of Elliott. A reasoning-trace summary for this family is in the repo (reasoning_traces/ordinary-two-point-correlations.pdf).
007.lean: main theorem formalized (OrdinaryTwoPointCorrelations: liouville_log_saving, binary and affine corrected Elliott; OrdinaryElliott). Standard axioms only.
007.summary: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound O(X/(log X)^c) for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute. More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times nⁱᵗ for |t| ≤ X.

papers.title: Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions

008.explainer: The Grothendieck-Teichmuller Lie algebra encodes symmetries of braided associativity; it governs deformation quantization and motivic Galois actions on pi_1 of P^1 minus three points. Deligne-Drinfeld predicted it is as simple as possible: freely generated by one element in each odd weight. Brown showed those generators exist and are free; the claim supplies the missing dimension bound via a filtered degeneration of the pentagon equation and an injective leading projection.
008.caveats: 41 pages. The new content is an all-weight upper bound on dim W_n matching the free Lie algebra. Since Willwacher's theorem identifies grt_1 with H^0 of the graph complex, consequences for Kontsevich's graph complex follow, but the paper's graph-complex statements are outside the Lean scope.
008.lean: main theorem formalized (DeligneDrinfeld.main); regularized-transport proposition and graph-complex consequences not included.
008.summary: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.

papers.title: The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture

009.explainer: Anabelian geometry asks how much of a field is determined by its Galois group. Bogomolov conjectured that for function fields of dimension >= 2 over algebraically closed fields, a tiny two-step nilpotent quotient of the Galois group already determines the field. By Kummer theory this is equivalent to knowing K^x/l and the Milnor K_2 relations; the proof reads off valuations and rational subfields (lines in the projective-geometry sense) from which elements multiply to zero in K_2.
009.caveats: The Lean covers the easy direction (injectivity). The headline Milnor K reconstruction (existence/surjectivity) is not formalized. ~73 pages across three papers.
009.lean: partial formalization: only injectivity of the Bogomolov-Pop correspondence (uniqueness of the field isomorphism up to the stated ambiguities) is formalized; existence of a field isomorphism for every admissible Galois-data isomorphism, i.e. the reconstruction itself, is outside the Lean statement.
009.summary: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from K^M₁/ℓ, K^M₂/ℓ, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory
Reconstruction from Milnor K-theory modulo the characteristic
The Bogomolov-Pop reconstruction theorem

010.explainer: The Fontaine-Mazur conjecture says Galois representations that look geometric come from geometry; for odd 2-dimensional representations over Q that means from modular forms. At odd primes this is essentially known; p = 2 is the awkward prime where residual representations can be scalar and standard Taylor-Wiles patching breaks. The claim proves pro-modularity first (occurrence in completed cohomology) and then classicality, adapting Pan's method to the dyadic case.
010.caveats: Not formalized; 113 pages over three papers. The Fontaine-Mazur paper says it supplies the weight-two modularity input for the Hilbert-tenth-over-Q proof (family 004), so H10 inherits its risk.
010.summary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.

papers.title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level
Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2

011.explainer: How do the prime factors of p-1 look when p is prime? Heuristically like those of a random integer, which follow the Poisson-Dirichlet law. Proving it requires counting primes in progressions modulo products of large primes, far beyond the Bombieri-Vinogradov range. The papers use determinant estimates with 'marks' and signed memory to get the needed correlations.
011.caveats: Not formalized; ~187 pages over three papers. The 'x^{1-o(1)} smooth shifted primes for every delta' claim is a very strong statement; the totient-fibre conjecture follows from it via Erdos-Pomerance. Each is a known hard barrier (level of distribution beyond 1/2 in some form).
011.summary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of p-1, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law PD(1) as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and x → ∞. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers n have more than n^(1-ε) totient preimages, for every ε > 0.

papers.title: Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers
The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors
Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors

012.explainer: Smooth numbers (all prime factors small) have density given by Dickman's function. The question is whether smoothness of n says anything about n+1; independence is expected. Logarithmic averaging was known; the ordinary-density version needs to rule out conspiracies at individual scales, done here via an amplification and second-moment argument on 'large-prime labels'.
012.caveats: 84 pages. Statement in the Lean is natural density as in the paper.
012.lean: main theorem formalized (JointDickman: joint law and both ordering densities).
012.summary: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and n+1 are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying P⁺(n) < P⁺(n+1) have density 1/2.

papers.title: The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers

013.explainer: Could the primes, up to finitely many exceptions, be exactly the set of sums a+b from two sets? Sieve theory forces any such A and B to have about sqrt(x) elements up to x, which looked consistent; ruling it out needs an inverse theorem for sets that are small modulo every prime. The claim supplies one via quadratic-character structure.
013.caveats: 80 pages; reduces (via Laffer-Mann) to two infinite summands, then uses character sums with translating centres and a finite-field tree comparison. Lean statement is the full conjecture.
013.lean: main theorem formalized (OstmannComplete: inverseGoldbach and the two-infinite-summands case; OstmannPrimes).
013.summary: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as A+B with A,B ⊆ ℤ_(≥ 0) each containing at least two elements. This resolves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture on additive indecomposability.

papers.title: The additive indecomposability of the primes

014.explainer: Geometric Langlands relates sheaves on the moduli of G-bundles on a curve to local systems for the dual group. Over C it was recently proved; in characteristic p only a 'restricted' version (local systems with restricted variation) makes sense and it ties directly to automorphic forms over function fields through the trace of Frobenius. These papers claim that equivalence under mild conditions on p and deduce Ramanujan-type temperedness for generic cusp forms.
014.caveats: Not formalized; 348 pages over eight papers, the largest family in this group. One result (Arthur enhancements) is explicitly conditional on a decomposition statement. Characteristic hypotheses on p are essential and stated. Hard for anyone outside the geometric Langlands community to assess; no Lean.
014.summary: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over 𝔽̅_q under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses. Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 0, the same conclusion holds assuming additionally that p is very good for the group and p ∤ |W_G|. Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions, and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic…

papers.title: Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters
Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration
Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level
Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups
The Restricted Geometric Langlands Equivalence in Positive Characteristic
Constructible tame Hecke eigensheaves in positive characteristic
Tame Hecke Eigensheaves with Several Marked Points
Frobenius Structures on Tame Hecke Eigensheaves

015.explainer: Duke's theorem says special points coming from quadratic fields spread out evenly; the higher-degree analogue asks the same for orbits of the diagonal group attached to number fields of degree n. Measure rigidity for higher-rank diagonal actions reduces it to ruling out escape of mass and intermediate invariant measures, which is where prime degree and primitivity help.
015.caveats: Primitive (no intermediate field) restriction in degrees 4 and 6 matters: it excludes intermediate tori obstructing rigidity. Measure rigidity (Einsiedler-Katok-Lindenstrauss) is a black-box input.
015.lean: partial formalization: the prime-degree (>= 5) theorem is formalized (DukePrimeDegree, unconditional); quartic and sextic results are not.
015.summary: Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields. Here primitive means having no proper intermediate field; the relevant order or field discriminant tends to infinity.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Prime-Degree Torus Packets with Arbitrary Local Type
Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders
Equidistribution of Primitive Sextic Torus Packets

016.explainer: Zilber-Pink is the 'unlikely intersections' principle: a subvariety should meet special subvarieties of too-small codimension only in a controlled, finite way. It unifies Mordell-Lang, Manin-Mumford and Andre-Oort. In abelian varieties the hard part is a height bound for atypical points; the claim gets it through height scales, tangent positivity and bounded-degree descent.
016.caveats: Not formalized; ~170 pages over four papers. Over Q-bar only (not C). The abelian theorem is non-effective. Relies on the Barroero-Dill reduction (published).
016.summary: Proves the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over ℚ̅: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset. It also proves the full curve case in the Siegel threefold A₂ for Hodge-generic curves defined over ℚ̅, without boundary or reduction assumptions.

papers.title: The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture
The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A2
Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold
Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2

017.explainer: The irrationality exponent measures how well a number can be approximated by fractions: 2 is the minimum (every irrational allows |x - p/q| < 1/q^2 infinitely often), and almost every number has exactly 2. For pi, 70 years of work only pushed the bound from 42 to about 7.1. The claimed proof assumes pi has abnormally good approximations p_i/q_i, uses several of them as interpolation centres c_ji = 2 i j p_i/q_i near the periods 2*pi*i*j, constructs a nonzero determinant over Q(i) from a weighted multi-variable interpolation theorem, and shows it is simultaneously at least 1/denominator (arithmetic) and too small (analytic, a quadratic saving from repeated Taylor degrees), a contradiction.
017.caveats: The comparator statement is a faithful, elementary statement about Real.pi, which makes this one of the cleanest checks in the release, but review status is 'unchecked' and I did not build it. The 23-page proof is not a better Hata/Salikhov integral: it is a Roth-style interpolation-determinant argument on logarithmic curves (in the spirit of Laurent's interpolation determinants and Roth's many-variable lemma), applied to approximations of the periods 2*pi*i of the exponential. The argument uses the periods 2*pi*i*j of the exponential.
017.lean: main theorem formalized (PiExponent.main: the epsilon-form lower bound for all large q and the sSup characterization equal to 2, stated with Mathlib's Real.pi). The Flint-Hills corollary is not formalized. About 95,000 lines of Lean under OAI/NumberTheory/PiExponent.
017.summary: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational p/q satisfies |π-p/q| ≥ q^(-2-ε). This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series ∑_(n ≥ 1)1/(n³sin² n), with angles in radians.

papers.title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2

018.explainer: In an arithmetic group like SL_n over a number field, normal subgroups are expected to come only from congruence-type quotients at the finitely many places where the group is compact. This 'no surprise normal subgroups' statement feeds the congruence subgroup problem. Most cases were done; the claim finishes the exceptional and outer-unitary anisotropic types by showing their finite quotients cannot exist.
018.caveats: Not formalized; ~159 pages. The new content is the remaining anisotropic outer A_n, triality D4 and E6 cases; it uses the classification of finite simple groups in places (finite simple-group obstruction section).
018.summary: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over every global field, including function fields of characteristic two. For an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group G over k, every noncentral abstract normal subgroup of G(k) is the inverse image of an open normal subgroup in the finite product of its anisotropic nonarchimedean local groups.

papers.title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global function fields
The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields

019.explainer: Grothendieck conjectured that for hyperbolic curves over arithmetic fields, rational points are exactly the splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group. Over p-adic fields the expected obstruction is a section supported at a non-point valuation; Pop-Stix show every section is localized at some valuation, and the claim excludes the bad valuations by building a finite etale cover with a prescribed exterior sheet whose degree is divisible by p over each small disk, lifting the section to a birational one, where Koenigsmann's theorem applies.
019.caveats: Not formalized. Remarkably short for its scope: 24 pages plus a 7-page cover-construction companion. The global consequence is conditional on the finite-descent locus equalling X(Q), which is known by other work for X_0(N), X_1(N) (Mordell-Weil/finite descent results), so the global section conjecture in general is not claimed. Short length for a problem this famous is a reason for extra caution.
019.summary: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of ℚₚ correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic étale fundamental group. It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over ℚ for the modular curves X₀(N) and X₁(N) of genus at least two.

papers.title: Étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet
The p-adic section conjecture

020.explainer: Are values of n^4 + 2 squarefree a positive proportion of the time? The sieve handles small primes; the trouble is excluding p^2 | f(n) for p near n^2, where counting needs geometry of numbers. The claim uses adaptive auxiliary primes and bihomogeneous determinant cuts, with extra quartic geometry.
020.caveats: 55 pages including an exact parameter certificate (Appendix A). Lean statement covers all d >= 4, which means the Lean also covers (or re-proves) Browning's higher-degree range. Error term not uniform in f.
020.lean: main theorem formalized (PowerFreeValues: QuarticPowerFree.allDegrees, every d >= 4 with k = d - 2, no monicity or height restriction).
020.summary: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor: squarefree values on positive integers have the predicted positive Euler-product density. More generally, establishes the (d-2)-power-free density for irreducible integer polynomials of degrees four through eight under the necessary local condition; together with Browning's higher-degree theorem, this covers every d ≥ 4.

papers.title: Squarefree values of quartics and power-free values of polynomials

021.explainer: Jacobsthal's function asks how long a run of consecutive integers can all share a factor with a number built from k primes. Linear sieve theory stalls at the square root barrier, giving k^2 times log factors; the claim reaches the sieve's limiting parameter and controls the boundary term with an inverse estimate.
021.caveats: Optimal order still unknown (gap between ~k log k and k^2/(loglog k)^2). 83 pages.
021.lean: main theorem formalized (Jacobsthal: quadratic bound; JacobsthalImproved: the iterated-log saving).
021.summary: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of Ck² consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.

papers.title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function

022.explainer: Khintchine's theorem says when almost every number is psi-approximable, assuming psi decreases. Without monotonicity, overlaps between approximation intervals break it, and Duffin-Schaeffer's totient-weighted fix was proved by Koukoulopoulos-Maynard via a graph/compression argument. The claim does the shifted (inhomogeneous) case, where the GCD structure that powers the homogeneous proof is scrambled by the shift.
022.caveats: Not formalized; 87 pages. 'Weak' version (unrestricted numerators, totient-weighted divergence), not the coprime-numerator form.
022.summary: Proves that for every real shift γ and finite-valued ψ:ℕ → [0,∞), divergence of ∑_qϕ(q)ψ(q)/q implies ‖qx-γ‖ < ψ(q) for infinitely many q, for almost every x. Here ϕ is Euler's totient and the norm is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators are unrestricted; no monotonicity or Diophantine condition on γ is needed.

papers.title: The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture

023.explainer: Cubic Gauss sums at primes look random on the circle, but Patterson predicted a small bias of size X^{5/6} coming from the cubic theta function. Dunn and Radziwill proved it under GRH; removing GRH requires controlling sums over primes twisted by cubic characters, which the claim does with a zero-detector and large-sieve argument.
023.caveats: Uses the same cubic-theta machinery as the quasi-RH family (003); the QRH paper says it does not use this result. The primary-prime normalization vs rational-prime normalization is discussed in the paper.
023.lean: main theorem formalized (PattersonFirstMoment: first moment, angular comparison, angular cancellation).
023.summary: Proves unconditionally the all-primary-prime form of Patterson’s first-moment asymptotic: normalized cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes of norm at most X, including both conjugates, have an explicit positive main term of order X^(5/6)/log X. Every fixed nonzero prime-angle Fourier mode has smaller order.

papers.title: An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums

024.explainer: How many numbers up to x are values of Euler's phi function? Ford pinned down the order of growth (just under x/log x) up to a constant factor; the claim finds the exact asymptotic up to a computable oscillating factor, which settles whether V is regularly varying.
024.caveats: The 'asymptotic formula' has an oscillating (phase-dependent) bounded factor defined by a limit, not a closed-form constant. 39 pages, built on Ford's structure theory.
024.summary: Gives an asymptotic equivalent for the number V(x) of distinct totient values up to x, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor determined by convergent arithmetic approximations. In particular, V(cx)/V(x) → c for every fixed c > 0, answering Erdős and Hall’s scaling question.

papers.title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients

025.explainer: Every fraction a/b is a sum of distinct unit fractions; the question is how many you need in the worst case. Erdos showed you sometimes need log log b and conjectured that always suffices; Vose's sqrt(log b) stood since 1985. The claim gets log log b by a divisor-moment argument showing most denominators have many divisors with small residues.
025.caveats: 33 pages; denominators are unrestricted in size. Lean includes explicit constants like 257/log 2 and e^{e^{k/600}}.
025.lean: main theorem formalized (ShortEgyptianFractions; EgyptianFractions with explicit constants such as length (257/log 2 + eps) log log m for prescribed denominators).
025.summary: Every rational a/b with 1 ≤ a < b is a sum of O(loglog b) distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erdős’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions.

papers.title: Short Egyptian fractions

026.explainer: The average gap between primes near p is log p, and huge gaps exist, but is it true that for any C, a fixed positive fraction of gaps exceed C times the average? Under Hardy-Littlewood the gaps are exponentially distributed and the answer is yes. The claim proves it unconditionally by building sieve weights that make a prime at the start of an interval likely while making the next interval of length about C log X empty.
026.caveats: 19 pages, constants c(C) not explicit and certainly tiny for large C. Short for the claim; the method (a weighted second-moment construction putting a prime just before an empty interval) is Maynard-sieve flavoured.
026.lean: partial formalization: the Lean challenge PrimeGaps (Problem344.large_gaps_and_ratio_density) is described as the prime-ratio corollary associated with the gap theorem; the Lean doc presents it as a supplement rather than the full gap theorem.
026.summary: For every fixed C > 0, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed Clog pₙ, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes. The proportion may depend on C. Consequently, the indices where pₙ/n increases have positive lower density, answering Erdős and Prachar.

papers.title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps

027.explainer: Character varieties parametrize representations of a surface group into SL_r; their integral points correspond to representations with algebraic-integer traces, which relate to which local systems can be 'of geometric origin'. The claim shows these integral points are dense after one field extension, by a rank induction cutting surfaces into simpler pieces.
027.caveats: Not formalized; 27 pages. Integrality is measured in the ambient character variety while the boundary conditions are imposed on complex representations, as the abstract notes.
027.summary: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question. For every smooth connected complex algebraic curve and every rank, integral points become Zariski dense in every component of its SL_r character variety over the full ring of integers of one number field. Prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary conjugacy classes are allowed, including nonsemisimple classes.

papers.title: Integral points on character varieties of curves

028.explainer: Can you walk to infinity on Gaussian primes taking steps of bounded length? Primes thin out, but in the plane you can route around gaps, so large gaps alone do not answer it. The claim shows that just removing the multiples of finitely many Gaussian primes (depending on D) already traps every bounded-step walk in a bounded region, using an information-theoretic argument: a long self-avoiding walk would have to carry more and more entropy in its residues.
028.caveats: 29 pages; the proof is a finite periodic sieve obstruction proved with geometric sampling and entropy estimates, i.e. the statement really only uses that the Gaussian primes avoid certain residue classes modulo finitely many split primes. That makes it essentially a combinatorial statement about sieved lattice sets, which is why it is so short. Nonexplicit bound.
028.lean: main theorem formalized (GaussianMoat.fullMain: uniform component bound for every real D, axis primes and associates included).
028.summary: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have uniformly bounded steps. More strongly, for every distance bound D, the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most D has uniformly bounded finite component sizes, depending only on D, including primes on the coordinate axes.

papers.title: Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes

029.explainer: Artin conjectured that 2 (or any non-square other than -1) is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. Hooley proved it on GRH; unconditionally Heath-Brown showed all but at most two primes work, but could not say which. The claim proves it for every admissible base by combining a uniform zero-free region for Hecke L-functions (which controls primes splitting in the Kummer fields Q(mu_q, a^{1/q})) with a sieve that restricts the factorization of p-1.
029.caveats: Not formalized; ~113 pages. Proves infinitude with x/(log x)^2, not Artin's predicted density A(a) x/log x, so Artin's conjecture in its quantitative form remains open. The analytic input (Theorem 1.2) is itself an enormous claim: a uniform zero-free strip of width 10^{-6} for all Hecke L-functions over all cyclotomic fields containing mu_12, from the same cubic-theta machinery as the quasi-RH family; it is not formalized here. The companion is explicitly conditional.
029.summary: Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square. For each such base, at least cₐ x/(log x)² primes in every sufficiently large interval (x,2x) have primitive root a, with cₐ > 0.

papers.title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases

030.explainer: Wiles proved elliptic curves over Q come from modular forms; over imaginary quadratic fields the analogous automorphic objects live on hyperbolic 3-space and contribute torsion classes, so the method was only recently made to work, for many but not all curves. The claimed proof is a prime-switching argument like Wiles's 3-5 switch: build a family of curves (Jacobians of cyclic covers) whose cohomology links E by a chain of congruences mod p, mod 3, mod p to a curve known to be modular, choosing parameters so each step satisfies the lifting theorems' hypotheses.
030.caveats: Not formalized. Only 30 pages for a statement whose previous partial cases needed the ten-author potential automorphy machinery; it relies on those modularity lifting theorems (Calegari-Geraghty patching, ACC+ results, Caraiani-Newton) as black boxes and contributes an auxiliary-curve switching construction (cyclic covers with characters of orders 1, p, 3p, 3 linking E to a curve already known modular).
030.summary: Proves the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.

papers.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields

031.explainer: Neukirch and Uchida showed a number field is determined by its absolute (or maximal solvable) Galois group. Uchida asked the stronger question for homomorphisms with open image: do they always come from field embeddings? The claim proves the cyclotomic compatibility needed (Hoshi's criterion) from openness alone, using a transcendence-style statement that an l-adic character vanishing on infinitely many degree-one primes is zero.
031.caveats: Not formalized; 23 pages. Uses an l-adic Waldschmidt-Masser/interpolation-determinant input which the paper reproves.
031.summary: Proves Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields comes from a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction. No restriction on the kernel or separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption is needed.

papers.title: Open Homomorphisms of Global Solvably Closed Galois Groups

032.explainer: The Hodge conjecture says every rational cohomology class that 'looks algebraic' (type (p,p)) actually comes from subvarieties; abelian varieties with complex multiplication are the most symmetric test case, where Deligne knew the classes were 'absolutely Hodge' but nobody could build the cycles. The paper reduces every CM Hodge class to a single four-factor relation v1+v2 = v3+v4 among CM types (two-row 'switches' plus algebraic polarization contractions), and realizes each four-factor class by mapping one smooth projective surface to four CM abelian varieties: if the cup product of four pulled-back one-forms has a nonzero integral over the surface, the image of the surface is the needed cycle. The surface is a compact ball quotient, and the nonzero period comes from theta one-forms varied by weak approximation.
032.caveats: No Lean formalization (OpenAI and press coverage both say the Hodge result has no Lean proof). README: the CM Hodge result was an EXCEPTION to the standard 3-hour single-problem procedure (no details given). The overview's headline ('rational Hodge for CM abelian varieties and products of K3 surfaces') is a special case of the Hodge conjecture, not the Millennium problem; press reports already note this.
032.summary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic. Companion results prove rational Hodge for arbitrary products of projective complex K3 surfaces and algebraicity of the Kuga–Satake correspondence for every such surface.

papers.title: The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces
Algebraicity of Kuga–Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces
The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
Algebraic Kuga–Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus
Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers
Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers
Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds
A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences

033.explainer: Iitaka's conjecture says the 'amount of pluricanonical forms' (Kodaira dimension) is superadditive in a fibration: κ(X) ≥ κ(fibre) + κ(base). It is a backbone of the classification of varieties and an input to abundance. The projective proof isolates positivity of the top Hodge line of a variation of Hodge structure, fed through the canonical bundle formula; the orbifold version works on Fujiki-class-C manifolds via a relative Iitaka reduction plus general-type addition.
033.caveats: Lean (lean/docs/033.md): only the negative-fibre branch of the log additivity paper (if κ of the fibre is −∞ then total log Kodaira dimension is −∞) — a small piece; comparator LogKodairaFiberNegative.lean; the subadditivity theorems themselves are NOT formalized. Several distinct manuscripts each claim C_{n,m}; the projective one (033_3) uses a new 'entire highest Hodge line' positivity theorem.
033.summary: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-C manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries. For projective fibrations f:U → V of smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with connected fibers, general fiber F, and κ̅(V) ≥ 0, proves Popa's inequality κ̅(U) ≥ κ(F)+max{κ̅(V),Var (f)}, where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber.

papers.title: Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation
The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity
Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity
B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations

034.explainer: Abundance predicts that when the log canonical class of a pair is nef (non-negative on curves) it is actually semiample, i.e. it defines a morphism; it is the last big missing piece of the minimal model program in characteristic 0. The claimed proof is an induction on dimension proving at once that smooth varieties with pseudo-effective K have a pluricanonical section (nonvanishing) and that lc pairs have good minimal models; the new ingredient is a 'signed boundary' criterion (if L = K_X+D is nef, L|_D is semiample, and L is a signed combination of boundary components, then κ(L) = ν(L)), proved by deforming boundary fibres into the interior using filtered Hodge-module lifting.
034.caveats: Family title says 'under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity': the Kähler paper (034_0, Oct 4) states this as an explicit Assumption 1.1; the projective char-0 paper (034_3) instead imports it from the companion 033_0 ([54, Cor. 6.2]) and notes the specific zero-boundary case it needs also follows from Hacon–Popa–Schnell (external) — so the projective headline is unconditional modulo the release's own 033 and 036_2 (minimal models for glc pairs, used after abundance for finite generation).
034.summary: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample. It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting.

papers.title: Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs
Conditional good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds
Log abundance in characteristic zero
Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints
Fourfold nonvanishing by minimal metrics and moving jets
Lifting sections from the reduced support of an adjoint
Schnell fiber spaces and good canonical models
Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators
Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations
Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations
Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi–Yau pairs
Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations for fourfolds
Abundance after nonvanishing for compact Kähler fourfolds

035.explainer: Miyaoka's 1980s proof of the ν=1 case of threefold abundance over C used Hodge theory and covering tricks unavailable in characteristic p. The papers transplant a cycle/infinitesimal-neighbourhood argument to p > 3, settling one of the open numerical cases there.
035.caveats: Positive characteristic, dimension three, numerical dimension one only — a single case of abundance. Relies on the char-p threefold MMP, which is only fully established for p > 5 in the literature; how the paper handles p = 5 (MMP for 3-folds in char 5 by Hacon–Witaszek) should be checked. No Lean.
035.summary: Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 3 when the effective boundary is rational and the ℚ-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one. The adjoint is semiample, without requiring the original variety to be terminal or ℚ-factorial.

papers.title: Log abundance in numerical dimension one for threefolds in positive characteristic
Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic

036.explainer: In the minimal model program one wants every variety to be birational either to a 'minimal model' (canonical class nef) or to a Mori fibre space; existence was known for log general type (BCHM) but not in general. Generalised pairs add a nef 'moduli' term that appears in canonical bundle formulas, so the generalised versions are the ones induction actually needs.
036.caveats: 036_1 explicitly uses the release's own log abundance theorem (034_3) and termination results (056) as black boxes ('The proof uses the log-abundance theorem of [28, Theorem 1.1] and the terminating minimal-model programs of [29]'), so it stands or falls with those. The Kähler version proves only numerical semiampleness up to a flat change of line bundle, which the abstract states carefully. 036_2 is the existence form only ('makes no assertion that every arbitrary MMP terminates'). No Lean.
036.summary: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints K_X+B+M with K_X+B pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case. Separately, projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed.

papers.title: Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds
Numerical Semiampleness of Nef Adjoint Divisors
Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs
Minimal models in numerical dimension one

037.explainer: Normalized volume measures how 'big' a klt singularity is; smooth points are the biggest. The conjecture says there is a gap: the next possible value is exactly that of the ordinary double point x0²+…+xn²=0, which bounds the volume of singular K-semistable Fano varieties. The proof is an induction on dimension starting from a separately proved fourfold case.
037.caveats: The every-dimension paper uses the dimension-four companion as its sole companion input (base case of an induction); both are unrefereed. Boundary-zero only (pairs with boundary not covered). No Lean.
037.summary: Proves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture: every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension n ≥ 2, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most 2(n-1)ⁿ. Equality holds precisely for an analytic ordinary double point.

papers.title: The ordinary-double-point gap in every dimension
The normalized-volume gap in dimension four

038.explainer: Fujita predicted that adding n+1 copies of any ample line bundle to the canonical bundle always yields a base-point-free bundle. The standard method builds a singular divisor with an isolated log canonical center at the target point, but cutting down positive-dimensional centers loses positivity; the paper claims a uniform estimate on minimizing centers that avoids that loss, then lifts a section by Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing.
038.caveats: Only global generation (freeness), not Fujita's very-ampleness conjecture — the overview states this correctly. 25 pages for a problem that resisted Angehrn–Siu-style methods for 30 years; the key new step (controlling a minimizing log canonical center via growth of restriction images plus a tangential first variation, uniform over singular subvarieties of unbounded degree) is short and should get specialist scrutiny. Used as an input by the release's Kobayashi-conjecture paper (051). No Lean.
038.summary: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension: for a smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n and an ample line bundle L, the adjoint K_X+mL is globally generated for every integer m ≥ n+1.

papers.title: Fujita's freeness conjecture

039.explainer: Nagata's conjecture says a plane curve can't pass through r ≥ 10 'very general' points with high multiplicity unless its degree exceeds (sum of multiplicities)/√r — the naive parameter count is sharp. It is equivalent to a statement about the nef cone of the blow-up of P² at those points. The proof is an interpolation/lattice-point argument: specialize to a structured configuration and bound how many conditions a degree-d form can satisfy by counting integer rows under explicitly sheared polygons (Figure 1 of the paper), with a uniform size condition absorbing endpoint errors.
039.caveats: Lean: ComparatorChallenges/Nagata.lean states exactly the full conjecture (∀ count ≥ 10, ∃ countable family of proper Zariski-closed exceptional sets with a point avoiding all, and the strict inequality Σ m_i < d√count for every effective plane curve); proved as OAI.Nagata.nagata_conjecture at OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/PlaneCurves/Nagata.lean:148; Seshadri companion OAI.MaximalSeshadri.Geometry.maximalSeshadriConstants at OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/Seshadri/Main.lean:25. Comparator permits only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice.
039.summary: Proves Nagata's strict inequality ∑ᵢ mᵢ < d√r for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d through r ≥ 10 very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities mᵢ. It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants (Lⁿ/r)^(1/n) for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension n ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large r: at very general points over ℂ, and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: Nagata's conjecture for plane curves
Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces
Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions
Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic

040.explainer: Bloch predicted that if a surface has no holomorphic 2-forms, then all its points are rationally equivalent (zero-cycles carry no more information than degree and Albanese). It was known only for surfaces of small Kodaira dimension and scattered general-type examples. The paper claims a uniform diagonal (Bloch–Srinivas-type) decomposition from virtual counts on Quot schemes, showing the coefficient of the diagonal is strictly positive.
040.caveats: Route: a determinant-fixed Quot-scheme calculation with two marked surface factors produces a diagonal decomposition 0 = c[Δ] + Γ in CH²(X×X)_Q; c > 0 is proved by a lattice argument when K² ≤ 8 and by a comparison with Cartwright–Steger's surface when K² = 9 (fake projective planes are the K²=9 case) — that split is where a specialist would look first. Integral statement via Roitman's torsion theorem. 45 pp, no Lean.
040.summary: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for every smooth connected projective complex surface S with p_g(S)=0, the Albanese map CH₀(S)⁰ → Alb(S)(ℂ) on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism. This combines the new p_g=q=0 theorem with the classical theorem of Bloch, Kas, and Lieberman.

papers.title: Bloch’s conjecture for surfaces with p_g=0

041.explainer: On a hyperkähler manifold a nef line bundle of BBF-square zero 'should' come from a fibration by half-dimensional Lagrangian tori — the hyperkähler version of SYZ mirror symmetry. Known only for the four known deformation types; the paper claims it for all, plus that the base is always projective space.
041.caveats: 041_0 (98 pp) and 041_1 (32 pp) cite each other ([44], [36]); the finiteness corollary needs b2 ≥ 5 and the external EFGMS boundedness theorem. No Lean.
041.summary: Proves the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold is semiample. It also proves that every projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base has projective space as its base, in every dimension and deformation type.

papers.title: Projective-space bases of Lagrangian fibrations
The strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture

042.explainer: A complex manifold is Oka if maps from Stein spaces into it are as flexible as maps into C^n (holomorphic h-principle). K3 surfaces were the key test of whether 'special' manifolds are Oka. The proof builds Runge approximations by gluing compact pieces through necks (the paper's 'core–neck' construction).
042.caveats: The family title says 'Oka classification for minimal compact complex surfaces: Kodaira dimension zero and class VII', but the single paper's headline is K3; an aside mentions combining earlier results for class VII and Enriques — the title over-reaches the theorem statement I read. No Lean.
042.summary: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.

papers.title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka

043.explainer: Nonabelian Hodge theory identifies Higgs-bundle moduli with character varieties; P=W says the topology of the Hitchin fibration (perverse filtration) matches the mixed Hodge theory of the character variety (weights). For SL_n the endoscopic (variant) parts are the hard part when n is not prime.
043.caveats: Builds on the GL_n proofs; the new content is the composite-rank variant cohomology. 39 pp. No Lean.
043.summary: Proves Pₖ=W₂ₖ=W₂ₖ₊₁ on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two. This includes variant cohomology and, together with the known prime-rank theorems, establishes the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in every coprime rank.

papers.title: P=W in composite rank for fixed determinant

044.explainer: Hikita's conjecture is a symplectic-duality prediction: cohomology of one side (Higgs branch) equals functions on a fixed-point scheme of the dual (Coulomb branch). The paper compares the full topological torus fixed scheme with the stability-cocharacter fixed scheme.
044.caveats: Requires a regular stability character (free action on the stable locus); 41 pp, single paper. No Lean.
044.summary: Proves the equivariant cohomological Hikita correspondence for every finite quiver, including loops and multiple arrows, with arbitrary dimension and framing vectors and commuting flavor torus. When every semistable point is stable and the gauge action is free, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic cocharacter-fixed locus of its flavor-deformed Coulomb branch.

papers.title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for arbitrary quivers

046.explainer: Shafarevich conjectured that the universal cover of a projective variety is holomorphically convex (it maps properly onto a Stein space after contracting compact subvarieties), a far-reaching generalization of uniformization. The surface construction pinches paired punctures in a family of curves so that a rational fibre lifts to a non-compact union of spheres, with an infinite pro-2 image certifying the fibre is not contracted.
046.caveats: Surface counterexample uses weighted pro-2 groups and an infinite quotient compatible with a family (non-linear fundamental group — consistent with EKPR). The fourfold disproves the 'large fundamental group ⇒ Stein' form. 67 pp total; no Lean; used as input by 057 (abelianity). A disproof of a famous conjecture in 26 pages deserves careful checking of the infinitude argument (§5–6).
046.summary: Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex. A separate smooth projective complex surface already disproves unrestricted Shafarevich holomorphic convexity in dimension two.

papers.title: A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover
A surface counterexample to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity

047.explainer: Cancellation asks: if X × A¹ ≅ A^{n+1}, must X ≅ A^n? Over C it was open beyond surfaces for 50 years. The example is an explicit hypersurface in C^5 cut out by one polynomial; adjoining one variable makes it a polynomial ring, yet it is not one itself — and Lean has checked both halves.
047.caveats: Lean: ComparatorChallenges/ComplexCancellation.lean states FiniteType ∧ IsDomain ∧ ringKrullDim A = 4 ∧ Nonempty (A[X] ≃ₐ[C] C[x1..x5]) ∧ ¬Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[C] C[x1..x4]) for the explicit H — exactly the claim; proof OAI.ComplexCancellation.main at OAI/Algebra/AffineCancellation/Main.lean:32. Standard axioms only; review 'unchecked'; I did not run the checker. Dimension 3 over C remains open. The stable-coordinate consequence is not formalized (lean/docs/047.md).
047.summary: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold X≇𝔸⁴ with X×𝔸¹ ≅ 𝔸⁵, disproving affine-space cancellation over ℂ in dimension four. It also disproves the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture: smooth surjections X → 𝔸¹ and 𝔸⁵ → 𝔸² have every residue-field fiber isomorphic to affine three-space but are not Zariski-locally trivial.

papers.title: An explicit failure of complex affine-space cancellation

048.explainer: If the vector fields on a variety form a free module of the right rank, is the variety smooth? Lipman and Zariski conjectured yes in characteristic 0. The paper constructs an analytic isolated Gorenstein surface singularity with free tangent sheaf and algebraizes it.
048.caveats: Not log canonical (consistent with GKKP/Graf–Kovács). Built first analytically then algebraized via completed local ring; 37 pp; no Lean.
048.summary: Constructs a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf, disproving the characteristic-zero Lipman–Zariski conjecture.

papers.title: A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf

049.explainer: The conjecture says any embedding of affine (n−1)-space as a hypersurface in affine n-space is 'straight' after a polynomial change of coordinates (true for lines in the plane by Abhyankar–Moh–Suzuki). The counterexample's zero fibre is A³ but some other fibre (or a derivation-kernel invariant) shows the polynomial cannot be a coordinate; Lean checks both the isomorphism of the quotient with a polynomial ring and the non-existence of any automorphism.
049.caveats: Lean: ComparatorChallenges/AbhyankarSathaye.lean (21 lines) states ∀ n ≥ 4, ∃ F, C[x]/(F) ≃ₐ C^[n−1] ∧ ¬∃ automorphism e, index i with e(X i) = F — exactly the conjecture's negation; proved as OAI.AbhyankarSathaye.exists_noncoordinate_polynomial at OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/AbhyankarSathaye/Counterexample.lean:35; plus CommutingDerivations (n−1 commuting locally nilpotent derivations with kernel C[F]) at OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/CommutingDerivations/OrdinaryExtraMain.lean:25. Standard axioms only; review 'unchecked'; I did not run the checker.
049.summary: Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is affine three-space, yet none of its embeddings is rectifiable, also disproving the Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture even when all fibers are affine spaces.

papers.title: A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables
An explicit noncoordinate polynomial with affine three-space zero fibre

050.explainer: Griffiths asked whether algebraic positivity (ampleness) of a vector bundle is equivalent to curvature positivity of some Hermitian metric — true for line bundles and on curves. The counterexample pulls back one bundle by higher and higher power maps; ampleness persists, but a curvature obstruction concentrated at a point eventually prevents any Griffiths-positive metric.
050.caveats: Lean: ComparatorChallenges/QuadricBundles.lean; OAI.QuadricCounterexample.main_theorem at OAI/Geometry/QuadricBundles/Main.lean:10 (the very-ampleness certificate for even exponents is NOT included per lean/docs/050.md). Formalizing ampleness and nonexistence of Griffiths-positive metrics in Lean implies substantial custom definitions — the fidelity of those definitions to the standard notions should be audited (I did not read the 181-line challenge file in full). m0 is ineffective (compactness). 18 pp.
050.summary: Constructs ample rank-two bundles on ℙ¹×ℙ¹ with no smooth Hermitian metric of strictly Griffiths-positive curvature, disproving Griffiths' positivity conjecture already on the quadric surface.

papers.title: Ample rank-two bundles on the quadric surface without Griffiths-positive metrics

051.explainer: If a compact Kähler manifold admits no non-constant entire curves C → X, its canonical bundle should be ample — a bridge between complex hyperbolicity and algebraic positivity. The proof starts from the uniform derivative bounds that compact hyperbolicity gives (Brody) and feeds them into the MMP/abundance-style machinery available in the release.
051.caveats: Uses two other release results as inputs: Fujita freeness (038, Corollary 6.3) and the semialgebraic-universal-cover theorem (058), which itself uses the release's log abundance (034_3) and abelianity (057). So this is downstream of the least-checked parts of the release. 31 pp; no Lean.
051.summary: Every compact connected Kähler manifold of positive complex dimension with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle and is therefore projective. This proves Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in the smooth compact Kähler setting.

papers.title: Canonical ampleness of compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds

052.explainer: When a manifold's tangent bundle splits into two foliations, is it (up to covering) a product? Locally yes by Frobenius; the problem is continuing product charts globally. The paper builds 'boxes' of product charts and extends them by Hartogs-type arguments across a mixed boundary.
052.caveats: Beauville's full conjecture allows any number of summands and does not assume integrability; this is the two-summand, both-integrable case plus automatic integrability for RC. Lean: OAI.UniversalCoverSplitting.main at OAI/Geometry/KahlerSplitting/Main.lean:14 (KahlerSplitting challenge); SplitTangentIntegrability challenge covers (b). Formalizing compact Kähler manifolds/universal covers required custom foundations (ComplexManifold structure) — check definitional fidelity.
052.summary: A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact Kähler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture. On smooth rationally connected projective manifolds, both summands are automatically integrable, establishing Höring's conjecture and the corresponding product decomposition.

papers.title: Universal-cover splitting for compact Kähler manifolds
Integrability of split tangent bundles on rationally connected manifolds

053.explainer: Pixton wrote down a uniform family of relations among tautological classes on moduli of curves and conjectured they are all the relations. The counterexample is an alternating product of corrected small diagonals on powers of the universal curve that vanishes in Chow but provably lies outside Pixton's span.
053.caveats: Astronomically large example (genus 10^60) — cannot be checked by computer; correctness rests on the proof. Disproves completeness for Pixton's ORIGINAL system specifically; extended systems may survive. 61 pp; no Lean.
053.summary: Constructs a tautological relation on a moduli space of stable pointed curves that vanishes in rational Chow, hence in rational cohomology, but lies outside Pixton's original relation span. This disproves the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of his original completeness conjecture.

papers.title: A high-arity counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow

054.explainer: Are cubic fourfolds rational? Kuznetsov predicted: exactly when their 'K3 category' is the derived category of an actual K3 surface. The paper claims that on most Hassett divisors the K3 category is geometric yet the cubic is irrational, by counting how many K3-like divisors a birational map from P⁴ would have to create or destroy.
054.caveats: Threshold d0 ineffective; 'very general' in each divisor; the proof uses a new additive invariant of birational maps counting divisors whose MRC quotient is birational to a K3 in a fixed lattice class, evaluated via weak factorization and a uniform bound on surface contributions. Depends on the KKPY-era landscape where even irrationality of the very general cubic is brand new and unrefereed. 62 pp; no Lean.
054.summary: For every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general smooth complex cubic fourfold is irrational despite having both an untwisted geometric K3 category and an integral Hodge-theoretic K3 association. This disproves Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture and the sufficiency of the associated-K3 criterion for rationality; the discriminant threshold is ineffective.

papers.title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with geometric K3 categories

055.explainer: Physicists predict stability conditions (D-brane stability) on the derived category of a Calabi–Yau threefold, including a special 'Gepner point' symmetric under an autoequivalence of order 5 on the quintic. Constructing any Bridgeland stability condition on a general CY3 required a Bogomolov–Gieseker-type inequality for tilt-stable objects; the paper proves a corrected inequality and builds the conditions.
055.caveats: Large-volume only for general CY3 (not the whole stability manifold); the strong tilt inequality is a corrected form, not the original BMT conjecture. 71 pp total; no Lean.
055.summary: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift 2/5. Also constructs numerical Bridgeland stability conditions at every sufficiently large volume on all smooth projective complex threefolds with trivial canonical bundle, with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd central charges.

papers.title: A Gepner stability condition on every smooth quintic threefold
Prescribed large-volume charges on threefolds with trivial canonical bundle

056.explainer: The minimal model program performs flips; whether every sequence of flips stops is the termination problem, open beyond dimension 3 in the log canonical setting. The papers claim termination for fourfolds, including on non-projective Kähler fourfolds.
056.caveats: Kähler results are about EXISTING flip sequences ('does not assert the existence of all contractions or flips'). Two separate manuscripts share the title 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (Sept 24 and Oct 5) with different statements — a versioning oddity. 231 pp; no Lean.
056.summary: Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs. Also proves termination of arbitrary permitted minimal model programs for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary in characteristic zero.

papers.title: Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds
Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds
Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary
Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds
Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds

057.explainer: Special manifolds (Campana) are those with no fibration onto an orbifold of general type; they are conjectured to behave like abelian varieties, in particular their fundamental groups should be virtually abelian. Previous results handled linear quotients of π1; the paper claims the full group via L² Hodge theory on the universal cover.
057.caveats: 057_0 cites the release's Shafarevich counterexample paper (046) and the proof goes through L²/Dolbeault spectral analysis on coverings ('zero in the Dolbeault spectrum'); 057_2 is conditional-labelled ('A conditional abelianity theorem…') though its abstract says it uses the now-claimed abelianity theorem. Used by 058/051. No Lean.
057.summary: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact Kähler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups. Using this theorem, establishes the same conclusion for order-two root orbifolds of smooth projective complex fourfolds along one nonempty smooth connected divisor, when special in the stated differential-line sense. For smooth special complex quasi-projective varieties, proves that every finite-dimensional complex linear representation of the fundamental group has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two.

papers.title: The abelianity conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds
Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties
A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor

058.explainer: When can the universal cover of a projective variety be described by finitely many real polynomial inequalities? Kollár–Pardon conjectured only the obvious products of a bounded symmetric domain, affine space and a compact factor. The bounded-domain half (formalized) generalizes Frankel's theorem from convex to semialgebraic domains.
058.caveats: Lean (lean/docs/058.md): only the bounded-domain symmetry theorem (b) is formalized — OAI.Release061.main at OAI/Analysis/SymmetricDomains/Main.lean:55, with self-contained definitions of semialgebraic sets, holomorphic maps on subsets and bounded symmetric domains (custom foundations; worth auditing). The classification (a) uses the release's log abundance (034_3) and abelianity (057) as inputs and is not formalized.
058.summary: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products D×ℂᵐ× F, with D bounded symmetric and F simply connected, normal, and projective. A universal cover is quasi-projective exactly when the bounded symmetric factor is absent. In particular, a smooth projective variety covered by ℂⁿ has a finite étale cover by an abelian variety.

papers.title: Semialgebraic universal covers of normal projective varieties
Symmetry of semialgebraic bounded domains with compact quotient

059.explainer: Zariski asked whether the embedded topology of a hypersurface singularity determines its multiplicity (lowest degree of the equation). In high dimensions, an isolated singularity's embedded topology is classified by algebraic data of its Milnor fibre (the Seifert form); the paper builds two equations with different lowest degrees but congruent Seifert forms.
059.caveats: The multiplicity 2 vs 3 example lives in very high dimension (N divisible by 8); the C⁴ example is the low-dimensional one. Uses classification of high-dimensional simple fibred knots via Seifert forms (Levine/Durfee/Kato-type classification theorems), so the topology rests on surgery-theoretic classification in ambient S^7 and above. Zariski's question for hypersurfaces in C³ (surfaces) remains open. 63 pp; no Lean.
059.summary: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities. The examples include hypersurfaces in ℂ⁴ with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.

papers.title: Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three
Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five

060.explainer: Class VII surfaces are the only compact complex surfaces not yet classified; Kato showed that if such a surface contains a 'global spherical shell' (a holomorphic copy of a neighbourhood of S³) it is obtained from a Hopf surface by blow-ups and a twist. The paper claims every minimal class VII surface with b2 > 0 contains one.
060.caveats: If correct, completes the classification of minimal class VII surfaces with b2 > 0 (all are Kato surfaces). Teleman's gauge-theoretic program needed b2-specific arguments; a uniform 39-page proof should be checked carefully. No Lean.
060.summary: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with b₂ > 0 contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-b₂ Global Spherical Shell conjecture. Such a shell is a holomorphically embedded neighborhood of the standard three-sphere in ℂ²∖{0} whose complement is connected.

papers.title: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII

062.explainer: Positive quaternion-Kähler manifolds have twistor spaces that are contact Fano manifolds; LeBrun–Salamon conjectured both are always the homogeneous models (Wolf spaces, adjoint varieties). The paper proves the complex statement directly: every contact Fano manifold is an adjoint variety.
062.caveats: 40 pp single paper. No Lean. A long-standing conjecture with many partial results by dimension; a uniform proof is a strong claim.
062.summary: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space. It also proves contact-Fano homogeneity and classifies smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds of complex dimension at least three: those with b₂=1 are adjoint varieties with their canonical contact structures, while those with b₂ ≥ 2 have underlying manifold ℙ(T*Z) for a smooth projective variety Z.

papers.title: Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture

063.explainer: The conjecture bounds how many independent 'directions' (Picard number) a Fano manifold can have given that all its rational curves are anticanonically heavy (pseudoindex); products of projective spaces are extremal. The proof extracts ρ independent eigenvalues of quantum multiplication from lower bounds on point descendant invariants.
063.caveats: Short (19 pp) and via Gromov–Witten theory: quantum multiplication by divisors and point descendants, 'independent joint eigenvalue tuple'. A short GW-theoretic proof of a long-standing Fano-geometry conjecture is plausible-looking but unrefereed. No Lean.
063.summary: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex projective Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ and pseudoindex ι satisfies ρ(ι-1) ≤ n, with equality exactly for (ℙ^(ι-1))^ρ. Here the pseudoindex is the least anticanonical degree of a rational curve.

papers.title: The generalized Mukai conjecture

064.explainer: Lê and Ramanujam showed that if the Milnor number stays constant in a family, the singularity's topology does not change — except for surfaces in C³, where the h-cobordism theorem fails in the needed dimension (4-dimensional). The paper builds the trivializing homeomorphisms directly, removing an 'angular seam'.
064.caveats: Surface case only (the remaining case). 37 pp. No Lean.
064.summary: Proves topological right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in ℂ³ with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the μ-constant problem. After shrinking the parameter disk and representatives, ambient homeomorphisms vary jointly continuously, fix the origin section and preserve the defining functions.

papers.title: Topological triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities

065.explainer: The Virasoro constraints are infinitely many differential equations satisfied by the generating function of Gromov–Witten invariants (generalizing Witten–Kontsevich). Non-semisimple targets such as most complete intersections were out of reach of Givental–Teleman reconstruction; the paper uses degeneration/transport arguments instead.
065.caveats: Projectivization theorem (065_0) is conditional on the base satisfying the full constraints (by design). No Lean.
065.summary: Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomology insertions. The constraints also pass from any smooth projective complex base satisfying them to the projectivization of every algebraic vector bundle of rank at least two, and hence to projective-bundle towers.

papers.title: Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization
Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections

066.explainer: A complement makes a Fano-type fibration Calabi–Yau-like near a point; boundedness of the index of complements is a key finiteness tool behind the BAB theorem. The claim upgrades Birkar's lc complements to klt ones with bounded index.
066.caveats: Finite-rational-coefficient form; 199 pp in two papers. No Lean.
066.summary: Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for ϵ-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor. For ϵ-lc Fano contractions over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, it gives klt complements near every base point, with index bounded only by dimension and positive rational ϵ.

papers.title: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions

067.explainer: Campana and Peternell conjectured that Fano manifolds with nef tangent bundle are homogeneous, a characterization of flag varieties. Dimension-by-dimension proofs use minimal rational curves and Chern-class constraints; this extends the list to dimension six.
067.caveats: One dimension only; Appendix A is an 'exact arithmetic certificate' (computer-checkable numerics). 27 pp; no Lean.
067.summary: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

papers.title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six

068.explainer: If the anticanonical bundle carries a non-negatively curved metric (e.g. Ricci-semipositive Kähler metrics), must some power have a section? Structure theorems split the universal cover into flat, Ricci-flat and rationally connected parts; the remaining difficulty is torus actions on the RC factor, handled by invariant Euler characteristics and twisted differentials.
068.caveats: Seven manuscripts (270 pp) form one chain; several are explicitly reductions ('Assuming...') feeding the main paper. No Lean.
068.summary: If X is a smooth connected complex projective variety and -K_X admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then H⁰(X,-mK_X) ≠ 0 for some m > 0. Thus smooth semipositivity forces a nonzero section of a positive tensor power of the anticanonical bundle in every dimension.

papers.title: Anticanonical nonvanishing from smooth semipositivity
Invariant anticanonical indices and conversion of twisted differentials
Bounded anticanonical metrics on klt pairs and torus quotients
Cohomological transfer and equivariant anticanonical sections
Metric descent and rank-preserving contractions
Integrable metrics and effectivity with controlled boundary
Exact orders and invariant anticanonical linear systems

069.explainer: Quantum geometric Langlands deforms the geometric Langlands equivalence by a level c: twisted D-modules on Bun_G at level c match those on Bun_{G∨} at the dual level −1/(rc). At irrational level, Kac–Moody representation theory is semisimple-like, making a localization–Whittaker proof feasible.
069.caveats: Irrational levels only (rational/critical levels excluded); 119 pp single paper; uses one stated assumption-type convention (normalization). No Lean.
069.summary: Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group on every smooth projective connected complex curve, at every shifted level c ∈ ℂ∖ℚ. It identifies the full derived categories of twisted D-modules for the group and its Langlands dual, retaining all global forms and connected components.

papers.title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level

071.explainer: Every finitely connected plane region can be conformally straightened so its holes are perfect disks (Koebe); the 1908 question is whether this works for regions with infinitely many, even uncountably many, wild holes. The proof collapses each hole to a point, picks test functions with finite Dirichlet energy on the domain, carries them through finite circle-domain approximations, and uses small-energy 'barriers' to force unmarked holes to shrink to points and a period argument to stop marked holes from bulging beyond their limiting disk. Lean formalization of the full statement makes this one of the best-supported claims in the release.
071.caveats: Existence only: rigidity/uniqueness of the model for non-removable boundaries is not settled (and Rajala showed rigidity does not imply removability). Paper (1) uses a quantitative transfer/selection theorem from paper (2), so the two are coupled. Very long, novel machinery (transboundary-extremal-length style path laws, barrier fusion). Not independently reviewed; I did not run the comparator. If the Lean check passes it is the strongest evidence available for any family in this chunk.
071.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/KoebeCircleDomains.lean states both koebe_circle_domain (every open connected U in OnePoint ℂ is conformally equivalent to a circle domain) and removability_implies_rigidity, solution module OAI.Analysis.CircleDomains.Main (~2,600 Lean files, ~211k lines).
071.summary: Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points. It also proves that circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid, meaning every conformal equivalence to another circle domain is Möbius, establishing this direction of the He–Schramm conjecture.
