papers.title: Removable Boundaries and Rigidity of Circle Domains
Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture

072.explainer: Brennan's conjecture asks how badly a conformal map onto the disk can compress area near an arbitrary boundary; it is equivalent to the integral-means exponent B(-2)=1 and had been stuck near s≈3.42 for 25 years. The proof moves all maps to a compact normalized half-plane family, encodes boundary growth of 1/|F'| as the growth rate of one positive transfer operator sampling two affine subscales, builds a probability law on maps from a hypothetical too-fast rate, and derives a contradiction by pairing saddle points with maxima of a potential (a Morse/Hopf-index argument). A strict version of the same argument gives B_b(-1)<1/4, refuting Kraetzer's 1996 formula at one point.
072.caveats: The Kraetzer disproof is only at t=-1 and non-quantitative (ε not computed); it overturns a long-held, numerically supported belief, so it deserves particular scrutiny of the Lean definitions (limsup of log M / log(1/(1-r)) as EReal). The two papers share an affine-law/saddle-to-maximum method but the strict-bound paper states it does not use the Brennan endpoint as input. Summary's 'B_S(t)=|t|-1 for t≤-2' is in the paper (Section 7) but beyond the formalized statement. No public expert reaction found.
072.lean: main theorem formalized — Brennan.lean (OAI.Brennan.main_theorem: uniform M_{-2} bound with exponent -1-ε, spectrum(-2)=1, area integrability for 4/3<s<4 on every simply connected domain with nontrivial spherical boundary, and -2<t<2/3 for univalent disk maps), BrennanSharp.lean (Koebe map divergence at all four…
072.summary: Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection ϕ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, |ϕ'|^s is area-integrable for 4/3 < s < 4. The sharp universal integral-means identity is B_S(t)=|t|-1 for t ≤ −2. A strict bound B_b(-1) < 1/4 for bounded univalent functions disproves Kraetzer's prediction at that parameter.

papers.title: Brennan's conjecture and sharp inverse-square integral means
A strict inverse-first-power bound for univalent functions

073.explainer: Falconer's question: if a fractal set in R^d is more than half-dimensional, must its pairwise distances fill a set of positive length? The proof builds directional 'cap bounds' for pairs of points via auxiliary projections and a planar Furstenberg incidence estimate, then runs a multiscale recursion on mass profiles of the two Frostman measures, closed by a 'two-depth potential' that pays for each step; a final shell-summation lemma shows the limiting distance measure is absolutely continuous. A fully formalized Lean proof of the all-dimension statement accompanies it.
073.caveats: Only 64 pages for one of the central problems of geometric measure theory, and the paper explicitly avoids decoupling and prior distance theorems, which is surprising; the Lean formalization is what makes the claim credible. Strict threshold only; nothing at the endpoint; the pinned version at d/2 is not claimed. Odd dimensions need an extra thin-tube 'half-integer' upgrade. No public expert reaction found.
073.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/FalconerAllDimensions.lean states OAI.Falconer.falconer_distance_conjecture exactly (∀ d≥2, compact E ⊂ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), d/2 < dimH E → 0 < volume of the distance set); solution module Campaign123PlanarFurstenbergProof.lean.
073.summary: Resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension d ≥ 2: every compact set E ⊂ ℝᵈ with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2 determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions

074.explainer: The Kakeya problem asks whether a set containing a needle in every direction must be 'full-dimensional'; the maximal version quantifies how much δ-tubes in different directions can overlap and is what Fourier analysis actually uses. In 3D the paper sets up an extremal problem with a temporal-deficit profile, shows any counterexample produces a stationary 'equality configuration' of planes and plates, and kills it with entropy increments and planar projection estimates. In 4D it fits quadratic polynomials to tube families across scales (charts) and shows a Hausdorff-dimension deficit forces an impossible trade-off between chart thickness and length.
074.caveats: The 3D set conjecture is human work (Wang–Zahl 2025); the new 3D content is the maximal-function upgrade (uniform λ^3 density dependence), which imports the Guth–Wang–Zahl set estimate, Ren–Wang Furstenberg, and multilinear Kakeya. The 4D paper (175 pp) uses a 'weighted full-time plank bound' from the 3D OpenAI paper (its Lemma 2.15 = [24, Lemma 2.3]), so it depends on another unreviewed release result. 4D is the Hausdorff set conjecture only, not the 4D maximal conjecture.
074.lean: none — no lean/docs/074.md and no comparator statement; OAI/Analysis/Kakeya/FixedScale.lean (761 lines) only sets up tubes, the maximal operator and elementary fixed-scale/Hölder lemmas, not the theorem.
074.summary: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four. In three dimensions, the radius-δ tube maximal operator maps L³(ℝ³) to L³(S²) with norm O_ε(δ^(-ε)) for every ε > 0. In four dimensions, every set containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension four.

papers.title: The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions
Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension

075.explainer: Carleson's theorem says Fourier series of square-integrable functions converge almost everywhere; Kolmogorov showed this fails for merely integrable ones, and the 60-year question is how close to L^1 you can go, with L log L the conjectured boundary. The proof reduces to a dyadic-tree estimate for all integer modulations simultaneously, controlled by an information budget: noisy observations of where the input mass sits identify which frequencies share a phase, and entropy accounting bounds the total cost; averaging the dyadic kernels recovers the Hilbert transform and hence the ordinary partial sums.
075.caveats: Unformalized, single 76-page paper with an unusual information-theoretic method (entropy compression lemma, Griffiths–Ginibre correlation inequalities, 'thermal labels'), which is far from the Fefferman/Lacey–Thiele time-frequency tradition; correctness rests entirely on the manuscript. Calling it 'the classical L log L sufficiency conjecture' is fair (it is the natural conjecture recorded by Lie) though not a single named historical conjecture. No expert reaction found.
075.lean: none — no lean/docs/075.md, no comparator file, no matching Lean directory found.
075.summary: Proves that the ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums of every complex-valued function in Llog L(𝕋) converge almost everywhere along the full sequence. This resolves the classical sufficiency conjecture at the Llog L scale.

papers.title: Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L

076.explainer: A ±1 polynomial of length N has average size √N on the unit circle; the old question is whether its maximum can be pushed down to (1+o(1))√N, which most experts doubted (Erdős conjectured a fixed gap, and coding theorists conjectured bounded merit factor). The construction builds a smooth function of modulus ≈1 out of quadratic-phase 'waves' on short arcs, fed by a real trigonometric polynomial on a higher-dimensional torus, arranges its first N Fourier coefficients to be nearly ±1/√N in size, and rounds them to exact signs with discrepancy theory (Spencer, Lovett–Meka, Pippenger–Spencer). The upper-bound half is checked in Lean.
076.caveats: Headline 'ultraflat' (two-sided) result is the Oct 5 manuscript and is unformalized; it reuses two lemmas from the Oct 5 version-2 paper. The formalized upper bound plus finite-p flatness already contradicts el Abdalaoui's published-preprint claim, so one side is wrong; the Lean check favours OpenAI if it passes. Merit factor → ∞ follows from L^4 flatness, which is formalized only implicitly (finite-p statement covers p=4 in an L^p sense of | |P|/√N − 1 |; deriving the merit factor needs a short extra step).
076.lean: partial formalization — AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood.lean (OAI.AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood.main: ∀η>0 ∃N0 ∀N≥N0 a ±1 signing with max ≤ (1+η)√N; Lean OAI/Analysis/Littlewood/Main.lean:187) and LittlewoodFiniteFlatness.lean (one all-length signing family with ∫| |P_N|/√N − 1 |^p → 0 for every p>0).
076.summary: Constructs polynomials with N consecutive coefficients in {-1,1} whose modulus is (1+o(1))√N uniformly on the entire unit circle, for every sufficiently large integer length N. Thus real Littlewood polynomials are ultraflat, including at the real endpoints. Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.

papers.title: Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials
Nearly minimal maxima and positive minima of Littlewood polynomials
Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials

077.explainer: The restriction problem asks how large the Fourier transform of a measure on a curved surface can be at infinity, measured in L^p; in R^3 the conjecture is all p>3 and the best human bound was 22/7. The proof introduces an 'elliptic capacity' that tracks how wave-packet mass can concentrate when tested by ellipses biased toward eccentric shapes, proves this capacity propagates along lines (via Ren–Wang's Furstenberg theorem and entropy arguments), and combines it with decoupling; the general-surface theorem then plugs in the 3D Kakeya maximal estimate to sum the capacity factors.
077.caveats: Paper (2) uses two same-release inputs: the packet propagation theorem of paper (1) and the 3D Kakeya maximal theorem of family 074, so it inherits their (unverified) correctness. The sphere case also follows, per the Bochner–Riesz paper (078), from 3D Bochner–Riesz via Tao's implication — consistent but not independent verification. The restriction conjecture in its strongest L^q→L^p form for general positively curved surfaces is not stated beyond diagonal; for the sphere the factorization upgrade is sphere-specific.
077.lean: none — no lean/docs/077.md or comparator; OAI/Analysis/FourierExtension/* (14 files) contains only surface/chart scaffolding and an equivalence lemma (mainStatement_iff_low_exponent_memLp), not the estimate.
077.summary: Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions. For every compact smooth positively curved surface Σ ⊂ ℝ³, including surfaces with boundary, the extension operator is bounded from L^p(Σ) to L^p(ℝ³) for every p > 3.

papers.title: Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere
Diagonal Fourier extension for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions

078.explainer: Bochner–Riesz means ask how much you must smooth the edge of a frequency ball for the corresponding Fourier cutoff to be bounded on L^p; Fefferman showed a sharp edge always fails because of Kakeya-type tube arrangements. The paper first bounds how fast 'information' about positive masses moving along lines can grow across scales (an extremal argument ruling out isotropic and anisotropic extremizers using planar projections), then transfers this to oscillatory wave packets, with a separate argument at the uncertainty boundary where a packet's position cannot be pinned finely enough.
078.caveats: Unformalized 114-page argument via an information/entropy 'positive transport' scheme and finite packet repayment, with Ren–Wang Furstenberg as the geometric input. The same strict range is also claimed by the local smoothing paper (079) by an independent route, and restriction (077) is implied — mutually consistent claims in one release, none independently checked. Zipeng Wang's prior all-dimension claim exists but is not generally accepted as far as I could establish. Strict order only.
078.lean: none — no lean/docs/078.md, no comparator file.
078.summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict range: the Bochner–Riesz multipliers of order δ are bounded on L^p(ℝ³) for every 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ whenever δ > max{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0}.

papers.title: Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions

079.explainer: Local smoothing says that averaging a wave over a short time window recovers almost all the derivatives lost by a fixed-time L^p estimate; the critical exponent in 3 space dimensions is p=3, where the best human results still lost a fixed 1/12 derivative. The proof combines wave-packet decompositions, cone square-function/wave-envelope estimates from 2+1 dimensions, and geometric control of how packets concentrate across scales in the extra dimension; it then feeds the estimate through known Beltran–Hickman–Sogge reductions to get Bochner–Riesz and restriction consequences.
079.caveats: 165 pages, unformalized. Uses the Guth–Wang–Zhang wave-envelope estimate as a lower-dimensional input. Since local smoothing in 3+1 at p=3 implies 3D Bochner–Riesz, restriction and Kakeya maximal, this single paper would independently re-derive families 074(3D), 077(sphere) and 078 — a strong internal-consistency check if all are right, but also means one error pattern could recur. Not to be confused with the human 2+1 result (GWZ 2020).
079.lean: none — no lean/docs/079.md, no comparator file.
079.summary: Resolves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in three spatial dimensions. The estimate holds throughout the full strict range 2 < p < ∞, with Sobolev regularity above max{0,1-3/p}. In particular, the critical L³ estimate holds with every positive Sobolev loss.

papers.title: Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation

080.explainer: Carleson asked how much smoothness initial data needs so that the Schrödinger solution returns to the data pointwise as time goes to zero; after Bourgain's counterexample and the Du–Guth–Li–Zhang work, only the borderline exponent itself remained. Removing the last ε of regularity requires estimates with no logarithmic or power loss in the scale, which the papers obtain from a fixed power saving for transverse packet configurations (via fractal restriction and robust projection theorems), a sparse packet estimate and a lossless bilinear 'frame' estimate, summed over frequency with a carefully ordered limit.
080.caveats: This is only the equality case s = n/(2(n+1)); the sharp range up to the endpoint is human work (Du–Guth–Li 2017; Du–Zhang 2019). The higher-dimensional paper reuses lemmas and the time-tree mechanism of the planar paper (same release). The maximal estimate has L^1 output, weaker than the endpoint L^p maximal estimates one might expect. The paper flags and repairs a support-versus-counting mismatch in a published refined-decoupling packet lemma (citing Singh–Singh Parmar arXiv:2608.28711). 179 pages total, unformalized.
080.lean: none — no lean/docs/080.md, no comparator file.
080.summary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence e^(itΔ)f → f as t↓0 for every f ∈ H^(n/(2(n+1)))(ℝⁿ) and every dimension n ≥ 2. This attains the sharp Sobolev equality case of Carleson's Schrödinger convergence problem, including the planar endpoint H^(1/3).

papers.title: Endpoint convergence for the planar Schrodinger equation
Endpoint pointwise convergence for the Schrodinger equation in higher dimensions

081.explainer: The David–Semmes problem asks whether a single analytic fact — the Riesz transform, a vector-valued singular integral, is bounded on a set — forces the set to be quantitatively made of Lipschitz pieces. The proof propagates flatness down scales: it measures the excess (L^2 distance from a plane), rescales normal heights by the incoming excess, and passes to a limit where small Riesz pairings force the rescaled heights to satisfy an equation whose only solutions are affine; this improves flatness at every scale, and a packing argument plus the David–Semmes bilateral weak geometric lemma gives Lipschitz images.
081.caveats: Only 56 pages for a problem that resisted the NTV techniques; credibility rests on the Lean formalization. Uses the hard-truncation formulation of L^2 boundedness (standard). The paper replaces the codimension-one maximum principle with a normalized-height energy/affine rigidity argument for reflectionless limits. Does not cover n=d-1 or n=1 (already known). No expert reaction found.
081.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/RieszQuantitative.lean, OAI.RieszRectifiability.quantitative_higher_codimension_riesz_rectifiability (Uniformity/Rectifiability.lean:89): for d≥4, 2≤n, n+2≤d, fixed AD and Riesz constants give θ>0, M with M-Lipschitz ball images capturing θ r^n mass at every support…
081.summary: Resolves the remaining higher-codimension Riesz-transform rectifiability problem: for d ≥ 4 and 2 ≤ n ≤ d-2, an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on ℝᵈ is uniformly n-rectifiable whenever its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly L²-bounded over all positive hard truncations. The rectifiability bounds depend only on dimension, regularity and operator bounds.

papers.title: Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension

082.explainer: The triangular Hilbert transform is the simplest 'entangled' singular integral: three functions each depend on a different pair of three variables arranged in a cycle, which defeats standard time-frequency analysis; no L^p bound at all was known. The proof writes the form as a trace of products of operators, attaches a nonnegative matrix 'energy' to it, and shows the energy decreases under Gaussian heat flow at a rate that controls the form, using a dimension-free mixed trace inequality; output-dependent masks then upgrade this to the maximal and variational versions. The maximal estimate is checked in Lean.
082.caveats: Only the symmetric point; boundedness at other Hölder exponents (the general THT conjecture) is not claimed. The method — a matrix-trace energy with a dimension-free trace inequality and Gaussian heat-flow dissipation — is short (27 pp for the maximal bound) and quite unlike prior time-frequency attempts, which makes the Lean formalization important. The dyadic paper reuses the matrix inequality from the maximal paper. No expert reaction found.
082.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/TriangularHilbert.lean, OAI.TriangularHilbert.main_estimate (OAI/Analysis/TriangularHilbert/Main.lean:38): ∃C, for all complex F,G ∈ L^3(R^2), a.e.
082.summary: Proves maximal and annular r-variation bounds, for every r > 2, from complex L³(ℝ²)× L³(ℝ²) to L^(3/2)(ℝ²). The maximal estimate controls both hard truncation endpoints and gives almost-everywhere and norm convergence. Pairing with a third input settles the triangular Hilbert transform estimate at the symmetric L³× L³× L³ point.

papers.title: Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
An L³ bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form
The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point

083.explainer: Averaging a function along short line segments whose direction varies with the point is easy if the direction field is analytic and can fail for merely Hölder fields; Stein asked whether Lipschitz regularity suffices for the singular (Hilbert-transform) version, and this has been a central open problem in planar harmonic analysis for decades. The paper localizes to frequency bands, proves a logarithmically improved band estimate with time-frequency tile/tree technology plus a new 'phase gain' iteration, and reassembles bands via a Lipschitz commutator. If correct and with the Lean check, it settles Stein's conjecture in its standard short-scale form.
083.caveats: Scale restriction (outer length ~ 1/Lip) is intrinsic to Stein's conjecture as formulated, but readers should not read it as boundedness at all scales or as the Zygmund differentiation conjecture. The abstract says 'Stein's weak-(2,2) conjecture'; the strong L^2 bound is stronger. 87-page time-frequency argument (popular-forest tiles, analytic interpolation) uses Lacey-Li's Lipschitz Kakeya theorem as a black box. No public expert assessment located (release dated 2026-10-06). Lean comparator check is the strongest evidence; I did not run it.
083.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/LipschitzHilbert.lean states both `main` (exists a in (0,1/2), C>0 with uniform hard-truncation, principal-value, weak-(2,2) bounds and bounded L^2 extensions for all 1-Lipschitz unit fields) and `uniform_truncation` (R <= 1/(10^6 K)).
083.summary: Proves a uniform strong L² bound for the planar Hilbert transform along any Lipschitz unit vector field, at integration lengths bounded by an absolute multiple of its reciprocal Lipschitz constant. The estimate is uniform over inner truncations and yields an L²-bounded principal-value operator, establishing Stein's weak-type conjecture at this short scale.

papers.title: A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions

084.explainer: Erdős asked whether every infinite set A can be avoided by some set of positive measure, i.e. whether a big set E can avoid containing any scaled-and-shifted copy of A; even A = {1/2, 1/4, 1/8, ...} was open for 50 years because the points crowd together exponentially fast, defeating the standard random constructions. The proof builds the complement of E as a random periodic open set using a finite tree of 'routing' coin-flip tables on nested dyadic grids, with sequence indices assigned to tree edges so each test only needs a bounded number of grid scales; this makes a union bound over all scales affordable. Rescaling and a union over dilations then gives a set of measure close to 1 avoiding every copy.
084.caveats: Resolves only the geometric-progression case, not the conjecture for all infinite sets (the papers say so explicitly; the family title 'geometric case' is accurate). E depends on q. The general-q paper is dated Oct 5, 2026 (one day before release) and is unformalized; it adapts the dyadic construction by choosing grid resolutions ~ q^{-b}/(1-q). Short (13-16 pp) elementary probabilistic proof — plausible, and the dyadic case is Lean-checked. Earlier attempts (Solymosi, Tom) at random-cell dyadic constructions were incomplete.
084.lean: partial formalization — only the dyadic case: ComparatorChallenges/DyadicAvoidance.lean `dyadic_affine_avoidance` (compact E in [0,1], measure > 1-eta, every x, s != 0 misses some x + s 2^{-n}); solution OAI/MeasureTheory/DyadicAvoidance/Main.lean:103.
084.summary: For every fixed q ∈ (0,1), constructs compact subsets of [0,1] with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of {qⁿ:n ≥ 1}, with dilations of either sign. This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture for every ratio.

papers.title: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture

085.explainer: Maximal functions smooth nothing in L^1, so it is surprising that they might still not increase total variation of the gradient; this was known in 1D and for special inputs but open for the basic centered-ball operator in the plane. The key tool is a moment identity at an optimal radius (the radial derivative of the average vanishes) plus a 'tangent-disk sweep' that shows shell mass concentrates near one point except for an exceptional set of centers, giving a scale-uniform gradient bound for a signed finite band of radii, then a local Poincaré subtraction removes any singular part.
085.caveats: Only the planar centered-disk case of the Hajłasz-Onninen question; higher dimensions and the uncentered/other-shape cases are not claimed, and the summary says this correctly. Uses Lahti-Weigt-type ideas but proves the variation bound itself. No expert reaction found.
085.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/DiskMaximal.lean `main_endpoint` (EndpointStatement: a.e. finiteness, W^{1,1}_loc, integrable weak gradient G with ∫|G| <= C ∫|g|) and SignedFiniteBand.lean (signed finite-band estimate); solution OAI/Analysis/DiskMaximal/Main.lean:144.
085.summary: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Hajłasz–Onninen maximal-function regularity problem. For every real f ∈ W^(1,1)(ℝ²), the centered disk maximal function satisfies ‖∇ Mf‖₁ ≤ C‖∇ f‖₁ with an absolute constant. It belongs locally to W^(1,1) and has a globally integrable weak gradient.

papers.title: An Endpoint Gradient Bound for the Centered Disk Maximal Operator

086.explainer: The bilinear Hilbert transform (two functions, one 'linear phase' symmetry) was tamed by Lacey and Thiele's time-frequency analysis in the 1990s; adding a third function introduces quadratic-phase (degree-2 Gowers) structure that time-frequency methods cannot see, and no L^p bound at all was known. The paper combines a quantitative quadratic inverse theorem from additive combinatorics (Leng-Sah-Sawhney) with continuous 'quadratic charts', localization by quadratic curvature, and a scale-summation scheme that avoids losing a factor per scale. A correct proof would open the multilinear Hilbert transform hierarchy.
086.caveats: Single exponent point (3,3,3 -> 1) of the conjecture; the full conjectured range is not claimed. If correct this would still be a historic first boundedness result for the straight-line trilinear Hilbert transform — arguably more striking than the 'case' framing suggests — but it is a 93-page, unformalized, very technical argument dated Oct 5, 2026 (one day before release); highest-risk item in this chunk for undetected errors. Relies on the Leng-Sah-Sawhney inverse theorem (external, published input).
086.lean: none — no lean/docs/086.md, no comparator challenge, no formalization.yaml entry.
086.summary: Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts x-t, x-2t, x-3t is bounded from L³(ℝ)³ to L¹(ℝ). This resolves the L³ exponent case of the standard conjecture for slopes 1, 2, 3.

papers.title: An L³ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform

087.explainer: Mahler's conjecture (1939) says the 'volume product' of a convex body and its dual is smallest for the cube (symmetric case) or the simplex (general case); it was known only in dimensions <= 3 and in special classes. The striking symplectic route puts K in position space and its polar K° in momentum space and shows a round symplectic ball of capacity arbitrarily close to 4 fits inside K x K°; since symplectic maps preserve volume, |K||K°| >= vol(ball) = 4^n/n!. The balls are built from holomorphic functions f_j = g(<b_j, z>)^k vanishing to high order k (g the inverse of Gross's conformal lens map), whose order of vanishing buys a ball of capacity ~πk, while a uniform slice estimate keeps the momentum inside (πk/4)K°. The general case uses a completely different Gaussian-projection/entropy argument on the cone over K.
087.caveats: Two independent proofs of the symmetric inequality are given (a holomorphic-mass/feasible-simplex argument, 26 pp, and the symplectic-ball argument, 19 pp), both built on Gross's conformal 'uniform-distribution' lens map (arXiv:1905.00852). The symplectic paper explicitly makes no claim about equality cases; equality comes only from the 26-pp paper, whose final step rests on the Hansen-Lima classification of finite-dimensional spaces with the 3.2 intersection property (Acta Math 1981).
087.lean: main theorem formalized — four comparator challenges, all with only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice permitted and no sorry/axiom found by grep in the solution trees: MahlerConjecture.lean:15 `OAI.SymmetricMahler.symmetric_mahler` (solution OAI/Analysis/Mahler/MainTheorem.lean:12).
087.summary: Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension, with Hanner polytopes and simplices as the respective volume-product minimizers and all equality cases classified. The corresponding sharp functional Mahler inequalities also hold. For n ≥ 2, every symmetric polar product K× K^∘ in dimension 2n has Gromov width 4.

papers.title: The symmetric Mahler conjecture and its equality cases
The Mahler Conjecture for General Convex Bodies
Symplectic Balls in Symmetric Polar Products

088.explainer: The projection body of K records the areas of all its shadows; Petty conjectured that, at fixed volume, ellipsoids make the projection body as small as possible — an affine isoperimetric inequality stronger than the classical one. The proof turns K into a measure via the first variation of volume, bounds a bilinear |x·y| pairing using spherical-harmonic estimates (a strict norm inequality kills degree >= 4 harmonics) and a fixed-point choice of affine position that kills the degree-2 component; this works for n>=4. The counterexample half is an exact computation: projection-body volume is multiplicative over Cartesian products, and two 10-simplices beat one 20-simplex.
088.caveats: The paper proves only n>=4; the 'full' conjecture (n>=3) and the Lutwak-Petty/Holmes-Thompson corollaries for n=3 rely on the separate human result of Chen-Feng-Li-Xi-Xu. The Brannen counterexample is NOT a first disproof — Feng-Hu-Liu-Xu had counterexamples for all d>=9 — it is a simpler explicit product witness; the summary's 'in contrast' phrasing could be read as first disproof. Petty's conjecture is a well-known named open problem; only 30 pages, but Lean-checked. No expert reaction found.
088.lean: main theorem formalized — PettyProjectionVolume.lean `petty_projection_volume` (n>=4, inequality + ellipsoid iff; solution OAI/Geometry/ProjectionBodies/Main.lean:11); ProjectionCounterexample.lean `universal_simplex_upper_bound_false` (dimension 20.
088.summary: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n ≥ 4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume. Also establishes the full Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities. In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.

papers.title: Petty’s projection-volume conjecture in dimensions at least four
A product counterexample to the simplex maximum for projection-body volume

089.explainer: Embedding a graph's distances into L1 with bounded distortion is equivalent to the multicommodity max-flow/min-cut gap being bounded, so this decides how well sparsest-cut LP relaxations work on planar and bounded-treewidth networks — a 25-year-old TCS question. L1 metrics are exactly positive combinations of cuts, so the task is to build a random cut distribution that separates each pair proportionally to its distance while cutting each edge rarely; the planar proof evolves monotone cuts from coarse to fine scales with exactly-gluing local interpolation formulas (single-source distance functions) so losses do not accumulate across scales, and the treewidth proof builds consistent cut laws bag-by-bag along the tree decomposition and transports separation along it.
089.caveats: Resolves two cases of GNRS, not the full conjecture for all minor-closed families (general clique-sums / closure under 2-sums remain). The constants are non-explicit (treewidth paper: 'existence of C_k, without an explicit estimate'). The almost-embeddable corollary depends on both same-release papers plus Lee-Sidiropoulos. The planar paper is 45 pp; the Lean formalization of both main theorems is the strongest evidence. No expert reaction found yet.
089.lean: main theorem formalized — PlanarL1.lean `planar_graph_metrics_embed_L1` (topological planar drawing definition, symmetric positive lengths, L^1(μ) target; solution OAI/Combinatorics/PlanarL1/Embedding.lean:96) and BoundedTreewidthL1.lean `main_theorem` (bags <= k, finite-dim l1.
089.summary: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture. Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L₁ with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded.

papers.title: Planar Graph Metrics Embed into L1 with Constant Distortion
L1 Embeddings of Graphs of Bounded Treewidth

090.explainer: Why do so many 2D systems (vortices in superconductors, Coulomb gases, packed disks) settle into a hexagonal pattern? Cohn and Kumar conjectured the triangular lattice is 'universally optimal': it minimizes energy for every completely monotone interaction, which by Bernstein's theorem reduces to Gaussians. Following the Viazovska-style method that settled dimensions 8 and 24, the paper constructs, for each Gaussian, a sharp 'magic' auxiliary function below the Gaussian whose Fourier transform is nonnegative and which touches at lattice points (built from an atomic interpolation certificate), and then integrates over Gaussians; the same philosophy gives the sharp Cohn-Elkies packing certificate and, via a separate Voronoi-cell argument, the Abrikosov-lattice (Sandier-Serfaty) conjecture.
090.caveats: Three of four papers lean on rigorous interval arithmetic / finite certificates (20x20 interpolation blocks, sign checks); the universal-optimality and Cohn-Elkies statements are Lean-checked, which covers those computations, but the Sandier-Serfaty proof (Voronoi-cell comparison + interval arithmetic, 49 pp) and Riesz/log jellium extensions are not formalized. Universal optimality is proved for the minimum value only, not uniqueness of minimizers among all configurations. Cohn-Kumar's original conjecture concerned periodic competitors.
090.lean: partial formalization — formalized: TriangularEnergy.lean `universal_energy_minimum` (solution OAI/Analysis/Triangular/Energy/Universal.lean:9), AtomicGaussian.lean (`sharp_gaussian_minorants_atomic`, OAI/Analysis/Triangular/Main.lean:75), TriangularGaussian.lean (minorant construction), PlanarPacking.lean…
090.summary: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one. It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for 0 < s < 2 and Coulomb energy, resolving Sandier–Serfaty and the two-dimensional Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy.

papers.title: An atomic certificate for triangular-lattice universal optimality
Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
A sharp Fourier certificate for planar circle packing
Triangular minimality for planar Coulomb renormalized energy

091.explainer: Brunn-Minkowski says volume is concave under Minkowski averaging; the log version replaces arithmetic by geometric averaging of support functions, which is stronger and false without symmetry, and it is equivalent to uniqueness questions for the logarithmic Minkowski (cone-volume) problem. The proof reduces volume interpolation to a variance (spectral-gap-type) inequality for even test functions along a path of bodies and proves it via moment coordinates and a tensor estimate — essentially the Kolesnikov-Milman local spectral formulation made global. Consequences include the Gaussian-type (B)-conjecture for all even log-concave measures.
091.caveats: Remarkably short (20 pp) for a famous conjecture; the core is a variance inequality in 'moment coordinates' proved via density of even tests and a tensor estimate. The B-conjecture and log-concave-measure consequences are deductions from external theorems (Saroglou) and are not Lean-checked; the B-conjecture is claimed only for scalar dilations (its standard form) and even log-concave measures. Equality cases of log-BM are not claimed. Stancu's earlier announcement deserves mention in any write-up. No expert reaction found.
091.lean: main theorem formalized — LogBrunnMinkowski.lean `OAI.LogBrunnMinkowski.main` (volume K^(1-t) * volume L^t <= volume of Wulff log-combination, all n>=1; solution OAI/Geometry/LogVolume/BrunnMinkowski.lean:24481).
091.summary: Proves the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures. For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive Lₚ Brunn–Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout 0 < p < 1.

papers.title: The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture

092.explainer: How wastefully must copies of a convex body overlap to cover all of space? Rogers showed n log n always suffices; this family shows a single lattice already achieves n log n for every body, and that some symmetric bodies genuinely need about n log n even with arbitrary placements, pinning down the worst case. The lower bound uses a random symmetric body cut out by many random caps and a Poisson-witness argument showing every periodic covering pattern misses many targets.
092.caveats: Part (1) removes an iterated-log factor from Li-Liu's July 2026 result and builds directly on their horizontal-vertical/binary-correction framework, so the lattice half is an incremental (if sharp) improvement of very recent human work; Li-Liu already had the matching lattice lower bound. The genuinely new qualitative statement is the translative lower bound c n log n (no linear bound even allowing arbitrary center sets). Uses Eldan-Klartag Gaussian marginal theorem and Rogers-Schmidt mean-hole method as inputs. Constants not optimized.
092.lean: main theorem formalized — SingleLatticeCovering.lean `single_lattice_covering` (solution OAI/Geometry/LatticeCovering/Main.lean:25) and CoveringDensity.lean `CoveringOrder.optimal_order` (all four suprema Θ(n log n), translative via thetaT <= thetaL; solution OAI/Geometry/CoveringDensity/Main.lean:79).
092.summary: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as Θ(nlog n), for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings. Every convex body in ℝⁿ, n ≥ 2, admits a lattice covering of density at most Cnlog n; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least cnlog n even without the lattice restriction, for absolute c,C > 0.

papers.title: A single-lattice covering bound of order n log n
Translative covering densities of order n log n

093.explainer: For log-concave distributions (uniform measures on convex bodies, etc.), Gaussian tails of every linear projection are necessary for a dimension-free log-Sobolev inequality; Bizeul asked whether they are also sufficient. The paper says yes, so subgaussian log-concave measures enjoy Gaussian concentration for all Lipschitz functions with constants independent of dimension. The proof assumes a minimal counterexample sequence and derives contradictory descriptions of its fluctuations using heat-flow (Bakry-Émery) calculus, Gaussian channel identities (Guo-Shamai-Verdú) and tensorization tricks.
093.caveats: 65-page unformalized contradiction argument (normalized counterexample sequences, Gaussian-channel/I-MMSE identities, tensor near-equalities); requires a Lebesgue density (full-dimensional) and centering. Significance is within the log-concave/KLS ecosystem; it is a recently posed (2023) conjecture rather than a classical one. Post-2025 progress on KLS/thin-shell (Klartag's log bound; Klartag-Lehec slicing) may make some steps easier, but I found no prior human proof. No expert reaction found.
093.lean: none — no lean/docs/093.md and no comparator challenge found.
093.summary: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.

papers.title: A dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures

094.explainer: Johnson-Lindenstrauss lets you squash n points of Euclidean space into O(log n) dimensions with small distortion; for other L_p norms it was not even known whether you could beat dimension linear in n. This paper shows n^{o(1)} dimensions suffice for every 1<p<infinity at any fixed distortion D>1, while exact isometric embeddings need about n^2. The method builds one probability distribution of random 1-D projections (via convex duality / minimax over weightings of pairs, using an electrical-flow projection with O(log n) L_infinity norm), then samples coordinates independently (Maurey's empirical method).
094.caveats: Upper exponent gamma(p) and lower bound log n are not claimed optimal; the gap to Naor-Ren's p>2 lower bound remains. Key ingredient is the 2 log n electrical-flow localization bound of Gurel-Gurevich, Nachmias and Sachdeva (arXiv:2605.24130, May 2026), whose abstract says the initial proofs were generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; the paper re-proves it in Appendix A and the Lean development is self-contained. The summary's 'answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question' attribution is not spelled out in the paper beyond citing Naor's survey.
094.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/SubpolynomialLp.lean states the paper's Theorem 1.1 in full (both bounds for D>1, the D=1 quadratic bounds for n>=9, and the log d/log n limits) for p>1, p!=2.
094.summary: For every fixed 1 < p < ∞ and distortion D > 1, every n-point subset of real Lₚ embeds into ℓₚᵈ with distortion at most D and dimension d=n^(o(1)), answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2. In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension Θ(n²) when p ≠ 2.

papers.title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp

095.explainer: Hyperbolicity cones generalize the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and support interior-point optimization; the generalized Lax conjecture said every such cone is just a linear slice of a PSD cone (so hyperbolic programming would be no more general than semidefinite programming). The explicit counterexample feeds the Choi-Lam form, a nonnegative biquadratic form that dominates no nonzero bilinear square, into a determinant construction; any hypothetical PSD pencil, rescaled and pushed to rank-one limits, would produce such a dominated square. The companion paper builds a much larger cone with no semidefinite lift at all, so hyperbolic programming is strictly more expressive than SDP even with extra variables.
095.caveats: Directly contradicts Gonzalez Nevado's Jan 2026 preprint claiming GLC is true; paper 2 Appendix A gives a counterexample to that preprint's Theorem 52 step. The headline 'no SDP lift' claim (paper 1, 29 pp., existential, enormous dimension, uses a finite-field certificate in Appendix A and semialgebraic selection) is the unformalized one; the formalized result is the weaker (but still GLC-refuting) non-spectrahedrality. Abstract of paper 2 says 'degree 16' while its Theorem 1.1 and the Lean doc say degree 20.
095.lean: partial formalization — ComparatorChallenges/HyperbolicCones.lean formalizes paper 2's explicit 23-variable degree-20 polynomial: homogeneity, p(e)=1, hyperbolicity, and that the cone differs from {x : L x PSD} for every linear L into N x N symmetric matrices (i.e. the cone is not spectrahedral, disproving GLC).
095.summary: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows. The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Cones Without Semidefinite Lifts
A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone
An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone

096.explainer: Split Gaussian space into pieces and add up the squared lengths of each piece's (unnormalized) center of mass; the question is how large this can get. Khot and Naor conjectured the best is a 3-blade 'propeller' in a plane, even though more pieces are allowed, and this number fixes the optimal approximation ratio for kernel clustering. The proof reduces to finitely many Gaussian linear scores, uses HJN for up to four active cells, and rules out five or more by a deletion estimate (Ehrhard-Borell Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski concavity) plus a covariance-determinant competition bound.
096.caveats: The paper (on paper) uses the computer-assisted HJN R^3 theorem as a black box for <=4 active cells; the Lean development covers the whole statement. The hardness corollary in the summary depends on a separate same-release preprint titled 'The Unique Games Theorem' (claiming the Unique Games Conjecture), which is an extraordinary unreviewed claim; treat the complexity consequence as conditional. No public expert reaction found.
096.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/GaussianPropeller.lean states the bound 9/(8 pi) for all d,k>=1 and attainment for d>=2,k>=3; solution OAI/Probability/GaussianPropeller (47 files, ~11.6k lines, incl.
096.summary: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most 9/(8π). In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle 2π/3, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor (8π/9)(1-1/k) for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.

papers.title: The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension

097.explainer: If unit vectors sum to zero, can you order them so that the running sum never strays far? In Euclidean space the conjectured answer was about sqrt(d), matching a simplex lower bound, but the best general bounds had an extra dependence on the number of vectors. The proof works in coefficient space with a sequence of contractions, shows a filtered convex body has bounded Dirichlet energy via a stationary Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and Gaussian correlation, and then uses a symmetrization argument to pick signs step by step; Chobanyan's transference converts signs into an ordering.
097.caveats: The constant C is not explicit in the statement. Builds on very recent (Sept 2026) preprints: Guo-Fang-Lu (AI-agent-discovered), Akbas-Sra (arXiv:2609.27172) and Bandeira's 2026 note, which have had little time for review; the Lean proof is self-contained though. Not an efficient algorithm, unlike Dutta-Jha-Jiang. No public expert reaction found.
097.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/SteinitzBergstrom.lean states exists C with both the signed-prefix bound and the zero-sum ordering bound for all d,N>=1; solution OAI/Analysis/Steinitz (29 files, ~15.1k lines) has no sorry and only standard axioms. Existential only (no online algorithm), as the doc notes.
097.summary: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝᵈ admits signs keeping every partial sum within C√d, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order S₂(d)=Θ(√d).

papers.title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström theorem

098.explainer: Doubling sets look 'finite-dimensional' at every scale, so one might expect them to fit into some R^k with bounded distortion; this was known to fail inside L_p for p>2, but the Hilbert case was the famous open one. The construction stacks orthogonal displacements on a base plane, controlled by periodically coloured horizontal and vertical strips at sparse scales. Differentiating a hypothetical embedding on 'sheets' and using two nested extremal choices of derivative norms forces nearly constant offsets along crossing lines, which produces too many separated points in a bounded Euclidean ball.
098.caveats: Short (13 pp.) but fully Lean-checked, which makes it one of the more trustworthy items. Gives an infinite (compact) set; finite-set quantitative versions are not the point. The summary is accurate. No public expert reaction found.
098.lean: main theorem formalized — ComparatorChallenges/DoublingHilbert.lean (a subset of l_2 with doubling <= 76800 and no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any EuclideanSpace R (Fin k)) and CompactBanach.lean (universal Lambda.
098.summary: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling set that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space. The doubling constant is universal. This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

papers.title: A doubling Hilbert subset with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding

099.explainer: Edit distance is hard to compute and to index, so a low-distortion embedding into l_1 would enable fast nearest-neighbour search; Ostrovsky-Rabani showed distortion exp(O(sqrt(log d log log d))) is achievable, but the best impossibility was only about log d. This work shows the OR embedding is optimal up to the constant in the exponent. The lower bound builds hierarchical words from rows of tagged payloads and markers, with components cycling at different prime periods, and uses a Fourier-analytic inequality over cut metrics showing that l_1 cannot compress the distinguished shift as fast as edit distance does, compounding over levels.
099.caveats: Determines log of the distortion up to constants, not the distortion up to constants. The upper bound is essentially Ostrovsky-Rabani's (reproved uniformly and formalized). 099.summary: Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most d into real ℓ₁: it is exp (Θ(√(log d loglog d))). Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost. The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with d; binary words already force the lower bound.
